_about: Everything this build made up, one line each, PROPOSED to Griz's ear (spec §8). Nothing here is written back to the wiki. RULED 09-24 (Griz, playtest fold): the game shows no [GRIZ] stubs and does not defer key NPCs' words to him; the seat drafts them, they stand as approved, and the wiki is not edited to match gameplay. SUPERSEDED-BY (in part) THE TWO CANONS (RULED 09-26b) and THE FOLD (RULED 10-09, Griz: "1 go"): every entry carries a fold word -- place, person, creature, thing and lore are owed to the realm wiki as PROPOSED lines on their page; event to the game's own wiki (wiki/ in this folder -- the game is one branch of the realm, "as if the table is never played and this is the realm's 'if Ly left Silverton' timeline", Griz 10-09, and "edited to match is the wrong move"); both by the fold lane (..\handoff-2026-10-09-the-fold.md; python tools/fold.py owed); rule, look and game are never folded. A folded entry carries folded: date and page.

entries.what: Barley's threshing flail statted as 1d10 bludgeoning, two-handed (so Great Weapon Fighting applies).
entries.why: No stats anywhere in the register; the register calls it 'a two-handed farm tool'.

entries.what: Barley starts with the flail and no armor (AC 11).
entries.why: The register has him owning nothing on Day -15; the game starts him at fighter 2 with his method in hand.

entries.what: The Warrens' 'Crawler' is an original stat block (AC 12, HP 40, feelers +5 1d6+2 poison with the register's CON DC 13 paralysis, mandibles +4 2d4+2).
entries.why: The carrion crawler is not in SRD 5.1; the spec forbids non-SRD monsters by name. The CON 13 touch is the register's own.

entries.what: The Stair's Keeper is an original stat block (AC 13, HP 58, constrict + drag under, STR DC 13 grapple, invisible in its water until light shows it). 10-03: on the grid this block is deep16/data/foes.js keeperold, the ladder's (keeper-ladder, #the-keeper-ladder-old); the 8-bit's stair fights the new one (#the-keeper).
entries.why: The water weird is not in SRD 5.1. The register's DC 13 and 'cannot leave its water' are kept.

entries.what: A 'Glory-Seeker' gnoll leader (CR 1, HP 38, spear + bite).
entries.why: The gnoll pack lord is not SRD; the register's Snoot overlay has glory-seekers.

entries.what: Hire terms: Barley joins if you front his 5-silver stake at the Hex; Aurdin if you cover his debt (20 sp, creditor unnamed — held OPEN); Vivian after you buy one of her candles (1 sp) and ask; Lymen once the party has any renown. Spots: Barley at the Hex bar, Lymen at the Hex, Aurdin outside the mission chapel, Vivian on vice row.
entries.why: The register gives no joining price for any of them; spots follow where the register places each.

entries.what: Hires join at the higher of their sheet level and (the lead's level - 1).
entries.why: Spec §13.7 suggestion (join-level floor).

entries.what: Level-up picks: Barley Champion at 3, STR+2 at 4; Aurdin Evocation, learns Scorching Ray + Mage Armor (3), Web + Shatter (4), Fireball + Lightning Bolt (5), INT+1/CON+1 at 4; Lymen Oath of Devotion at 3 (+Divine Favor), Heroism at 4, Lesser Restoration + Aid at 5, STR+1/CHA+1 at 4; Vivian DEX+2 at 4.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 offers one subclass per class; the register leaves Barley's and Lymen's unruled. Spells chosen from the SRD list for usefulness in menu combat (Griz 09-23: the build picks casters' spells; no need to include every spell).

entries.what: At rogue 3 the player chooses Vivian's archetype: THIEF (SRD Fast Hands: ITEM is a bonus action) or CUTTHROAT (see #cutthroat).
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz): storywise it has a lean, but in this game it's the player's choice.

entries.what: CUTTHROAT, an archetype original to this game: Opening Cut, first round only, advantage against a foe that hasn't acted yet, and a hit on it is a critical. 2026-10-29: Opening Cut gave way to STAB DEBUT on Griz's word ("replace 'opening cut' with 'Stab Debut' where she gets a straight weapon damage attack (no bonuses) on targets that haven't first-turned"): with the Attack action at a foe that has not had its first turn, one more attack at it, the weapon's dice alone -- no ability modifier, no Sneak Attack, no rider; free, once a turn, the same foe while it stands (the seat's reading). No advantage, no critical.
entries.why: The canon lean is Assassin, which is not in SRD 5.1; this is the game's own path in that direction, named and built fresh. Opening Cut's trigger and both effects were the PHB Assassin's Assassinate (the leveling register, leveling-srd-by-class.md, read it CLOSE); his SD names ("our sufficiently distinct will be acronyms SD").

entries.what: Vivian's SKILL menu offers HIDE + ATTACK and ATTACK + HIDE (the bonus-action hide before or after her attack).
entries.why: Griz 09-24; SRD Cunning Action lets the bonus action fall anywhere in the turn.

entries.what: Winters' Errands: two courier runs in town. The estate papers (Androit seals, Casper Venn values, back to Winters: 12 sp and the shelves open) and Pryor's debt (Mical signs the crate off, Brennan is paid, back to Winters: 20 sp, a potion and the one renown for the pair; Griz 09-25: one renown for both errands, not one each). 'The Pryor estate' is invented.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz): easy 'help people in town' renown, courier missions between important NPCs, Winters starts. Gives a solo lead early renown (and Lymen's hire).

entries.what: Ambrose Winters' own voice and lines: 'Everything on these shelves outlived somebody. I price the somebody first.' He watches Vivian's hands. He holds the Ring of Binding for whoever can use it.
entries.why: Were reserved; RULED 09-24 the seat drafts key NPCs for this game. RE-TAGGED 10-09: drafted lines are the branch's (fold: game); the person stands on the realm wiki by their own line.

entries.what: Winters sells magic items after the first errand: healing potions (incl. a Superior Potion), an Elixir of Health, the Ring of Protection, +1 dagger/maul/staff, splint.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: he should sell magic items, acquisitions). Stock and gating are the game's. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: Mama's Pharmakaiea is a shop: Lucia sells simples, potions, antitoxin and kits, potions a little under the pawnbroker's price. Lucia's lines are drafted.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: make Mama's a shop).

entries.what: Hessle's drawer holds a stiff old purse of forty gold in thirty-year-old coin and an unsigned note: FOR WHOEVER COMES BACK UP. It pays 400 sp.
entries.why: The backer was held open; RULED 09-24 the seat drafts. The note keeps the backer unnamed. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: The ending: the Waterbys keep the inn; the lantern stays on its hook unlit; next morning Doran draws from the lake in front of everyone and drinks.
entries.why: Was held open ('do not ruin it'); RULED 09-24 the seat drafts. Written to not ruin it.

entries.what: Fronting Barley's five puts him straight onto the card: a solo bout vs a 'Card Bruiser' (Bandit scaled up, HP 22). Win: he hands your five back. Lose: the five is gone; he joins anyway.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: covering his silver should go straight to a fight scene).

entries.what: A shift at the cradle is a hold-and-release squeeze drawn at full resolution over the 8-bit screen (js/cradle.js): eight feelers hooked under the bar, the brightest gland the readiest; hold Z to work it and let go while the ring sits in the gold. Gold = a sealed thimble (1 sp; the inner third is a 'full' thimble, flavor only), short = a dry pull, long = spilt, and past the red or held to the top the feeler comes off the bar: CON 13 rolled on screen (the draught rolls twice and keeps the higher); a fail plays the paralysis and ends the shift. Six draws because the settle wears off: the ring's gold drifts more and the animal twitches from the fourth draw. Animal Handling or Nature (the better) widens the gold. Tuned 09-25 after Griz's hand (the late draws were too easy): from the fourth draw the gold narrows (to 0.7 by the sixth), the drift widens and quickens, and the twitches come oftener and jump further. Rebuilt 2026-09-25 on Griz's word ('make it FABLE-OUS... no 8-bit limitation'); the first version was a swinging-mark timing bar.
entries.why: Playtest 09-24 went looking for a milking minigame; Griz 09-25 asked for the cradle alone to break the 8-bit frame. The dose-rate, six draws, the settle, the choice of skill and CON 13 are the register's (WarrensModule/crawler-warrens-DM.md section 3).

entries.what: JOURNAL: pin one quest; a gold arrow marks the next person, door or place it needs (or the way there from another map). Each quest carries steps with a NEXT line.
entries.why: Griz 09-24: highlight a journal entry to make it active, with a marker over whoever you need next.

entries.what: Silverton has a north gate: a cut up through the mountain's skirt, onto the Doors road. The town icon lets you in by whichever gate you walked up to.
entries.why: Playtest 09-24: no way north of town, and the Doors road was unreachable.

entries.what: Cassia's inn: 8 sp alone, a flat 16 sp for a company.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz). RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: The first night the party stays at the Halfway Inn, Amara's wagon comes in (a cutscene). Whoever had second watch rolls Perception (DC 15 at the window); a success shows the children through the glamour, with no words. INVESTIGATE sends the watcher out, WAKE THE PARTY sends everyone, KEEP WATCH lets it happen. Outside: Perception DC 12 each; if still hidden, the inn lady's lie (the mine across the lake), Insight DC 13 on it, then Perception again at +5.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz's shape of the scene); the cast and the glamour are module-halfway-inn.md.

entries.what: Never seen through: the handover and the walk, with a goblin at the inn lady's side. Seen through with Lymen outside: his line, then the fight. Otherwise: 'Those are children', Amara offers 500 sp. Taken: the inn lady 'adopts' the child, the wagon leaves that night with Katarina, the child still goes to the lake, and Elsbeth never speaks to you again. Refused: the fight.
entries.why: RULED 09-24.

entries.what: Amara (AC 13, HP 38, two Eldritch Blast beams) and Willem Glass (AC 12, HP 30, Ray of Frost, Mirror Image) fight only to get away: each round one covers while the other runs for the horses (d20+DEX vs 10 + the party's best DEX, the party's own RUN rule). Amara's darkness goes up on her first run. RE-CUT 09-27 (Griz): the yard is fought in DEEP16 (deep16/data/fights.js wagonnight): the team stands hitched in front of the wagon; Willem spends each turn at the traces until a blow lands on him, then both run for the road ON FOOT (full stride, blasting), and either one reaching it is the chase (the horses are out of the escape; Darkness not yet read there). The two of them drove the wagon themselves; there are no hired drivers (cut 09-25 on Griz's word). The beats of the fight hold for Z. A lone watcher fights round one alone; the rest of the party arrives in round two.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz); stat blocks built from SRD 5.1 pieces for the module's warlock 5 and wizard 5. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: If they get away (on foot since 09-27: the lines say running feet and runners, not hoofbeats and riders): the party runs them down once on the road past the gulch (a second fight, the whole party). If they get away again, it's a chase on the world map at your own speed. The pair pulls up at the fork for about a second, and if Willem is alive he throws a false pair of riders down the west road. Catch them for a fight to the death, or they ride into the Tower, which then gives the expansion popup (its door still doesn't open). Changed 09-25 (Griz): the chase comes before the yard and the reward, the road is dark, doors and map edges are shut mid-chase, and when it ends (caught on the road, at the fork, or the Tower) the party is set back in the yard at night with a closing line, then the wagon, the strongbox, the children (+1 renown), Doran's night drive and the morning.
entries.why: RULED 09-24; the false riders are module-halfway-inn.md §4 (Willem's favorite trick).

entries.what: Stopping the wagon: +1 renown; the strongbox (600 sp and Amara's order, sealed with a dove and signed V, which Hessle pays true word for, unlisted). However the pair is stopped (the yard, the road or the Tower), the party ends back in the yard that night: Doran takes the wagon of children back to Newland, and the morning follows at once (09-25). Next visit: Doran gone, one girl kept back by the inn lady out back, and Elsbeth gives you the lake's thanks (+1 armor of the main's kind, or a Ring of Protection) and urges you to Winters. A later night with the ring on: the kept girl is the one who walks to the lake.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz); 'the lake gave it back' is module-halfway-inn.md §9 (bog-grave goods).

entries.what: If the wagon was stopped, Katarina runs inside when steel comes out and the day after gives the party her book, then walks south. If it went on (KEEP WATCH or the bribe) she goes in with the others and rides out with it at first light, since nobody can know what she saw through (Griz 09-25), and the book is in the drawer upstairs. READ shows the opening of Book One (serial-castegut installment 01, to 'Now the first thing.'). Given to Androit: +2 renown, not in the journal. The drawer is read by stepping onto the stair (fixed 09-25: the stairs tile is walkable, so a walk-into trigger never fired; the morning line now says the room stands open).
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz).

entries.what: After the credits, CONTINUE: morning at the lake. The inn lady sits inconsolable at the table; Doran thanks you, says he lost his way, and gives you free rooms for good; Elsbeth sells candles on vice row in Silverton.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz).

entries.what: The listed true word is the Snoot. Beating the Snoot's challenge on the road yields a Dominion wagoneer's anchor-pin taken at the moot; Hessle pays 500 sp for it.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (the listed true word is re: the Snoot; a drop the party takes to claim it). RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: Spell-component parts from monsters, if someone standing has the skill (no roll): bat fur and wings (Survival), gulch silk from spiders and the ettercap (Survival or Nature), darkmantle hide (Survival), crawler ichor (Arcana), glow glands from fire beetles, snake tongues (Survival or Nature), axe beak feathers and wolf fur (Survival). Only Percy buys them, at a fifth of the rendered price. Bat wings he won't take; Marta Venn cooks them into bat-wing pies (1 sp each, free with Vivian in the party): eaten in a fight, +2 CON and +5 HP until it ends.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: parts, a fifth of post-process pricing; wings to Viv's mom).

entries.what: Percy's Particulars has an interior: jars in ranks, Percy at the counter, Ned Halloway minding the shelves, the shelf card on the wall (flavor, nothing for sale).
entries.why: Griz 09-24; the shelf is shops-silverton.json pin 38.

entries.what: CUT 2026-09-25: Dancing Lights is out of Aurdin's list (older saves drop it on load). Light and a torch still reveal the Keeper. It had been castable in battle as dim light that revealed the unseen (09-24).
entries.why: Griz, playtest 09-25: one use doesn't warrant it; 'you were right the first time'.

entries.what: Find Familiar is cut from Aurdin's book. REINSTATED 09-29 (Griz: 'it'll be a pain, but familiars are pretty sweet - let's reinstate'); his lean: cast from the worldmap menu, the familiar picked by biome. A spec is owed: handoff-2026-09-29-the-druid-and-the-familiar.md. BUILT 09-29 in the 8-bit game (js/familiar.js: the ritual from the field menu, the shoulder in a fight); the grid's familiar follows (deep16/js/familiar.js).
entries.why: Griz 09-24: no reason it should be in the game. See #calling-herbs, #familiar-ground, #familiar-shoulder.

entries.what: Lymen's AC is computed as 19 (chain mail 16 + shield 2 + Defense 1).
entries.why: His sheet reads 18 with Defense 'included' — the arithmetic doesn't reach 18. Flagged for Griz.

entries.what: Currency is silver pieces; SRD gp prices x10. Register prices win where they exist.
entries.why: The town talks in silver; the Hex stake, the dose-rate and the lantern law are all in silver.

entries.what: Calla's 'simples' heal 1d4+2 in the game.
entries.why: The register prices theriac/purges/simples at ~2 sp but gives no effect.

entries.what: A healer's kit is sold per use (5 sp) and gets a KO'd hero up at 1 HP.
entries.why: SRD kit (10 uses for 5 gp) stabilizes; the spec wants KO'd heroes revived 'with an item'.

entries.what: The tent is a consumable short-rest item (half HP back; Second Wind, Action Surge, Channel Divinity recover).
entries.why: Spec §7: short rest = a TENT item.

entries.what: Warding chalk pushes the next random encounter back ~60 steps.
entries.why: The register sells warding chalk and threshold lines with 'no promises made'; the effect is the game's. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: Lisbet's charm is a ring-slot item with no effect.
entries.why: 'Charms (no promises made)' — taken at its word.

entries.what: Vilar's show-armorer sells the full SRD weapon and armor list (beyond the register's spear, mace, shield); Kessler's pawn stocks a few pledges (rapier, crossbow, studded, splint, potion, two +1 weapons).
entries.why: The register has no armorer; Lymen's chain mail came from the show-armorer, so the game treats Vilar's as the armor shop. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: A night at the Halfway Inn costs 5 sp a head.
entries.why: No price in the register for ordinary guests. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: Encounter weights, group sizes and step rates for every zone.
entries.why: The register's road d20 and regional d8s name the creatures; the numbers are the game's.

entries.what: The Hex ladder for a free fighter: a floor-bet brawl (Bandit stats, fists), a freeman challenge vs a stable fighter (Thug), the card vs a hired blade (Bandit Captain stats), Talmok (register block, pit fists), then a festival bout (Berserker). Bouts are solo; a loser is stitched up on the house at 1 HP. AMENDED 09-27: the hired blade cut to a merc between contracts (CR 1: AC 14, 40 HP, two attacks), because Griz found the card harder than the champion ('the guy before the champion is getting 3 attacks and is striking me as more difficult than the champion').
entries.why: The register has no ladder for free fighters; the rungs follow its stated rules.

entries.what: Under a roosted ceiling, fire and thunder spells are grayed out in MAGIC (marked ROOST). Casting Light, lighting a torch, or throwing an oil flask brings the roof down: the bats fill the screen and the run ends in a failure screen, NOT THIS KIND OF NAME. Every roost battle opens with a one-line reminder (no fire, no bright light).
entries.why: The register's one law (no fire, no noise; hooded lamps only). RULED 09-24 (Griz): a 'you wanted to make a name for yourself, but not this kind of name' failure; gray out the spells, keep Light or a torch as the trigger.

entries.what: Warrens flow: talk to Edric (or work a shift) to get in the book; talk to Skarn 'as a man' to open his gate; take the bucket to feed the otyugh or fight it; the mark wakes the keeper; rope the five out from the landing or wade in and fight. Killing 6+ crawlers makes the stock 'dead' and Dunmore's line holds the camp. 10-03: a hand on the mark now starts the Keeper's fight there, the party by the rune; WADE IN starts it on the ledge (#the-keeper-two-ways-in).
entries.why: Every step is the register's; the thresholds and the order are the game's.

entries.what: The rescue set-piece is fixed in G3's side gallery (four giant bats); pits in G3 drop to G4; bad air costs 1d4 on a failed CON 12.
entries.why: The register's set-piece is a d6 table fired once on the GM's word.

entries.what: Casting Light or using a torch in battle: the first time, the cloaker recoils and loses its next turn; after that its attacks are at disadvantage (shown as DAZZLED). It also reveals the Keeper.
entries.why: SRD Light Sensitivity; the register says light is the weapon. The lost turn is the game's (playtest: the light needed to visibly do something).

entries.what: The lake's offering plays the first night the party sleeps at the Halfway Inn holding the Ring of Binding; the chuul then waits at the point.
entries.why: Griz ruled what the cutscene shows (the inn lady and the kid go, only the inn lady comes back); when it plays is the game's.

entries.what: The Castegut road ends at a signpost (not this road, not this time); the east and west edges are the sea, the cliffs and the black mountains.
entries.why: Spec §5: east/west stoppages as appropriate. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: Ettercap fangs and the cloaker's tail are the proof tokens for Hessle's board.
entries.why: The register names the tail; the fangs are the game's. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: The lead starts in the Gate Plaza with 10 silver, 3 simples and 1 healer's kit.
entries.why: Barley's ten silver is canon; the rest is the game's.

entries.what: Each major quest (Pete's five, the rescue, the cloaker, the ettercap, Talmok, the Snoot) pays a magic weapon of the hero's own kind to the main and to one hired companion in the party: +1 for the first two, +2 after. Barley's is his threshing flail made +1/+2. 10-29: the first game's alone -- the second game pays no weapon in kind (RULED, Griz to the lanes desk: "those 'in kind' magic items were meant to be discontinued in game 2"; deep16/js/counter.js C.questWeapons, Hessle's majors on the grid since 10-22, taken out).
entries.why: Griz 09-23, mid-build: 'add magic weapons as reward for major quest - one for main and one for one hired'. The weapons are SRD Weapon +1/+2.

entries.what: Narration and UI lines marked 'invented: connective' in content/text.json and content/npcs.json.
entries.why: Glue between register facts.

entries.what: A Renown counter (+1 per resolved local job, +2 for the lake) and its titles; each point also gives 250 milestone XP to everyone standing.
entries.why: Spec §4: 'local hero' as the motive.

entries.what: All tile maps are simplified from corridor v3, city v6, environs v3 and the module sheets; building footprints, the Hex outline and the dungeon layouts are approximate.
entries.why: 8-bit tile scale.

entries.what: Heroes take the maximum of their hit die at every level (plus CON), and their level-2 starting HP is figured the same way: Barley 26, Aurdin 12, Vivian 18, Lymen 24. An older save's heroes are brought up on load.
entries.why: RULED 09-25 (Griz, playtest: 'always give characters max possible hp when they level, and recalculate their level two hp with that in mind').

entries.what: When the glamour breaks the whole yard ripples for about three seconds (a row-shear wave over the frame with a violet cast at its peak), and the goblins are children when it settles. Still no words.
entries.why: Playtest 09-25 (Griz: the switch was too quick; 'a more visual transition, takes longer, wavy').

entries.what: In the chase to the Tower the riders hold at the start until the player touches a key, or a second and a half, whichever comes first.
entries.why: Playtest 09-25 (Griz: 'they take off a little too quick').

entries.what: Winters' first errand pins itself in the JOURNAL and a line tells the player how the pin works (X, JOURNAL, the gold arrow, the NEXT line). Taking a job ends the conversation instead of returning to his menu.
entries.why: Playtest 09-25 (Griz: a use-your-journal tutorial after his lines; a job should work like LEAVE, not loop back to 'lifted pen').

entries.what: Elsbeth's gift, the morning after the wagon: she walks over from the kitchen to you before she speaks, then goes back to the tub.
entries.why: Playtest 09-25 (Griz: you wake beside the inn lady with Elsbeth across the room, so it read as the inn lady talking).

entries.what: Wizard's Robes (AC 11 + DEX, the 'robe' armor type only wizards wear; Mage Armor still works over them) and Robes +1. Aurdin starts in them, Vilar sells them, Winters' shelves hold the +1, and the lake's gift to an Aurdin lead is Robes +1. An older save's Aurdin gets them on load.
entries.why: Griz 09-25: 'wizard robes or something for Aurdin's armor slot'. Not SRD armor; the AC is padded's. RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).

entries.what: The party takes its long rest before the wagon rolls in (HP, slots, Lay on Hands), and again in the morning.
entries.why: Griz 09-25.

entries.what: Once Elsbeth has said 'go and see Winters', the lead tells Winters so at his counter; under level 4 he answers that he has been watching the challenges make you greater, but you are not yet ready. Explains his closing 'Not ready. Not yet.'
entries.why: Griz 09-25.

entries.what: Vera the secondhand dealer, in Silverton, says Androit the notary pays for a real book, written by one hand from first page to last: the pointer to Kat's book.
entries.why: Griz 09-25: seed one Silverton NPC to point at Androit buying books.

entries.what: Papa Urtusk walks out of his door to meet the party the first time they enter Silverton after the chuul; his lines (the scales lit, the stair drained, the one law, 'go and get them before the council picks one') and his look at Lymen are drafted.
entries.why: Griz 09-26 pour: Urtusk approaches the party, council is being called. The family is reserved; the no-stubs law (09-24) has the seat draft.

entries.what: The water stair drained by a siphon over three nights; the five's tokens on the bottom step if not yet recovered; the keeper a shivering puddle; the warranted door cut with a chisel.
entries.why: Spec §5.3 (game-only: the register's stair stays flooded at campaign start).

entries.what: The Burial laid out as seven Silversands families fanning down four tiers to the empty king's chamber. Families named for their patrons: Geirmund (wiped out; the crew's sack), Audun the door-warden (wiped out at the Third Lamp; the Door-Shield), Orri, Hallveig, Kolbein, Asmund (the heir's wedge; Asmund's Hammer +1), Brandr (Brann's). Niche names drawn from an Old Norse list; season-marks 1-33; lamp numbers for the highway's dead. Thora, Ari and Svala are the last of Geirmund's line.
entries.why: Spec §5.2 left the families to the seat; the burial law is Griz's (CANON 09-26).

entries.what: Hask (Bandit Captain with a pry-bar), the wheelwright (a Spy with a mallet, who bolts once Hask falls) and two crewmen (Thugs); the four options; Persuasion 13 (Vivian) and Intimidation 15 (the cut); 200 sp; the three-long-rest return.
entries.why: Spec §5.3 (names and numbers the spec's; the bolt rule its own).

entries.what: Skill checks as dialog options shown on screen: the skill and DC, whose hand (the party's best, or the one named), a d20 tumbling and landing, the total, SUCCESS / NOT ENOUGH.
entries.why: Spec §7 and §11 (checks on screen); the milking's CON roll is the precedent.

entries.what: Ingrith Scalebeam's arrival and every line of it (the ledger felt the seal go; her name and office; the trade; the highway as the argument; the offer; the warrant for Audun's shield; the iron across the cut door), her office lines, and the second-visit line.
entries.why: Spec §3 beat 3 and §4.4; her withheld and escort-less lines are the spec's own. RE-TAGGED 10-09: drafted lines are the branch's (fold: game); the person stands on the realm wiki by their own line.

entries.what: Every niche is a container: bodies and stone unless the family is wiped out. Taking without a warrant = blasphemy; Ketil stops the party at the vault door, confiscates, renown -1 per item; Ingrith takes it back too if she meets you carrying it. The sack goes back for dwarven favor +1.
entries.why: Spec §5.4.

entries.what: The Door-Shield: shield +2 (AC +4). On a miss against the wearer where the attacker rolled a natural 15+, a 3% chance: energy out from the shield and down onto the party, a silver sheen, 'The Door-Shield protects the party.', +3 AC to all until the wearer's next turn. Menu text is its name and the +2.
entries.why: Spec §8, the proc RULED 09-26 by Griz in his words; '+3' read as AC (his one word stands open).

entries.what: SOLSKAFT as built: the vault hall (two portcullises raised into the ore-chute), the tollhouse (the covered scales, the tariff board, Ingrith's ledger desk, the quartermaster), the falls-works (the stamp-mill wheel, the cistern, the bricked cut), the muster yard and cots, the Sunshaft (a light column with drifting motes; the race on the east wall), the clan hall, the shrine of the Triad, the kitchens, the lit and dark barracks; below, the works (sorting floor and smith, smelters and cupel-hearth, the assay house, the sealed mint, the empty treasury, the boarded trade hall, the highway's gate).
entries.why: Spec §4.3. Place-level: the Cowork seat folds it to the wiki (the two-canons law, 09-26).

entries.what: The garrison's drafted words: Pyro's four lines (his first is the Cowork seat's), Ketil Silversands (door), Ragna Copperbottom (water), Brann and Hedda (the escorts-to-be), the troopers, cook, drill-sergeant, the quartermaster's and the Copperbottom smith's shops (splint the one armor better than the surface sells).
entries.why: Spec §4.4-4.5; the no-stubs law.

entries.what: Vera: 'You went through the door. Everybody knows. Nobody says.' A Shaft Rows hand: 'Dwarves let you in. What's it like?' A townsman while the scales are lit. A rumor of the drained stair.
entries.why: Spec §4.5 (Vera's and the Shaft Rows lines are the spec's) and §11 (consequences as rumor).

entries.what: Two new songs: 'solskaft' (D dorian, a hammer somewhere below) and 'burial' (four slow bars).
entries.why: The build's own.

entries.what: Dark maps can keep lights: holes cut in the dark for kept flames, with a warm glow (the Burial's one lamp). The Sunshaft's beam is drawn over its floor.
entries.why: The build's own; the highway's between-lamp dark (spec §6.2) uses the same code.

entries.what: Heroism's temporary HP is shown: the cast line names the number, a cyan number at each turn's top-up, +N beside the name in the party panel, and 'heroism takes N' on a hit. The rule is unchanged (SRD: the caster's spellcasting modifier each turn).
entries.why: Griz 09-26: 'heroism says +4 temp each round and I'm not seeing that effect'.

entries.what: E is the talk-and-choose key (Z, Enter and Space still work); every hint says E.
entries.why: Griz 09-26: more used to E for interacting in WASD.

entries.what: Cap 9 once the chuul is dead (5 before). XP 14k/23k/34k/48k; proficiency +4 at 9; full and half caster slots to 9; skills grow with proficiency (twice where there's expertise) and now with the ability too; CON raised at level 8 counts back to level 1.
entries.why: Spec §9; the cap-at-5-until-the-lake is the build's reading of 'the chuul at 5 is the expansion's entry'.

entries.what: The build's picks, no selection screens: Barley 6 STR +2, 7 Remarkable Athlete (initiative), 8 CON +2, 9 Indomitable; Aurdin 6 Acid Splash + Potent Cantrip, 7 Ice Storm + Greater Invisibility, 8 INT +2 + Stoneskin, 9 Cone of Cold + Hold Monster; Vivian 6 Expertise (Stealth, Deception: Perception already had it), 7 Evasion, 8 DEX +2, 9 Supreme Sneak (hidden 3 rounds); Lymen 6 Aura of Protection, 7 Aura of Devotion (no charm exists in the game yet), 8 STR/CHA, 9 Revivify + Daylight. Ice Storm rolled as 2d8 bludgeoning + 4d6 cold on every foe.
entries.why: Spec §9 (SRD 5.1 features; RULED 09-23: the build picks).

entries.what: Guests: AI-run allies drawn behind the four with their own HP bars; they attack the nearest foe with what they carry, take no XP, sit out when KO'd until a long rest, and are saved with the game. Brann (battleaxe, splint, AC 17) and Hedda (warhammer, chain and shield, AC 18), fighter 5 with two attacks, HP 58, poison-resistant.
entries.why: Spec §6.2 (RULED 09-26: build the guest slots general, the escorts first; veteran numbers).

entries.what: Three road maps: dressed floor down the middle, raw cavern either side, seals set in the walls (whole/cut), open caverns off the road. Leg one: the cut seal and the goblins' camp, the truesilver seam, First Lamp (held; Ulf and troopers). Leg two: the great cavern with a causeway (the roper under a false stalactite) and a rim-path, the bulette's month-old breach, Second Lamp (dark; the roster slates; the pudding in the drainage cut). Leg three: the xorn in the wall, Third Lamp taken by the raid.

Game-original stat blocks from SRD 5.1 pieces, because the named monsters aren't in the SRD: Bugbear Chief, Hobgoblin Sergeant, Drow Blade-Captain, Drow Spell-Weaver. A bulette stands in for the umber hulk (not in the SRD). The xorn's resistance is read as all mundane blows. Gibbering reads as a WIS 10 stun; the roper's tendrils grab (DC 15) and do no harm themselves.
entries.why: Spec §6.3 names SRD creatures by leg; the SRD 5.1 lacks the umber hulk, goblin boss, hobgoblin captain, bugbear chief, drow elite warrior and drow mage.

entries.what: The day-clock (LAMP n · DAY n); the dark with the ledger-lamp's radius (84 against a torch's 56) and its seal-glow (white/red lights in the dark); a lamp reached ends the day (rest, milestone XP 4,000 / 7,000 / 10,000, THE SECOND DAY); held lamps as warp points from the tower and the gate ('you walk back up the lamps').
entries.why: Spec §6.2 and §11.

entries.what: Every line on the road is drafted: the muster (Hedda's orders, Brann's reason), the ledger-lamp's gift, Ulf at First Lamp, the escorts at Second Lamp, the set pieces, the raid (Brann: 'Our lamp.'; Hedda on the weaver), the relighting, the escorts staying ('our orders end at the lamp'), the captain's knife and Hedda's line, the smith and the Winnower.
entries.why: Spec §3-§8; the no-stubs law.

entries.what: The Winnower (Barley's threshing flail with a truesilver head, +2, knocks prone on a crit) from the smith with the lump from the First Lamp seal; the Greyseam knife (dagger +2, a sneak attack poisons, CON 13) off Third Lamp's captain. Both noSell.
entries.why: Spec §8 (the other two are the Door-Shield, M1, and the Sunshaft staff, M3).

entries.what: Engine: surprise rounds (either side), invisibility (both ways), Stoneskin, Revivify with a diamond (battle and field), a second damage type on a spell, several specials per monster, data-driven blast/curse/self specials, martial advantage and first-round damage, grab-only attacks, short names in the foe panel.
entries.why: The build's own, for the spec's creatures and features.

entries.what: CREEP UP FIRST at Third Lamp is a group Stealth check (DC 13) at the pace of the middle of the party; success gives the party the first round.
entries.why: Spec §7's checks-on-screen pattern; group check is 5E's.

entries.what: Deepholm's door as one screen: the made road, the three-tall door with light under it, Dagny's toll-grille, a live-coin tariff, a weigh-station, a bench. Dagny Scalebeam's three lines (the king's-coin line is the spec's) and her one ware, a diamond.
entries.why: Spec §6.4 (place-level: the Cowork seat folds it to the wiki).

entries.what: Torvald's scene as built: he heals when he leaves (not before the talk), so a failed lift costs the healing; the check menu shows what each check watches for; Persuasion ends the talk with the sentence; his fight: priest strengthened (AC 13, HP 40), Spirit Guardians as a WIS 13 3d8 radiant on everyone (recharge), Hold once, Sanctuary when bloodied read as invisibility; he yields at half HP (LET HIM GO / FINISH IT). The party never learns his name; he is 'the cleric'.
entries.why: Spec §7.1 (his words and the sentence are the spec's and Griz's).

entries.what: The sect's blades at the next rest of any kind after Torvald (tent, lamp, cot, inn): the watch chooser (passive Perception vs Stealth +9), surprise with Assassinate crits, the five answers, a lie either way when he never went up, a circle-back once; SRD Assassin numbers with the 4d6 sneak attack as once-a-turn extra damage while the other stands; loot: two Sect Blades (the poison spent), the ward-knots, 120 sp.
entries.why: Spec §7.2.

entries.what: Beat nine as built: Pyro's word after the road is held, Ingrith asks to be walked down and joins as a healing guest (three 2d8+3 heals a rest), the door opens the width of one dwarf for her; Dagny's line and the Sunshaft Staff; a 13,000 XP milestone; the expansion's credits with the receipt line and THE ROAD IS HELD; CONTINUE wakes the party in Solskaft. Ingrith's, Dagny's and the scene's lines are drafted.
entries.why: Spec §3 beat 9, §7.3 (the receipt lines are the spec's).

entries.what: The Sunshaft Staff: quarterstaff +2, spell save DC +1; its 'Light at will' built as every foe starting a fight revealed while it's carried (Aurdin already has the Light cantrip).
entries.why: Spec §8.

entries.what: Milestone XP: 2,500 at Ingrith's offer, 4,000 / 7,000 / 10,000 at the lamps, 13,000 at the consult. With the road's fights, about level 6 at First Lamp, 8 at Third Lamp, 9 at the door. SUPERSEDED 09-27 by recut-ladder: only the consult's milestone stands, at 5,000 (RULED 09-26d).
entries.why: Spec §9 (the main at 6-7 for the highway, all four at 8-9 for Third Lamp and the door).

entries.what: The smoke as built: Tam's couch (5 sp) opens after the chuul; the den drawn by the scene itself in 8-bit (the party laid out on the couch, lamp, racks, smoke rising, grey down from the top); a 23-second full-resolution dream in three beats (Solara on its headland with a sun-disc over the gate; the storm, light down by thirds, three strikes, the tallest tower's top falling, the disc dark; the cloud closing, the copper spire rising from below and through it; the pierce, the cloud torn outward, daylight, the broken tower, the disc lit; a hold, a fade); wind, thunder, a bright ring, the title theme on waking; skippable on a second viewing by holding E. The common pipe is a short rest for a silver.
entries.why: Spec §12 (the three beats APPROVED by Griz 09-26 §15-8; the den on vice row per his correction).

entries.what: Tam's offer, her line after the dream, and the dwarf-on-the-couch line (shown once the party has met the cleric and he lives).
entries.why: Spec §12 (Tam's part, drafted by the Cowork seat). RE-TAGGED 10-09: drafted lines are the branch's (fold: game); the person stands on the realm wiki by their own line.

entries.what: All ten sidequests of spec §10 built in the seat's order (3 6 9 1 5 10 2 4 7 8), each as the spec's paragraph describes, with journal entries and pins for six of them.
entries.why: Spec §10 (RULED 09-26: the seat's department, all ten).

entries.what: The heir's names are the build's: Wenna (the dying woman in the chapel), Asmund of the Silversands (her husband, the wedge's patron), Signy (the child hidden in the Shaft Rows, now a rope-maker who looks sixty); Old Hob as the one who knows a face that never aged; Ingrith (or, once she has gone down, the ledger-clerk) records the heir; the rite gives Asmund's Hammer and renown +1.
entries.why: Spec §10-9 (the seed is Griz's, personae slot 30; the names are not in it).

entries.what: Every line in the sidequests is drafted: Brann on the Geirmund gear and his father's axe, Vera's price, the First Lamp trooper, Aldwin, Old Hob, Signy, Ingrith on the weights, the count and the heir, Hessle ('My daughter'), Falstaff, the wheelwright's plea, Idony's price and her copy, Androit's refusal, Ragna, Mical, Tobin, Winters, Lucia, Pyro's four road lines. RETIRED IN PART 09-27: sidequest 1 (the assay weights, Hessle's scales, Falstaff's 150 sp) is retired (Griz 09-26d: 'retire it'), and sidequest 5 (Second Lamp's dark, the slates, the hit-die rest, the lamp's debt) falls with Second Lamp's abandonment (it is a manned outpost now, CANON 09-26d). Their lines stay in content/text.json, unused.
entries.why: Spec §10; the no-stubs law. RE-TAGGED 10-09: drafted lines are the branch's (fold: game); the person stands on the realm wiki by their own line.

entries.what: Numbers the spec left open: Vera pays 80 sp for the sack; Falstaff 150 sp; Winters 500 sp (the spec's); antitoxin at cost = 25 gp; the dark-lamp rest costs each hero one hit die of HP; the stair-holding fight is a crew boss, two thugs and two night crews; Hessle's true word names only 'something a dwarf pawned, copper-coloured' (the game never says egg). RETIRED IN PART 09-27: sidequest 1 (the assay weights, Hessle's scales, Falstaff's 150 sp) is retired (Griz 09-26d: 'retire it'), and sidequest 5 (Second Lamp's dark, the slates, the hit-die rest, the lamp's debt) falls with Second Lamp's abandonment (it is a manned outpost now, CANON 09-26d). Their lines stay in content/text.json, unused.
entries.why: Spec §10 (the build's figures).

entries.what: The wheelwright's lift: two platforms in the Sunshaft (the foot and the head of the shaft), warping between them.
entries.why: Spec §10-10 (a warp between tiers; a mechanic, not a cutscene).

entries.what: The spine re-cut around Pyro (09-27): the hook hands out no mission; Pyro, sympathetic, walks the road with the party when they say so (never imposed); Second Lamp, then off the highway to Halldor's unit pinned up the north cut; the escort home past a relief column; Pyro's trust opens the halls and shuts the road; Halldor's petition after two sidequests; the nest; the first rest after it brings Ulf's runner (the drow have taken Third Lamp) and the muster; the raid, leg four, the door, the consult as built. Flags pyroLeads, captainFound, captainHome, pyroTrusts, halldorUp, petition, nestCrushed, wordBelow, mustered, raidWon, highwaySecured.
entries.why: handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §2 (his arc, verbatim in TarlynsPit/source/pours-2026-09.md §09-26c/§09-26d: 'Have him go lead the adventurers to the second stop ... escort pyro and wounded captain back up the highway (he sends reinforcements back down) ... captain will be healed and petition the party ... then word of the Drow taking the third station')

entries.what: Pyro's sheet: fighter 9, two hand maces (three attacks: Extra Attack and the off-hand), Second Wind at under 40% HP, Action Surge when two or more foes stand, Indomitable, dwarven plate AC 18, 85 HP; counts as two heroes when fights are sized. His lines drafted: the first talk ('I've wanted someone through that door for a long time who wasn't a dwarf' is the seat's), the party check (Persuasion or Athletics 10), the offer, Ketil keeping the door, Ulf, the three road lines (the burial law, the sealed mint, what the road was for), the trust, the consult's word.
entries.why: handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §2 beat 2, §7 item 6 (RULED 09-26d: 'yes and bump to 9'); Griz 09-26c: 'I want to change Pyro to highly sympathetic with the adventurers. He dual-wields hand-held maces'

entries.what: Captain Halldor Silversands (fighter 6, warhammer and shield, 64 HP) and four troopers (fighter 4) holding a neck of rock in the north cut against phase spiders; he fights wounded at a third of his HP, at disadvantage, draws the foes' attacks, and a night's rest doesn't mend him; a healer's kit or 10 of Lymen's Lay on Hands mends him (flag captainTended), which he remembers at home and in his petition. His lines, the pinned troopers' and the relief column's are drafted ('The king's word came up the lamps. We go down.' is the seat's).
entries.why: handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §2 beats 3-5, §7 item 1 (RULED 09-26d: 'sounds fun')

entries.what: Second Lamp manned, never abandoned: Thyra Silversands and three; the drainage cut's two black puddings under a weighted grate; the roster slates and the dark-lamp debt cut (sidequest 5 with them). Third Lamp in three states: held by Geir Silversands and two before the word from below, taken after it (dark tower, crates, the captain's body), lit again after the raid. Past Third Lamp, before the word, the road is Deepholm's and nobody walks it. Names Thyra and Geir drafted.
entries.why: wiki/solskaft.md (Second Lamp a manned outpost: CANON 09-26d, his word 'The second lamp just an outpost that wasn't abandoned'; its garrison 'a captain and three' PROPOSED); handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §4

entries.what: Leg four, Third Lamp to Deepholm's door (highway_4, 80x24): the drow's fallback line (a blade-captain and four), the causeway over black water (a spirit naga), the troll hole (two trolls), the made road beginning at the midpoint (the first dressed stone moves here), the made road's cut (two earth elementals). The door's 'small spot' ends the fourth day; its lines re-cut for four days.
entries.why: wiki/solskaft.md (four days: CANON 09-26c, his word 'The 3-days journey with a stop at each day makes me want a 4 day journey'); handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §4

entries.what: Two new maps: the north cut (pinned, 20x15, off leg two just short of Second Lamp: a cavern, a neck of rock, a crate wall) and the nest (24x16, past the neck: a cocoon gallery, the brood chamber). The nest's cocoons hold a lost patrol's gear, taken on Halldor's word and the ledger's line: a diamond, a greater potion, dwarven plate (AC 18).
entries.why: handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §2 beats 3 and 5 (new map pinned, one screen, dark, a defensible dead-end; the nest one screen deeper, a cocoon gallery; the four-items thread may hang here, seat's call)

entries.what: The 6-9 ladder read right: no milestone XP at the lamps or at Ingrith's offer; one milestone stands, 5,000 at the consult. Encounter tables per leg (leg one 5-6: hobgoblin squads with a sergeant, bugbears, ogres with goblins; leg two 6-7: gibbering mouthers, gricks, ettins, phase spiders; leg three 7-8: duergar, a xorn pair, a cloaker, drow blade-captain squads; leg four 8-9: drow in force, troll pairs, a spirit naga, an earth elemental with a xorn, a stone giant with duergar), step rates 14-26 (legs one and two) and 12-22 (three and four). Random groups grow with the guests present (Pyro 2, Halldor 1 or 0.5 wounded, Brann and Hedda 1, a trooper or Ingrith 0.5: n x (4 + w) / 4). Set pieces budgeted hard by the DMG for the party present: the cut seal, the grick den, the roper with darkmantles, the bulette(s), two puddings, five phase spiders at the neck, the brood, a xorn pair, the stone giant's camp, the raid (a captain, the weaver, six drow). Estimated from the tables: about 6 by the north cut, 7 by the nest, 8-9 at the door before the consult's 5,000.
entries.why: handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §3 (his correction verbatim: 'It's meant as the combats available (at least a ways off the highway) should be appropriate for characters of lvls 6-9, increasing as the party approaches deepholm'; 5,000 RULED 09-26d 'rewarding talk-through is good')

entries.what: Eight creatures added: Ogre, Ettin, Phase Spider (Ethereal Jaunt read as one jaunt when bloodied, back through the wall at its next turn, attacking from out of sight), Stone Giant (Rock as a DEX save), Troll (Regeneration 10 unless fire or acid), Spirit Naga (Lightning Bolt, Hold Person), Earth Elemental (all mundane blows resisted, as the xorn), all SRD 5.1; and the Broodmother, game-original from the phase spider at CR 6 (AC 15, 120 HP, two bites with 6d8 poison, web, a jaunt). Art is recoloured from existing sprites (ogre and ettin from the bugbear, stone giant from the orc fighter, troll from the gnoll, naga from the snake, the elemental from the xorn, phase spiders from the giant spider); the Broodmother is the giant spider's painter drawn larger.
entries.why: handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §3; RULED 09-27 (Griz): 'recolor where possible makes the most sense with those givens'

entries.what: The clan hall turned on its axis: the throne on a dais at the north end, the oath-stone directly south of it, the doors south of that opening on a noon court, the Sunshaft's west bay; the beam drawn from the court through the doors to pool on the stone ('At noon the light lands here.'), not over the shaft floor. The hero-wall on the court's south face; the shrine of the Triad west of the hall on the court. Solskaft widened ten columns west and six east.
entries.why: wiki/solskaft.md (CANON 09-26c, his word: 'The sunbeam would land on the swearing stone, directly south of the throne dias and throne, straight through the doors'); handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §5

entries.what: The residential quarter: a street off the Sunshaft above the clan hall, ten barred family doors (Greyseam, Orri, Hallveig, Kolbein; Copperbottom with AT THE FORGE chalked on the bar; Asmund, Brandr, and the ended lines Geirmund and Audun), and one lit door, the Scalebeam house, where Asdis Scalebeam feeds the party (a rest point) and remembers Ingrith at six. Her lines drafted.
entries.why: wiki/solskaft.md (the familial residences, CLOSED; the Scalebeam house and Asdis; placement a west gallery above the clan hall: CANON 09-26d/e, his word 'Her family's residence would be in the same part of Solskaft as the other familial residences (which would be closed ...)'); handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §5

entries.what: The grow on the top terrace east of the Sunshaft: apple trees, cherries, pear trees, hops for the brewhouse, a mint bed, dry-land wheat along the long edge, a gardener trooper; the shroom farm in the dark past the dark barracks, and a trooper who says it's what Solskaft actually eats. 'Bread from below' and 'food comes down the highway' cut; the cook's line is the seat's draft ('Meat in the smoke, shrooms from the dark, apples from the light. Sit if you're sitting.').
entries.why: wiki/solskaft.md (the grow an apple orchard, RULED 09-26d: 'apple orchard and whatever else makes sense for east Washington state climate'; the shroom farms, CANON 09-26c); handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §5

entries.what: The Burial re-cut: both ways in (the drained stair's cut door, the dwarves' own stair) land in one hallway with four sealed doors and the Triad's chapel (the Forge-Father's grave-anvil, Rekknar's ledger-stone, the Dormant's empty cut, a lamp, a kneeling-stone); two straight stairs, Warrens side and Solskaft side, down through four tiers to a landing and the king's chamber at the bottom centre; eight wedge-places (two each side of each stair), seven families, the eighth waiting. The crew still works the Geirmund wedge; the catch springs at the head of the Warrens stair.
entries.why: wiki/solskaft.md (CANON 09-26c/d/e, his words: 'stairs we come down should lead into a hallway, with either sealed off rooms or a Cleric's chapel'; 'the shrine/chapel would be to all (3?) dwarven deities'; 'wide enough for two of those on each side - staircase to warrens side and staircase to solskaft side'); handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §5

entries.what: The mark reads as a mark once the stair is drained or the keeper is settled (F1); a keeper beaten in the base game leaves a dry stain (F2); the wheelwright bolts after any turn that ends with Hask down (F3); every bunk is a bed (F4); lamps offer a night and never impose one (F5); no LAMP · DAY box, legs named for where they go (F6); the journal one line at a time, the lamp warps only after the escort (F8); the weights retired and the front door a leave for four, the town not knowing why (F10).
entries.why: handoff-2026-09-26-dragonsleep-spine-recut.md §1 (his findings, verbatim)

entries.what: ?round6 on the URL: after the lead pick, all four at level 4 on their +2 weapons, every quest done but the Halfway (errands, the five by rope with the stock alive and the landlord fed, the cradles, the cull, the tail, the ettercap, the Hex card to Talmok, the Snoot, Winters' ring), renown 8, 1,500 sp, a modest bag, the lake pinned, Fountain Street. Vivian's archetype is left to the player.
entries.why: Griz 09-27 in the Code tab: 'Can you do with one all the char at lvl 4, all quests done but as if they've never gone to the half-way in the whole game, start in Silverton please? Don't worry about the saves'

entries.what: DEEP16, the 16-bit proof of concept past Deepholm's door (deep16/): a Diablo-angle grid fight on 5-ft squares with the fuller 5E rules, the 8-bit save carried across by PAST THE DOOR on the expansion's credits.
entries.why: Griz 09-26c: 'can we switch the game to 16-bit when they're on the other side of the edifice?'; spec handoff-2026-09-26-deep16-poc-spec.md; RULED 09-27: 'consider the proof of concept proven'.

entries.what: The Cocoon Gallery, an off-highway cavern below Third Lamp: a narrow neck off the road, a loose row of stalagmites, a ledge two steps up with a fallen slab for a ramp, rubble in a corner, a still pool, cocoons on the far wall (deep16/data/cavern.js).
entries.why: RULED 09-26d: 'let's do off highway cavern we can use somewhere' (the spec leaned to the re-cut's nest gallery). Place, so the Cowork seat folds it (THE TWO CANONS; his '4': the 16-bit layout is the truer rendering).

entries.what: The POC's two drow are the expansion's Drow Captain block (content/monsters.json drowcaptain, CR 5, 71 HP) given the SRD drow's hand crossbow (DC 13 poison) and Faerie Fire once (DC 12); the phase spider is the SRD block as written.
entries.why: RULED 09-26d: two drow and a phase spider; a plain SRD drow (13 HP) falls in a round to four level-9 heroes and would test nothing.

entries.what: DEEP16's second wave: when the two drow and the phase spider are down, the cocoon at the far wall's (5, 1) splits and a drider drops out -- the SRD 5.1 Drider as written (CR 6, 123 HP, AC 19; three attacks, longsword or longbow, one may be the bite; Faerie Fire 1/day; Fey Ancestry; Web Walker), dealt into the initiative on its own roll. Its look (09-27, the Cowork seat): its own pipeline-1 sheet, drider_p1 -- the hooded drow's upper half (KayKit Rogue_Hooded, legs hidden, the pack's knife for a blade since it has no longsword) mounted on the spider's thorax bone in Blender and rendered with it; replaces the JS composite of two sheets.
entries.why: Griz 09-27: 'adding a new monster to appear when these ones go down (your choice monster!)'. The code seat chose the drider for the gallery of cocoons under a drow ledge.

entries.what: The POC's looks: LPC figures (pipeline 0) for the heroes and the drow, a Blender pre-render (pipeline 1) for the phase spider, and Denny -- Griz's generated monkey in a denim jacket -- wearing Barley's sheet.
entries.why: RULED 09-27: 'Pipeline 0 is the way to go, maybe pipeline 1 for special monsters or fights'; 'Denny should play as Barley but look like Denny for this POC.' Barley is unchanged in the 8-bit game and the wiki.

entries.what: In DEEP16 a wizard of 3rd level or more knows Misty Step (it is not in the 8-bit game's spell list).
entries.why: The POC spec (sec. 3) lists it among Aurdin's grid features.

entries.what: Every spell the heroes know has a grid shape and range in DEEP16 (deep16/data/spells.js, from the SRD); Revivify, Daylight, Light and Detect Magic are listed as no use in the fight.
entries.why: Griz 09-27 in the pane: 'aurdin only being able to cast firebolt and lyman no spell access'.

entries.what: DEEP16's menus -- RING (a Secret of Mana ring, the main one: MAGIC by level, a level a ring of its spells; the turn starts on the grid and the ring comes up on Q or E over the hero), WINDOW (a Chrono Trigger command window, for those who'd rather); the first try's BAR of buttons dropped. BARM on the bar (bonus, action, reaction, move). A rogue's hiding places are tinted as she moves, always (the HINTS toggle gone), and a gold gem marks each square that would flank a foe with an ally across it.
entries.why: Griz 09-27: 'Curious about trying different menu ideas as well'; 'square tinting when she's moving that the rogue knows are places she can try to hide'; "what about circle menu 'magic' turns into level circle turns into spell list?"; then RULED: 'keep the ring (main) and menu (for people who don't like it)', the bar 'isn't pretty at all'; 'start of turn using wheel have move already selected'; 'seems we should just always do that for her (show where hide is possible)'; 'some indicator if you being in the square you're in ... you grant flanking of that enemy to at least one ally'.

entries.what: The ladder's fights (deep16/data/fights.js, 09-27): the 8-bit game's set pieces rebuilt on the grid -- 28 of them, from the Hex floor (L1) to the sect blades (L9) -- each on a map the Code tab drew from the 8-bit game's scene text (data/maps.js), each foe from content/monsters.json with SRD sizes, speeds and reaches, and each fight sized hard for the four by the DMG table where the 8-bit game sized it for its guests (the entry card says what the 8-bit list was). Levels are by that table, not by where the 8-bit game fights them (the night crew at 4, holding the stair at 2).
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'get as many fights ready for testing as you can. We should start with boss fights from the 8-bit that don't involve water ... The otyugh fight should probably slot in there'; the approved rung plan; 'better to disconnect and then pull the fights from the simulator and slot into the 8-bit later'.

entries.what: Water on the grid, hand-waved: a creature that lives in the water keeps to it (bound: the otyugh, the Keeper, the naga -- they move there unslowed and reach out of it) or swims in it and comes ashore (the chuul); nobody else swims, and water is difficult ground for them. The Keeper fight starts the four at the water's foot (the 8-bit game's WADE IN), and it starts unseen.
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'we're going to have to figure out the water thing (we'll probably hand wave the chuul fight rather than add swimming (for example))'.

entries.what: The lake fight on the ladder: Barley wears the Ring of Binding (+3 CON saves; on rounds 1, 4, 7 and 10 the chuul must turn on him), as the 8-bit game's ring reads.
entries.why: content/text.json winters.ring (RULED 09-23); the ladder has no equip screen, so the lead wears it.

entries.what: The wagon yard on the ladder: Amara and Willem fight only to get to the horses -- each turn a step (15 ft) toward the stable gate and their spells; either one through the gate loses the fight (THEY GOT AWAY WITH THE HORSES), where the 8-bit game starts its chase.
entries.why: events.js S.wagonFight ('the pair fight only to get to the horses'); the ladder has no chase to hand off to.

entries.what: Level-1 sheets for the four (deep16/js/save.js SV.levelOne): drawn back from the 8-bit game's level-2 starts -- one max hit die plus CON (the starts are exactly two: Barley 13, Aurdin 6, Vivian 9, Lymen 12), the level-1 slot table (Aurdin two first-level slots; Lymen none, so no Smite), no Action Surge, Lay on Hands 5.
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'might as well add level 1, we'll want it eventually'; RULED 09-25: a max hit die at every level.

entries.what: The ladder's creatures wear CC0 stand-ins (tools/deep16-figures.json, all PROPOSED to his eye): Quaternius Alien (ettercap), GreenSpikyBlob (otyugh, and in stone grey the xorns), Monkroose (bugbear chief), Orc and Orc_Skull (hobgoblins), Tribal (gnolls), BlueDemon (stone giant; in brown the earth elementals), Dino (bulette), Cactoro (roper -- it wears a hat), Frog (chuul -- no crab in the packs), Ghost (cloaker), Glub (darkmantle), Squidle (grick), the snakes (naga, the Keeper), the slime (puddings, ochre jelly, gray ooze), Bat, Husky (hyenas), Wolf at two squares (worg); KayKit Adventurers graded for the people (guards, Hask's crew, duergar, the sect blades, the spell-weaver, Amara and Willem); the phase spider at three squares (the broodmother).
entries.why: Griz, 09-27: 'loose fits are better than no fits'; the Cowork seat's asset map (handoff-2026-09-27-deep16-drider-and-bestiary-assets.md sec. 3).

entries.what: Inside the 8-bit game DEEP16 fights the 8-bit scene's own foes (sized there for the guests), each on its DEEP16 fight's spot for that kind; one with no spot is set on the nearest free square beside a spot of its kind in turn (hidden or in the rock as that one is), else beside the fight's first foe, never in the party's lap; a party bigger than the map's entry takes the nearest free squares behind it.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (Griz): the 8-bit's list is the roster; the placement is the seat's.

entries.what: The 8-bit game's dwarves on the grid (pyro_p0, halldor_p0, trooper_p0, brann_p0, hedda_p0, ingrith_p0, torvald_p0), LPC layers in the 8-bit LOOKS colours: the king in silver plate with a gold crown and a white winter beard; Halldor in iron plate; a trooper in mail and a nasal helm; Brann in steel plate with the war axe for his battleaxe; Hedda in mail; Ingrith in a white robe (her mail not drawn); the cleric hooded, a brown traveling cloak over a frock coat. Warhammers are drawn as the mace. Each squashed to a dwarf's build (tools/lpc-squash.py: short legs).
entries.why: Griz 09-28: guest art by LPC compose. LPC has no dwarf body and no warhammer.

entries.what: Torvald on the grid: 'He Will Not Be Held', at Deepholm's door (a new map: the made road's end, the step up to the door, the grille's bars either side, the bench). The card: 'A dwarf in a cleric's coat, a pack on his back and somewhere to be, and you fill the road. He will not be held.' He yields at half his hit points with his own words (deep.tvYield) on the card; killed outright, 'THE CLERIC IS DEAD ON THE MADE ROAD.' The 8-bit's AC 13, 40 HP and mace; WIS 16 and speed 25 drafted.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: 'under most circumstances it shouldn't end in a fight, but given the weight of the scene I think we should redo it in 16'. The door from deep.doorSee.

entries.what: The grid's opening cards inside the 8-bit game: 'CAUGHT OFF GUARD: they have the first round.' and 'THEY NEVER SAW YOU COMING: the first round is yours.' (the 8-bit battle's own two lines); the roper seen under the lamp, 'One of them is not a stalagmite, and the lamp has already shown you which.'; the lake without the ring, the 8-bit's own lake.risesNoRing; with it on someone other than Barley, the card names them.
entries.why: The 8-bit scene has already said who saw whom (its `surprised` / `revealed`), so DEEP16 rolls nothing and says so.

entries.what: Ottilie stops a party at the guano mine's mouth if anything it carries is always lit (an item's light with when: always; today only the Sunshaft Staff): '{name}. You can't go in there wielding that {item}. The light would spook the roost.' (or carrying it, seen glowing through the pack). LEAVE IT WITH HER / TURN BACK; left, it goes under her stool and back to the pack when the party is next at the mouth. The Sunshaft Staff's light drafted at the Light cantrip's 20 ft bright and 20 dim.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: the other light sources roost too; 'have the guy out front stop the players in the 8-bit if they have them equipped'; 'only things that are actively lit ... he can see the glow of the always on ones even when they are sheathed'; his line, the item named. The register gives the mouth's refusals to Ottilie (GalleriesModule/guano-galleries-DM.md §4). She keeps it because this game has no way to set a thing down (the staff is noSell).

entries.what: Shooting blind: an attack at a creature the attacker cannot see is at disadvantage, both games, as the SRD 5.1 has it; an unseen attacker has advantage, so two blind fighters roll straight.
entries.why: RULED 09-28: his first notion was a -4 ('shooting blind is just handled with a -4'); AMENDED the same day on his question -- the -4 was AD&D's number (2e: -4 to hit an unseen opponent), 'shouldn't be what the game does'. R.BLIND in js/rules.js keeps the -4 as a switch for both games.

entries.what: A torch takes a hand: a two-handed weapon takes both, a shield one, a torch one; a versatile weapon held with a torch hits for its one-handed die. Lighting one is an action (the SRD tinderbox); the Thief's Fast Hands make it a bonus. Dropped it burns where it fell; thrown (an action) it lands within 20 ft; doused it goes back in the pack; a lit one is spent.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: 'Aurdin would pretty much have to carry it lest lyman drop shield'. The action-or-bonus is a one-line switch (deep16/js/light.js LIGHT_COST), open for his word.

entries.what: Magic Missile may be aimed at a square the caster cannot see into (dark, magical darkness, fog): the darts fly and strike whatever hostile stands there; an empty square takes nothing but the slot. The card says AT THE DARKNESS.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: 'we have to do magic missile at the darkness gimmick somewhere in the game'. A switch (deep16/js/magic.js D.RULES.missilesAtTheDark), on by default; the set piece for it (the drow raid?) is his to place.

entries.what: Continual Flame asks for no ruby: a 2nd-level slot sets a heatless torch-bright flame on the weapon in hand, for good; it counts as always lit (Ottilie stops it at the roost's mouth).
entries.why: RULED 09-28: the rest spells are the game's only consumed components, 'nothing else consumes one'. Flagged: the SRD's 50 gp ruby is its balance.

entries.what: A torch lit in the field (ITEM, on a dark map) is carried by one hero with a free hand: the field's shadow opens wider and warmer round the party, a fight starts lit, and it burns till a rest or another map.
entries.why: The SRD torch burns an hour; the game has no clock between doors, so the map is the hour.

entries.what: The Mirror's eye, the pact of the Mirror's class feature (all its warlocks; Amara first): a mirror worn facing forward. In the cone before the wearer, a creature standing in any light cannot hide from her and gains nothing by being invisible. It shows nothing in the dark.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (Griz, on the ear file's hold: 'I'll agree with Mirror Eye and it needing light. All Mirror Warlocks should get it as a class feature'). In place of the PHB's Awakened Mind (not SRD); the register's 'asking' stays a story note. The cone is the wearer's facing and a little past the two beside it (deep16/js/magic.js inMirror).

entries.what: The gimmick's home: in the cloaker's deep gallery, the first Magic Missile thrown at the darkness is a cutscene -- a close-up of the caster with the clip 'attacking the darkness', the cloaker hit, its face with 'AND THE DARKNESS ATTACKS BACK' -- and the cloaker comes for the caster.
entries.why: Griz 09-28: the mp3 is the livestreams' branding; his own storyboard ('a quick cutscene close-up of Aurdin and then that mp3, then a close up of the cloaker showing it hit, then big close up cloaker face'). The second line's clip is his to record (deep16/audio/the_darkness_attacks_back.mp3); the caption carries it till then.

entries.what: The SRD 5.1 is used as it stands (licensed, CC BY 4.0; an SRD spell may wear a new name). What the register names past the SRD (the Player's Handbook's) the game makes its own: our name, our words, a function of our own -- never the book's thing under a new label. The register keeps what words it likes for the table; this is about what the public game ships.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (the ear file, dist-1, canon): his lean was 'sufficiently distinct' for a game a 12-year-old plays.

entries.what: Mirror's Gaze (Amara's 1st-level spell, in Hex's place), built on the SRD's Hunter's Mark: a bonus action, concentration; her hits on the marked one deal an extra 1d6 psychic, and while it is marked it cannot hide from her -- she always knows where it is, and being unseen gains it nothing against her. No curse on its checks.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-2, AMENDED: the name is his, 'Mirror's Gaze'). Hex is the PHB's, not the SRD's.

entries.what: Friends is dropped from Amara's cantrips; Minor Illusion (SRD, the warlock list) takes its place.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-3, canon): nothing in either game plays a Charisma contest where she'd cast it; Friends is the PHB's.

entries.what: Phantasmal Force is dropped from Willem's book; Blur (SRD, an illusion) takes its place. He keeps Mirror Image, Major Image, Hypnotic Pattern and his Ray of Frost.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-4, canon): Phantasmal Force is the PHB's.

entries.what: Amara's patron is the pact of the Mirror, a patron of our own in the Great Old One's place. Its expanded list, SRD spells, glass all through: 1st Silent Image, Hideous Laughter (and Glass Whisper, its own harm; and Command, the asking); 2nd Mirror Image, Detect Thoughts; 3rd Hypnotic Pattern, Clairvoyance; 4th Greater Invisibility, Confusion; 5th Mislead, Dominate Person. Its class feature is the Mirror's eye (#mirror-eye).
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-5, canon). The register's patron is the Great Old One (RE-RULED 08-29: 'the Great Old One -- the Mirror'), the PHB's; the SRD has only the Fiend. Flagged: the SRD's patrons carry two spells a level, this one four at the 1st. TRIMMED 09-28g (Griz: 'Trim'): its 1st carries two, the SRD's patrons' count -- Glass Whisper and Command, the two his words named; Silent Image and Hideous Laughter (the seat's) are off it.

entries.what: Glass Whisper (the pact of the Mirror's own 1st-level harm, ours): one creature within 60 ft that can hear her, WIS save or 2d6 psychic (+1d6 a slot above the 1st), and on a failure it sees itself in the glass and cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn; half on a save and nothing more.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-6, his note 'Glass Whisper'): in the place of Dissonant Whispers, the PHB's Great Old One spell, not carried.

entries.what: The register's 'asking that arrives like the memory of an asking' is Command (SRD 5.1, 1st level): one word, WIS save, and the target obeys on its next turn (FLEE, GROVEL, HALT, DROP, APPROACH). It is on the pact of the Mirror's expanded list, as the SRD's own Fiend patron carries Command at the 1st; Amara knows it. Kat described it in her own words; the spell keeps its SRD name.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (dist-7's open half; his words: 'if command is SRD we'll assume that's what Kat saw working and described in her own words, not change spell name' ... 'except it was a warlock not a cleric, so you're right unless warlocks have access to it'). The SRD Fiend's expanded spells are Burning Hands and Command at the 1st (dnd5eapi.co /subclasses/fiend), so a warlock's patron giving Command is the SRD's own shape. Flagged: it makes Amara's known spells seven at the 5th (the SRD's table says six). TRIMMED 09-28g (Griz: 'Trim'): Amara knows six at the 5th, the SRD's count -- Gaseous Form (OUT in the game) comes off her list for Command.

entries.what: An NPC of each SRD class, levels 1 to 6, built by the SRD's tables on the grid (DEEP16) to test every spell and feature before the story calls it in. Where an existing named NPC holds a class the generator builds that NPC by name (Higertha the half-orc druid; Torvald and Ingrith, clerics; Amara, warlock of the Mirror; Willem, wizard of illusion; and the others the register names); the rest are human, standard array (15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8) by the class's priorities, named only by class and level ('Cleric 5'). HP the SRD's fixed average (the max-die rule is for the story-vital, by name). Subclass the SRD's one each (the warlock's the Mirror or the Fiend).
entries.why: RULED 09-28 (Griz: 'Higertha is half-orc Druid, see if other existing NPCs need classes built and human the rest of the classes'; 'except when matching existing NPCs, generic is good'). The handoff 09-28 npc-classes-to-six.

entries.what: Aurdin's book grows by Rope Trick (learned at wizard 3) and Tiny Hut (at 5) in the build's picks; the climb's level-up list offers both.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 ('The build's picks'). The resting spells are field spells only (#rope-trick, #tiny-hut).

entries.what: The Dome Whorl: a fist-sized whorl off the Dominion shore, clear as glass and cold; a wizard breaks one to raise Tiny Hut for the night. Percy sells it, 250 silver -- his shelf's first thing for sale (a part: he buys one back at his fifth).
entries.why: RULED 09-28: 'have the bead be a special snailshell we just invented - we'll put them as a dominion shore export', Percy's, not cheap. The name and the price are the seat's draft (the drafts stand, RULED 09-24). FOR THE COWORK SEAT: a Dominion-shore export to fold into the realm (the place is canon, THE TWO CANONS).

entries.what: Rope Trick in the 8-bit field: a short rest wherever a tent could go (outside, or down a dark working), the party up a rope into a hidden space; it takes a 2nd-level slot and a skein of Gulch Silk.
entries.why: RULED 09-28: 'the resting spells ... a short rest like the tent, spends a skein of Gulch Silk'. The SRD's needs a rope; the silk is the game's first consumed component.

entries.what: Tiny Hut in the 8-bit field: a long rest wherever a tent could go, the same rest the inn gives (the story clocks count it, the morning's spells, the save); cast from the book as the SRD's ritual (no slot, never prepared); it breaks a Dome Whorl.
entries.why: RULED 09-28 ('making sure their long-rests are counted with the others and allow saves'). The SRD's needs a small crystal bead; here the whorl.

entries.what: Lymen's paladin list grows by Command, Branding Smite and Magic Weapon, and his Oath of Devotion keeps Protection from Evil and Good and Sanctuary ready from the 3rd, in both games (one law: js/rules.js R.PALADIN_SPELLS, R.oathSpells). The 8-bit battle casts all five: Command, one of four words (GROVEL, HALT, FLEE, DROP), and the commanded foe's next turn is spent obeying (the dead and the witless don't understand it); Branding Smite's +2d6 radiant rides the next weapon hit and takes invisibility off the one struck; Magic Weapon makes an ally's plain weapon +1 (+2 from a 4th-level slot) and magical; Protection from Evil and Good gives the otherworldly (aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, fiend, undead) disadvantage on the warded one and keeps their fear off it; Sanctuary makes a foe save WIS to strike the warded one, else it turns on another, and it ends when the warded one attacks or casts at a foe. Each lasts the fight (ten rounds); the 8-bit battle keeps no concentration, as with Bless and Hold Person.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on 'Should the 8-bit's own battle get Lymen's new spells?'): 'yeah, they have to be able to transfer back and forth from 16bit fights'.

entries.what: In the 8-bit battle a bonus-action spell costs the bonus action, not the action, as on the grid (SRD 5.1): Divine Favor, Shield of Faith, Branding Smite, Magic Weapon, Sanctuary, Healing Word, Spiritual Weapon. The hero still has the action (FIGHT, an item, a cantrip); a levelled spell with it is greyed, the SRD's rule. Before this every 8-bit spell took the action.
entries.why: The seat's, 09-28g, from the same ruling: a spell that crosses should play the same on both sides, and Branding Smite taking the whole turn before its blow would have made it nothing in the 8-bit. Divine Favor and Shield of Faith get cheaper for Lymen: the playtest's to say.

entries.what: Ingrith is a cleric 4 in the 8-bit game too: the SRD's average HP by the d8 (31, where the fighter sheet had 36), slots 4/3, WIS; the drafted list (Sacred Flame, Guidance; Bless, Cure Wounds, Healing Word, Shield of Faith; Aid, Lesser Restoration) and the Life Domain's Spiritual Weapon; the Life Domain, the SRD's one (heavy armour, so her chain mail and shield stand at AC 18; Disciple of Life; Preserve Life). The 8-bit battle runs her turn as a cleric: a friend down gets Healing Word and the mace after; two or more low, Preserve Life; one low, Cure Wounds; two or more dead things, Turn Undead; the first round against more than one, Bless; else the floating weapon and the mace. The old heals counter is retired; a save made with the fighter sheet walks her on as the cleric, as hurt as she was. On the grid the overlay steps aside: her sheet is the cleric's.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz: 'Yes, she's meant to be Cleric.'). The domain is the seat's: the register names none (Cleric of Rekknar), the class-NPC rule gives the SRD's one, and it fits a guest who heals and keeps her armour.

entries.what: What the 8-bit pack and gear do on the grid, checked (dev/bench16.js mode=items): the pack crosses as it stands (no crossbow lent inside the 8-bit game), and the named items and the pie now do there what they do in the 8-bit battle: the Winnower knocks one flat on a critical; the Greyseam knife's Sneak Attack poisons (CON 13, till the end of its next turn); the Door-Shield's ward (a miss at its bearer on a natural 15 or more, 3%: +3 AC to the party till the bearer's turn); Marta's bat-wing pie eaten in the fight (+5 HP, +1 CON saves, the fight's alone: it crosses back without the +5, never read as Aid); the elixir cures paralysis too. Already there: potions, kits, antitoxin, oil, torches, the Flame Tongue, the Cloak of Displacement, the Ring of Protection, the Sunshaft staff's DC and its light, the Ring of Binding at the lake.
entries.why: Griz 09-28g: 'Also need to make sure items are being loaded into the 16bit fights.'

entries.what: The black pudding's and the gray ooze's acid eat weapons and armour for the fight only; nothing is worn down for good.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on 'Should the ooze's acid wear gear down for good?'): 'No'. (The SRD's corrosion is permanent.)

entries.what: The Path of the Sand, Talmok's barbarian path, our own in the Totem Warrior's place. 3rd: FIRST BLOOD -- when he takes damage and isn't raging, he can rage as his reaction (a use spent); DOWN IN THE SAND -- raging, once on each of his turns, a creature no bigger than Large that he hits in melee saves STR (8 + proficiency + STR) or goes prone. 6th: ANSWER BACK -- raging, when a creature in his reach misses him in melee, his reaction is one melee attack back.
