Built on the grid (deep16/js/features.js); on the Pocket DM as ?npc=talmok (barbarian 3, his register numbers and pit fists, no handaxes to throw). The ladder's card keeps his bestiary sheet, whose rage-on-hit and prone fists are the 3rd level's two features in stat-block form. Levels 7-9 (09-28h): no new path feature till the 10th; the barbarian's own -- FERAL INSTINCT at 7 (advantage on initiative; caught unaware, he acts on his first turn if he rages first), BRUTAL CRITICAL at 9 (one more weapon die on a melee critical: his pit fists have none, so it adds nothing to them), rage +3 at 9, and the ASIs past his register's 3rd (STR 18 at 4, 20 at 8). Built at any level as ?npc=talmok:7 and on the tester ladder (?ladder&party=ours); the story's Talmok stays 3. 09-28h: PIT FISTS (3rd) -- his unarmed strikes hit for 1d4 + STR, 1d6 from the 6th (js/rules.js damageExpr, both games); the 8-bit Talmok's Pit Fists 1d4+3 (content/monsters.json; a flat 4 before), the grid's bestiary sheet the same.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on the subclasses past the SRD: 'Sufficiently distinct'): the register's 'rages on first blood, wrestles to the sand' (npcs-by-location.md §TALMOK) made the path's own; the Bear's resistance to everything is the PHB's and is not carried. 09-28h (Griz: 'can we do the levels for the original classes up to nine' -- 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'; 'AI now, buttons later'). RULED 09-28h (Griz, asked why the fists had no die, so Brutal Critical added nothing: "Almost certainly, but I don't know why they didn't already"). They had none because the register's pit fists were built as the SRD 5.1 unarmed strike, a flat 1 + STR.

entries.what: The Rimeglass, Willem's arcane tradition, our own in the School of Illusion's place: illusion with the cold in it. 2nd: RIME DOUBLES -- a blow that breaks one of his false images (Mirror Image) breaks rime over the one who struck: its speed 10 ft less till the end of its next turn. 6th: RIME STEP -- when he casts an illusion of the 1st level or more, he steps 10 ft through the rime (a teleport, to the square farthest from his foes). Built on the grid; Willem (wizard 5) has the 2nd's in the wagon yard. Levels 7-9 (09-28h): no new tradition feature till the 10th. Past his register's 5th, the seat's picks, illusion with the cold in it: Sleet Storm, Fear, Slow (3rd); Phantasmal Killer, Greater Invisibility, Ice Storm (4th); Cone of Cold, Mislead, Hold Monster (5th); below it Color Spray, Magic Missile, Sleep, Hold Person; the cantrips Chill Touch and Shocking Grasp; INT 19 at 8; Mage Armor up when he is built away from his 5th. Built at any level as ?npc=willem:9 and on the tester ladder; the story's Willem stays 5.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz: 'Sufficiently distinct'); his cold is his own word ('Willem is a frosty person', 09-28), the doubles his register's Mirror Image, the step his office of covering the going. 09-28h (Griz: 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'): the list is the seat's draft, standing as approved; every spell on it casts on the grid.

entries.what: The Window, the cleric's domain of Tronupholen, the Fey in the Mirror (Kat's), our own in the Trickery Domain's place. Its spells, always prepared: 1st Disguise Self, Silent Image; 3rd Blur, Pass without Trace ('close the ground'); 5th Hypnotic Pattern, Clairvoyance. 1st: THE HAND ON THE NECK (WIS a long rest) -- a bonus action, a touch: the first blow that would land on the touched before the mender's next turn is rolled again, and the second roll stands (the glass takes it). 2nd: THE DOUBLING (Channel Divinity) -- two glass doubles step out of her mirror, and a blow at her may strike one instead (Mirror Image's odds). 6th: THE SHOWING (Channel Divinity) -- one creature within 30 ft that can see her mirror saves WIS or is shown something in the glass and can do nothing till the end of its next turn. On the Pocket DM as ?npc=katarina (human, at any level: her level is unruled in the register), leather and a shield, a mace. Its spells at the 7th: Greater Invisibility, Confusion; at the 9th: Mislead, Hold Monster (all four cast on the grid). 8th: DIVINE STRIKE -- once on each of her turns, a creature she hits with a weapon attack takes 1d8 psychic more (the glass shows it a crack). On the tester ladder (?ladder&party=ours) at every level 1-9. 09-28h: Katarina's register level is 3 (deep16/js/classes.js NPC.NAMED.katarina lvl 3).
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz: 'Kat supposed to be Cleric of trickster deity trapped in mirror'). The names are the register's field words (serial-castegut/BIBLE.md 08-27: 'the hand on the neck', 'close the ground', 'the doubling'; 'three of her'); the functions are new, not the PHB's Blessing of the Trickster, Invoke Duplicity or Cloak of Shadows. Tronupholen shows, never speaks (08-13i). 09-28h (Griz: 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'): the seat's drafts; Divine Strike is the SRD Life Domain's 8th, in her god's own kind. RULED 09-28h (Griz): "at campaign start she's just hit 3".

entries.what: The Vigil, the cleric's domain of Dvalgarda, the Ward of the Dormant (Torvald's): the register names no domain, so it is our own. Its spells, always prepared: 1st Sanctuary, Protection from Evil and Good; 3rd Hold Person, Warding Bond; 5th Spirit Guardians, Glyph of Warding (not built: not cast). 1st: KEEPER'S WARD (WIS a long rest) -- a bonus action, one he can see within 30 ft (or himself): the next damage it takes before his next turn is cut by 1d8 + his cleric level. 2nd: HOLD THE DOOR (Channel Divinity) -- each foe within 10 ft saves STR or is shoved 10 ft away from him. 6th: WAKEFUL -- magic cannot put him, or one of his within 10 ft, to sleep. Built on the grid; Torvald (cleric 5) carries the 1st and 2nd at Deepholm's door. Its spells at the 7th: Guardian of Faith, Freedom of Movement; at the 9th: Hold Monster, Dispel Evil and Good (all four cast on the grid). 8th: DIVINE STRIKE -- once on each of his turns, a creature he hits with a weapon attack takes 1d8 radiant more (the Dormant's cold light). Past his register's 5th, the seat's picks: Protection from Energy, Mass Healing Word, Death Ward, Banishment, Mass Cure Wounds, Greater Restoration; WIS 18 at 8. Built at any level as ?npc=torvald:9 and on the tester ladder; the story's Torvald stays 5.
entries.why: RULED 09-28g (Griz, on 'Torvald has no domain': 'Sufficiently distinct'). Grounded in the register's Dvalgarda, Ward of the Dormant, whose sect keeps the vigil over the sleeping Silver and the egg (pantheon.md, CANON 08-28), and in his own fight's card: 'He will not be held.' 09-28h (Griz: 'the off SRD ones we made to 9'): the seat's drafts; Freedom of Movement for his card's 'He will not be held'.

entries.what: The tester ladder (?ladder&party=ours) builds our four as their grown builds at every level, their register's own included; one of ours who is that rung's foe (Willem in the Wagon Yard, Talmok on the Card's Top) is swapped for an alternate: Higertha, then a paladin (deep16/js/classes.js NPC.ours, NPC.ALTS).
entries.why: RULED 09-28h (Griz): "grown builds please"; "swap in alternates (your choice) rather than mirror" -- Higertha the seat's choice (a named NPC who stands at any level).

entries.what: A hooded lantern (50 sp at the Provisioner's and the Chandler's): bright 30 ft and dim 30 more; hood down, dim light 5 ft only and no bright light, so nothing light-shy is dazzled and a roost sleeps. It takes a hand like a torch, is never thrown, and is not spent: doused or put away it goes back in the pack. On the grid: ITEM lights it (under a roost, hood down), HOOD DOWN / HOOD UP, SET DOWN, DOUSE, TAKE UP; HOOD UP is refused under a roost. In the 8-bit fight the hood is implicit: under a roost the lantern lights the place dimly and nothing wakes; elsewhere it is a 30-ft torch. The camp's A LIGHT IN HAND walks in with either. Sleet does not put it out (its flame is not exposed).
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Hooded Lantern (5 gp; bright 30, dim 30; hooded: dim 5 ft) at the x10 economy (#economy). RULED 09-29 (Griz: 'like a mode that sort of lights and doesn't wake the bats'; 'I meant to cancel the no hood function decision'). Seat's calls: no oil to count (no fight runs six hours); the hood as the turn's free object interaction; sleet spares it.

entries.what: A generic druid NPC on the grid is a Circle of the Land druid of the Underdark: its circle spells (always prepared) are Web at 3, Stinking Cloud at 5, Greater Invisibility at 7 and Insect Plague at 9 (the SRD's list, the built ones; spider climb, gaseous form, stone shape and cloudkill left off). Higertha keeps the mountain (#higertha-druid): Spike Growth at 3, Lightning Bolt at 5, Stoneskin at 7.
entries.why: The SRD's Circle of the Land needs a land; the Pit is underground. The seat's call, 09-29 (Higertha to nine); a spec may name another land.

entries.what: WILD SHAPE offers the bestiary's beasts by the Circle of the Land's rule: the wolf, the wolf spider and the axe beak from 2 (CR 1/4, no flying or swimming), the giant frog from 4 (swimming allowed), the giant spider from 8 (CR 1); a Large shape stands in the druid's own square, and the beast's whole attack rides (the spiders' poison, the frog's grip). OWN SHAPE, a bonus action, ends it early.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Wild Shape and the Land circle's CR table, limited to the sheets the grid has; the button and the pick RULED wanted 09-29 (Griz: 'druid beast form ... we'll have to do that').

entries.what: Enlarge gives no reach: the SRD 5.1 text grants +1d4 on weapon hits, advantage on STR checks and saves, and one size category, nothing about reach. The +5 ft the grid gave on 09-29 (a runner's build on Griz's 'might') is kept as a house-rule switch, off: D.RULES.enlargeReach (deep16/js/magic.js), read by G.reachOf.
entries.why: Griz 09-29: 'check rules if you can, that was my remember guess' -- checked, the SRD says no reach; the switch keeps the option.

entries.what: Calling Herbs (content/items.json callingherbs, 500 sp, sold only at Mama's Pharmakaiea): charcoal, incense and herbs Mama mixes; a wizard burns one bundle each time he casts Find Familiar, a new shape included.
entries.why: RULED 09-29, Griz: 'i'd like to add a material component for 500 sp only mama sells despite our normal hand-wave of components' (the SRD's 10 gp of charcoal, incense and herbs, priced up and placed with Mama, who mixes).

entries.what: Find Familiar's shape is picked from what lives on the ground under the party (js/rules.js R.FAM_GROUND / R.famForms): on the world map by tile (snow: snowy owl; fields: owl, rat; forest: owl, spider; water: frog, poisonous snake; stone and gulch: bat, spider, snake; cave mouths: bat, rat, spider), off it the caves' (bat, rat, spider) or the town's (rat, owl). Forms with no DEEP16 sheet yet (hawk, raven, cat, weasel, lizard, crab, octopus, fish, sea horse) are left off the pick. The snowy owl is the owl's regional form (the same numbers).
entries.why: Griz 09-29: 'we can do it from the menu on the worldmap menu and select by biome'; the lists are the seat's draft; the snowy owl came with the generated sheets ('SNOWY REGIONAL FORM').

entries.what: In an 8-bit fight the familiar rides the wizard's shoulder: if he makes no attack roll on his turn, the first ally to attack after it has advantage; if he does, his own first attack roll that turn has it. The foes never pick it; a blast that catches the wizard catches it whatever his save (at 0 it is gone, flags.familiarGone; the ritual calls it back). 09-30: the help is drawn -- it goes from his shoulder (or heel) to the target just before the roll it helps (his own first attack, a spell's first ray, the spiritual weapon's swing, or the first ally's blow) and back: the fliers arc (14 frames out, 10 there, 14 home), the others run the ground line. The bat loops about his head (a figure-eight in front of him); in the 8-bit the bat still helps ("8bit should be fine as is").
entries.why: RULED 09-29, Griz: 'my notion at giving 8-bit the help action of the familiar without adding a choice to the combat. First ally to attack after wizards turn if the wizard doesn't attack should work'; and 'not targeted by AI but subject to splash damage that includes the wizard, even if wizard saves'. 09-30, Griz: "I thought it would fly to help after aurdin picked a spell to attack with but before the spell went off, and fly from aurdin to target before allies attack lands when aurdin doesn't target on his turn"; the bat: "correct" (about his head in the 8-bit too). Geometry and timing a runner's draft (js/familiar.js).

entries.what: On the grid the familiar has no initiative: its turn comes right after its caster's. A touch spell on one not beside him goes by the familiar when a square beside that one is within the familiar's movement (flier or walker, from his square while it rides); it goes as the spell is cast and its own turn is the rest of that movement, spent heading home; not when he has ordered it to Help that turn, and an owl that carried one does not help that round. The owls help on their own (Flyby), the bat never, the others on his order (FAMILIAR: HELP on his SKILLS, free: SRD 'it always obeys your commands'; FAMILIAR: STAY calls it off); a caster the fight runs orders it himself. It rides again once it gets back into his square (5 ft to spare from beside him); short of it when its movement runs out, it holds a square and the foes may strike it. Out on the field the bat stand-in is drawn up in the air; riding, it loops about his head. AMENDED 09-30: the bat helps on his order like the others (it keeps its place about his head); in the 8-bit it helps as ever.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "I'd put the familiars 'turn' after his casters ... if my familiar is out and I cast a touch spell on someone not next to me - it should fail if it's out of the familiars movement ... (only way a familiar is on a square is if it runs out of movement - at which time it would enter enemy targeting"; the bat "flutter around his head". The seat's calls: the ordered one picks the foe the party is on (as the owl does); the AI's casters order it; +5 ft to step into his square. Built deep16/js/familiar.js (09-30). Griz 09-30: "i think the bat not helping is out of balance and should be orderable in the 16 and let it keep doing it in the 8".

entries.what: What each familiar lends its caster while it is in the fight (js/rules.js R.FAMILIARS perk): rat darkvision 30 ft; bat sonar 15 ft (blindsight: any dark, the unseen); poisonous snake senses the hidden and the invisible within 15 ft (as sight), +1 to the save DC of his charm spells (R.CHARM_SPELLS), advantage on his Persuasion (a familiar's Help on a check, SRD); spider Web Walker and +1 to his Web's DC; frog: he is never caught off guard (a croak, js/audio.js croak). A perk is its caster's, whoever that is (the NPC casters and the Pocket DM's too). And on a dark map with no light, on a hero's turn, the grid is drawn through that hero's own senses: what he does not sense darker, darkvision grey, blindsight cool with a ping (deep16/js/light.js senseMap). In the 8-bit (no ranges): the rat's and the bat's caster sees in any dark; the snake's sees the invisible and the `unseen` foes (the keeper, the cube, the roper) plainly; a charm spell +1 (no hero spell charms yet); Persuasion with advantage, and when the party's best hand rolls he ranks +3 for the pick; the spider's caster is not held by a foe's web spit, and his Web +1; the frog's caster acts in a surprised first round (no assassin's crit on him) and the croak sounds.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "rat grants nightvision, spider buffs web spell and gives 'webwalk' ... snake sense hidden within 15 feet (counts as vision)" · "Agreed with vision range." · "EXCELLENT call on the frog. will need audible." · "Snake still charm related spells, diplomacy and persuasion checks by caster" · "when map = no light source and player turn, active player vision filter on dark map (i.e. bat familiar sonar sight filter unless light on map)". The ranges were the seat's proposal, agreed; the +1s, the advantage, the croak's sound and the filter's look are the seat's drafts. The 8-bit reading of the 09-30 perks: a runner's draft (js/familiar.js, js/battle.js, js/deep.js EV.check; bench8 perks/perks2).

entries.what: The summons on the grid (deep16/data/summons.js D.SUMMON / D.summonPool, deep16/js/grimoire.js summonSpell): a summoning spell's pool is the bestiary itself, read by creature type and CR (a creature joins by being drawn into data/foes.js; `summon: false` keeps a story's own out; named, bound and class-built sheets and familiars never answer). The caster picks the creature, and the count is the most the SRD's options allow of it (x2 at a 5th-level slot for Conjure Animals); the AI's casters take the most worth (its best blow times its blows times the count, its HP as a wall). They appear on the free squares he can see nearest the point within 60 ft, take one initiative for the lot, fight under the AI (ai.js brute), vanish at 0 HP and all together when his concentration ends; they keep no fight going and cross nothing back to the 8-bit game. Conjure Woodland Beings is built on the same frame and waits, greyed, for the first fey. The ranger's 3rd is Conjure Animals too (SRD).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "1 - I like it. Build a frame so that it's pulling those selections from a place where more to choose from might go as the world expands?" (the seat's proposal: the caster picks from the beasts we have by count and CR; they fight under the AI as if commanded, not the SRD's defend-only). The worth formula, the placement and the ranger's list are the seat's.

entries.what: The walls on the grid (deep16/js/walls.js; B.walls read by grid.js through G.wallAt): each is the SRD 5.1's line form, a straight run of squares laid across the caster's line to the point he picks, centred on it (one click; the ring and the dome forms are not built). Wall of Fire 60 ft, opaque, lit along its length; its burning side is the one away from him. Wall of Thorns 60 ft, blocks sight, 20 ft more a square. Wall of Stone 60 ft (the SRD allows ten 10-ft panels), bars the way and the eye; whoever stands where it rises is pushed out, his own to his side, the rest to the far one; the panels' AC and hit points are not built -- it stands till his concentration goes. Wind Wall 50 ft: arrows, bolts and thrown weapons across it miss; a small flier cannot cross; sight passes; the gases it keeps back are not built. The AI raises the burning ones (fire, thorns) where they catch the most of the other side; the stone and the wind are the player's. The wizard's and the sorcerer's class lists carry Wall of Fire and Wall of Stone; Higertha's mountain gets Wall of Stone at 9.
entries.why: The druid to twelve (Griz 09-29: "please complete druid to 12"), the handoff's step 2 (WALLS). The line form, the lengths, the burning side, the push, the AI's reach and the looks are the seat's; the damage, saves and costs are the SRD's.

entries.what: Polymorph, Dominate Beast, Charm Person and Animal Friendship on the grid (deep16/js/grimoire.js, deep16/js/features.js F.morph, ai.js heroes). Polymorph: the new shape is one of the world's beasts (deep16/data/summons.js D.pool, the summons' place) of the target's CR or level or less; the player picks, the AI makes a foe the weakest it can and never polymorphs a friend; the target keeps its footprint. Dominate Beast: the beast fights for the caster's side under the AI while concentration holds and saves again each time it is hurt; it keeps no fight going for them and is still the 8-bit's foe when the fight ends. A charm (Charm Person, Animal Friendship) takes its charmer off the charmed one's list of targets; harm to it on a turn of the charmer's side breaks it (the source of a blow read as whoever's turn it is). The charms were added last to each class's list (druid, bard, ranger, wizard, sorcerer), so what the NPCs prepare mostly stands.
entries.why: The druid to twelve (Griz 09-29: "please complete druid to 12"), the handoff's steps 3 and 4 (SHAPES, CHARM / DOMINATE). The mechanics are the SRD 5.1's; the picks, the AI's use and the harm-by-turn reading are the seat's.

entries.what: Antilife Shell, Plant Growth, Cloudkill and Giant Insect on the grid. Antilife Shell (deep16/js/walls.js): no creature but the undead and constructs steps across its 10-ft edge (grid.js stepCost via G.shellBars) or lands a melee blow across it (battle.js: the blow is turned; the AI may yet waste a swing on it); the caster moving so that the set of creatures inside changes ends it. Plant Growth: the road maps' grass squares within 100 ft of the point, 20 ft more a square, for the fight; no exclusions; greyed where nothing grows. Cloudkill (deep16/js/grimoire.js): obscuring fog (B.darks kind 'kill'), CON 5d8 on entering it the first time on a turn or starting a turn in it, rolling two squares straight away from its caster at the start of his turn; a Gust of Wind or a Wind Wall scatters it; the Underdark druid's circle spell at 9, the wizard's and the sorcerer's 5th. Giant Insect: the summons frame's fixed kinds (three giant spiders; the centipedes, wasps and scorpion when drawn), dealt in right after him on his roll. Tree Stride and the one-minute conjures wait.
entries.why: The druid to twelve (Griz 09-29: "please complete druid to 12"), the handoff's step 6. The mechanics are the SRD 5.1's; the grass as the plants, the drift's straight line, the shell's turned blow and the insects' place in the order are the seat's.

entries.what: The camp's CAST AHEAD shows only what someone in the party has on their list (known, or preparable today); with nothing to cast, the row itself is gone. Conjure Elemental joins it (a minute to cast: the camp's, never the fight's): whoever has it prepared and a 5th-level slot spends the slot; the elemental (the world's of CR 5 or less, the earth elemental first; the xorn is one too) walks in beside him on his side, with its own initiative, run by the fight, and holds his concentration -- the class AI values that concentration above any other spell; if it breaks the elemental breaks loose, hostile to its caster's side, a foe like any other (it keeps the fight going, and is not the 8-bit game's to count). Tree Stride is left out; Conjure Minor Elementals and Conjure Fey wait.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "We'll need to revisit the campfire precast interface since we're adding potentials - what's in there should be dependent on party members. Let's add the earth elemental to camp and hold off on the rest." · "tree stride ... leave it out for now". The loose elemental is the SRD's ("it becomes hostile toward you and your companions"); the side it takes, the xorn in the list and the AI's hold on the concentration are the seat's.

entries.what: The class feature gaps on the grid (deep16/js/features.js, rules.js, grimoire.js, magic.js, tactics.js, classes.js; bench mode `features`): the monk's Patient Defense, Step of the Wind and Evasion (7; RU.evasion, the rogue's too -- and not while incapacitated); the Devotion paladin's Turn the Unholy (fiends and undead, a WIS save, turned for ten of its own turns or till hurt; class NPCs only -- Lymen keeps Sacred Weapon); the bard's Countercharm (advantage on saves against frightened or charmed within 30 ft; hearing and silence are not modelled); the sorcerer's Twinned (the generic sorcerer's second option; not for concentration spells or Chain Lightning; cost the spell's level, 1 for a cantrip), Careful (up to CHA-mod friends spared, in the order they save) and Heightened (the player picks the foe); the warlock's Pact of the Tome for the generic Fiend warlock (Fire Bolt, Sacred Flame, Vicious Mockery) and of the Blade for a spec (a rapier by default) -- the Chain waits for its sheets, Amara has none; Dark One's Own Luck (taken without asking when a save with something at stake falls short by 10 or less, or the web's break-free check); Mindless Rage (a charm or a fright suspended while he rages, back after if its caster still holds it); the Hunter's Escape the Horde (the generic Hunter's), Multiattack Defense and Steel Will (a spec's); the Thief's Supreme Sneak. Found and fixed: the turned (Turn Undead's) were set free by the end-of-turn sweep of their caster's fright, so an AI cleric's Turn Undead did nothing.
entries.why: The class NPCs' feature gaps (handoff-2026-09-30-druid-to-twelve.md §6), Griz 09-30: "Class feature gap proceed". Built by a Sonnet runner; the SRD 5.1's rules; the named choices are the runner's and the seat's, his to overrule.

entries.what: HIDDEN MECHANIC (never shown to a player): Lisbet Crane's Charm (content/items.json `charm`, a ring, 5 sp, Charms & Chalk in Silverton) makes whoever wears it immune to being frightened, in both games -- the 8-bit's Moan never takes the wearer (and says nothing: a resisted Moan prints no line); on the grid a failed save against a fright simply holds (RU.save: the card shows the real roll and the outcome, never why). Its words stay "Lisbet's charm. No promises made." The rule lives in js/rules.js R.fearWard.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "that lady who sells an equipable charm in silverton - let's make that charm grant immune to fear in the mechanics, but not say so anywhere the player sees".

entries.what: CHANNEL DIVINITY is a list of its own on the grid's ring, beside SPELLS, with the uses left in its name: Sacred Weapon and Turn the Unholy (the Devotion paladin, Lymen too), Preserve Life and Turn Undead (the Life cleric; Preserve Life's button new: the lowest first, none past half), our domains' Doubling, Showing, Hold the Door. In the 8-bit, Lymen's SKILL shows CHANNEL DIVINITY (1/1), which opens Sacred Weapon and Turn the Unholy (the fiends and undead before him save WIS or cower, as the cleric's Turn Undead makes them).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "should the channel divinity be a button similar to spells?" -- "3 yes"; Lymen's Turn the Unholy: "pretty sure he's supposed to have it".

entries.what: A charm holds a hero the player runs as it holds the AI's: a charmed one cannot attack its charmer, aim a harmful spell at it, or take an opportunity attack at it (battle.js canHit and the attack, magic.js targetWhy, moveAlong); the refusal says so and spends nothing. And Fear, Phantasmal Killer and Weird bite on the grid: the fright a spell lays holds as long as the spell (the end-of-turn sweep of a caster's frights spares a spell's), so the feared flee -- Heroism is the answer (Lymen's from 4), and Lisbet's charm, hidden.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: "1 yes 2 yes" (on "fix Fear so it bites?" -- his lean before: "biting can be good" -- and "enforce charm on heroes you run?").

entries.what: Pyro at 12 (content/heroes.json, deep16/js/classes.js NPC.NAMED.pyro): the Champion; STR 20 by the fighter's 12th-level ASI (his register's 18 at 9); HP 112 (the 9's average on); his off-hand the SRD Mace of Disruption (content/items.json macedisruption, 'clearly magical': magic, its 20/20 light while drawn); Dwarven Plate +3 (kingsplate: the SRD's Dwarven Plate is +2, ours +3 by his word; its shove-reduction reaction not built); the King's Mantle (kingsmantle: +5 to saving throws against spells -- name and words the seat's). The 8-bit guest is 12 too now (the measure holds him back), and the road weighs him as one guest, not two (js/deep.js GUEST_WEIGHT).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'Gonna have to Pyro NPC up to 12, he's key', 'his off-hand to be a mace of disruption if it's in our available magic items via SRD, clearly magical'; 09-30b: 'Also give him +3 dwarven plate, and a cloak +5 to saves vs spells.' The ASI, the name and the weight are the seat's.

entries.what: Hammer and Tongs, our fighting style (the Champion's Additional Fighting Style at 10, Pyro's): fighting with a one-handed weapon in each hand, light or not, one of the Attack action's swings may be the off-hand's -- besides Two-Weapon Fighting's bonus-action strike. At 12 that is five swings a turn: three by Extra Attack (5 and 11), one off-hand in the action, one off-hand as the bonus action (deep16/js/pyro.js, js/pyro.js).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'unless there's a fighting style (make it up if it's not) that gives him an extra attack with off-hand'; 09-30b: 'Yes regarding offhand' (the seat's reading, five swings at 12). Name and words the seat's.

entries.what: Pyro's measure (deep16/js/pyro.js, js/pyro.js): every fight he walks in, both games. Phase 1: one swing of the plain mace and his turn is over; the white mace at his belt. Phase 2 (he is at half HP, or one of the party is down): he draws the Mace of Disruption, two swings a turn, says his piece, and each of the party's XP is halved (the level kept). Phase 3 (one of the party leaves the fight -- on the grid, out the way they came in; in the 8-bit, the party's RUN): the white mace into his main hand, full level 12 to the end, then the save is loaded (FOUND WANTING). Down: the fight ends there and the save is loaded (THE KING FALLS). On the grid's own ladders and as a foe he fights at full from the first round. His lines (pyro.m2Down, m2Hurt, m3; fail.pyro, fail.pyroDown) are the seat's drafts. AMENDED 09-30b (his answers): phase 2 halves that fight's XP at its end (the party's own XP untouched: js/battle.js xpHalf); leaving the fight is a grid fight's thing only -- the 8-bit RUN takes him along, no harm, no foul; his fall's screen is his own line and a click to load; the road weighs him as 1.5.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'use a single attack with his regular mace in his main hand and then end turn, start using the mace of disruption and two attacks if he gets to half hp or a party member goes down ... If any character in the party leaves the fight, he goes into full lvl 12 combat until the fight is over, and player has to load from a save. If he ever goes down player has to load from a save.' 09-30b: 'every fight he guests with the party ... the party either loses half XP and continues, or it goes so bad they have to reload', 'he flips the mace of disruption to main hand if a party character has exited the fight'. The halving of each hero's XP (not the fight's) and the 8-bit RUN as leaving are the seat's readings, flagged for his word. Griz, 09-30b: "end of fight rewards /2 if pyro gets the disruptor out", "1 - that fight's xp", "2 - only the grid fights, no harm/foul on strategic withdrawals from random encounters", "3 - do 1.5, he'll likely tank a lot in that plate", "'the dwarf king fell in battle... well, obviously that didn't happen. (click to load)".

entries.what: The Ledger-Lamp in both games' fights and the field: the hooded lantern's law at bright 40 ft and dim 40 more (hood down: dim 5 ft), never spent, one hand, offered at the camp's A LIGHT IN HAND when the pack has it; it keeps its highway light, the seals and the roper's check (possession, lit or in the pack).
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'now should function like a lantern but better' -- '3 perfect' (the seat's proposal, handoff-2026-09-30-the-settling-and-pyro.md §2C). Built by a runner 09-30b.

entries.what: The wet's grid keeps the party till one of them walks off it (the south edge, or up the stair): nothing dead, asleep, fed or quiet ends it now; all of them down is still lost, and a hero down still brings the herd. Out with something dead behind them: a win, its XP at the 8-bit's Victory; else a run. They come up in the 8-bit on the square he walked off at (up the stair: into warrens_b as the stair takes them). The landlord fed from the bucket pays 500 XP, shared among those standing like a fight's, once, on the grid or at the rim (LOWER THE BUCKET): 'The landlord is fed, and lets the wet be. 500 XP for the bucket: each fighter standing gains {n} XP.' (text.json w.fedXp; js/events.js EV.wetOut, EV.fedXp; deep16/js/wet.js). A walk-out plays no game-over tune. 09-30e: the bucket pays 125% of the otyugh's XP (1800 -> 2250), shared among those standing (w.fedXp: 'The landlord is fed, and lets the wet be. Each fighter standing gains {n} XP.'). Stepping onto the south line or the stair asks LEAVE THE AREA? YES / NO ('Up the stair' / 'Out of the wet to the south': all of you go with <name>; a foe in reach gets its swing); NO stands there, LEAVE THE FIGHT still on the ring; an AI-run hero is not asked. No card on the way out (the leave card and the ending's head both gone). They land on the 8-bit square the one who walked off left by before the 8-bit ending runs; by the stair: on the stair, the Victory and the bucket's XP, then up.
entries.why: RULED 09-30d, Griz: 'Can we keep on the grid after everything is dead (or as yet unrevealed) (assuming only exit is to the south) and do have the xp award when the players finally leave it (500 xp if we aren't giving any for bucket the landlord)'. The seat's calls, his to overrule: the 500 shared among those standing (not 500 each); the stair counts as a way out beside the south edge; the landing square; the line's words; a save already fed pays at the next trip or at the rim. RULED 09-30e, Griz: '1 - let's make it 125% the xp they get if they kill it' -- '2 - stair exit is good. Do an auto-pop-up 'leave the area? yes/no' when they hit the stairs or the south line - there's a popup from after the card we removed or something - the wet, out the way they came in - let's remove that.' -- 'the exit square on return to 8-bit should match where the character that triggers the exit, exits. True for stair exit as well, though I think you'll have to land them on the stair, reward and then stair them up.' The prompt's words are the seat's.

entries.what: A lantern or the Ledger-Lamp, once lit, stays in the hand: map to map, through a rest, out of a fight on lit ground, both games and the seam. A torch still goes out at a rest or leaving the map. The field's EQUIP has a LIGHT row while a hero holds one (grey in a fight's EQUIP): (put it away) -- the lantern or the lamp back in the pack -- or, for a torch, (put it out), spent (js/scenes.js equipHero; js/events.js EV.torchOut(all)). 09-30e: a rest puts any light away (a lantern or the lamp back in the pack); only a map change leaves a lantern lit.
entries.why: RULED 09-30d, Griz: 'I don't mind torches working that way, but using a lantern should stick using. I equipped in silverton was off by first random in the warrens. Equipped in the warrens, didn't carry over as in Aurdin's hand when the Wet triggered.' The seat's calls: through a rest too; the EQUIP LIGHT row (a light that sticks needs a way out of the hand). RULED 09-30e, Griz: '3 - let the rest put the light away'.

entries.what: When the herd comes in (deep16/js/wet.js W.noticed): their Stealth, rolled once and never shown (d20 + the crawler's DEX, +1), against each standing hero's passive Perception. Noticed: the camera on the first crawler, held 75 frames, 'Your comrade's fall has attracted the herd.' Unnoticed: nothing said, they walk in out of the dark. The landlord's watching card: the camera on it, held 60 frames (was 12). The clackers' picture: a chip-synth chitin click ('clack', js/audio.js) each time a claw snaps shut, ten in its 150 frames. The edge's prompt line: '<name> goes, and the party goes too.'
entries.why: RULED 09-30f, Griz: 'can we do passive perception checks silently when the crawlers show up, then cam pause on them with 'your comrades fall has attracted the herd'' -- 'can we add clacker sound effects for when the appropriate telepathy image shows?' -- 'Need a little bit longer pause for the 'the landlord is looking at you' (gist) warnings cause the camera has to pan and such' -- 'misgendered viv, 'party goes too' instead of 'goes with him''. The seat's calls: the Stealth roll (the crawler sheet has no Stealth: its DEX), the holds (75, 60), the clack's sound.

entries.what: The Wet, 09-30g. The landlord's rim (the 8-bit's picture squares, (7-10, 8)) takes the party onto the grid on the square stepped on, the landlord asleep in its water and its bucket picture before anyone moves; fed or dead, the rim is only stone. Fed, the landlord sinks on its next turn ('The landlord settles, fed, and sinks out of sight under the fall.'), off the grid and out of the order, whoever stands at its edge, and it is never on the grid again. The bucket is one hero's: whoever took it up (the lead at the station, or whoever walks onto it on the grid); the others' ITEM greys it ('<name> carries it'); the carrier down, it rolls onto the nearest free ground for another to walk onto. A bound landlord with nobody in reach churns where it can be seen (the camera on it, its flinch, 60 frames). The herd comes in at full speed again. 09-30g (later): awake with no one standing it could get at this turn (keeping to its water), the landlord sinks and waits ('The landlord sinks under the fall, and waits.'): off the grid, out of the order at the next turn's start, its wounds kept, not killed; a hero who ends a move where it could reach rises it ('(it was waiting)'). The churn card stays for a bound creature outside the Wet.
entries.why: RULED 09-30g, Griz: 'the 8-bit landlord trigger should pull them into the grid area at the trigger spot' -- 'Landlord should settle and go underwater turn after bucket telepathy and be removed from having turns - even if people are at his pool edge (carrion bucket delivery kills trigger tile triggering)' -- 'Only the character that picked up the bucket should be able to use it as an item, and if they fall the bucket should become an item in a nearby available ground tile for a diff character to pickup' -- 'The otugyh is currently looking frozen after taking damage from vivian and he's still very alive' -- 'restore the crawlers get attracted in to full movement speed'. The seat's calls: the lines' words, the churn's camera and hold, a bucket left on the floor goes back to its station. RULED 09-30g, Griz: '1 - i like sink and wait, drag is good but too harsh for a reload likely coming anyway :)'. The seat's calls: the lines; the rise on a move that ends in its reach.

entries.what: The three deep-rate stations at the Wet ((15, 6), (35, 6), (24, 16)) work: in Edric's book (tallyMet), a milker takes the pens' shift on a harnessed crawler nobody settled -- the scene's unrest whole from the first draw, the gold narrowed as for DC 15 (the milker's skill counted 3 less), three silver the sealed thimble. A whip rouses it, the touch held or not: the shift ends ('IT TEARS LOOSE'), the thimbles so far paid, and the fight is on the Wet's grid, the crawler loose at its cradle and the milker on the square the party worked it from (poisoned and paralyzed if the touch took). Lines: w.deepNoBook, w.deepAsk, w.deepPaid, w.deepRoused, w.touchedDeep, w.cradle.enterDeep, w.cradle.twitchDeep, w.cradle.roused, w.cradle.paidDeep.
entries.why: RULED 09-30g, Griz: 'the 8-bit crawler harnesses should instantiate the crawler milking mini-game if they've unlocked it, with the higher payout and un-settled crawlers in the harnesses' -- '1 - is a dice roll even happening - if player error makes a whip, start your combat that's great' -- '2 - being in the book is enough'. The numbers are the module's (crawler-warrens-DM.md section 3: the deep rate three silver a thimble, DC 15 at the wet, a natural 1 rouses the animal). The seat's calls: un-settled as the whole unrest, DC 15 as skill -3 on the band, a held whip rousing it too, the lines.

entries.what: Hideous Laughter's hyena, 09-30h (DEEP16). A hyena (any unit on a hyena_ sheet: grimoire.js M.hyena) is not too simple to find it funny, its INT 2 notwithstanding: the spell lands on it as on anyone (the class AI weighs it as a target too). While it laughs it rolls on the floor: the rofl row of hyena_p2, cut from Griz's second hyena sheet (deep16/_src/hyena_grok_2.webp, its ROFL row's figures 2-7, played there and back), in place of whatever it would be drawing. The spell landing on one plays 'cackle' (js/audio.js: eleven quick climbing hee-hees); each turn it starts still laughing plays 'cackle2' (seven slower, running down, and a whoop) and the card 'The Hyena rolls in the dirt, cackling.' Also: a laughing creature no longer gets up off the floor at its turn's start (rules.js: SRD 5.1 'unable to stand up for the duration'). Testing rooms: ?fxgallery&spell=hideouslaughter&foe=hyena; ?npc=hyena,hyena,hyena&vs=bard&lvl=3 (the class floor takes a bestiary creature's name now). SUPERSEDED-BY: #aurdin-joke-egg (10-02): a hyena is too simple to find the spell funny again (SRD 5.1, INT 4 or less); its rofl row, its card and both cackles stay, for the hyenas caught by Aurdin's joke.
entries.why: RULED 09-30, Griz: 'I'd like to add an Easter Egg for Casting Hideous Laughter that uses this 'rolling on the floor laughing' art on the model (except frame one, where they gave it 2 heads)'; then 'despite the SRD, for this easer egg have the spell function on them - and them playing the animation. Try approximate a hyena laughter sound effect for when it lands and a slight different one for when it starts its turn under the effects'. The card's line and both cackles are the seat's draft. Then 10-02, Griz: 'since you'll be messing with hideous laughter anyway, I want you to change the easter egg. The current easter egg is 'you can cast hideous laughter on hyenas''.

entries.what: The level-three start, 09-30h (the 8-bit: ?lvl3 on the URL, js/scenes.js DS.levelThree): pick a lead; all four at level 3 at its XP to the point, on Fountain Street (silverton 29,8), the journal's Company and Winters' Errands done (both errands: the one renown they pay is what lets Lymen join) and nothing else; the purse as those jobs leave it (10 to start, 12 and 20 from Winters, the hires' fees out, Barley's five back from his bout) with Brennan's potion and Vivian's candle; Vivian's archetype asks at once.
entries.why: Griz, 09-30: 'if you could make a new on where everyone just hit lvl 3 and only the silverton paper delivery and collect the party missions are done' (the seat read 'the silverton paper delivery' as the journal's Winters' Errands: 'Ambrose Winters has papers that need carrying').

entries.what: The clacker on the grid, 10-01 (deep16/data/foes.js clacker; Griz's sheet, tools/clacker-sheet.py): the realm's hook horror, the colony crowning the crook (wiki the-warrens.md, the clacker cavern), never named in the game. Not an SRD creature, so the block is the seat's own from SRD pieces: Large monstrosity, CR 3, AC 15 (a hide like cobbles), 68 HP, speed 30, two Hooks +6 (1d10+4 piercing, reach 10), blindsight 60 by echo, STR 18 DEX 10 CON 14 INT 6 WIS 12 CHA 6, passive Perception 13. At the start of each of its turns it strikes its hooks together (the sheet's CLACK row, a clack on each strike): the clacking that is their speech. Fights only where asked for (?npc=clacker): no story fight has one yet. Its climb is not read. 10-01, later: the sheet is Griz's two Grok sheets now (clacker_p2; the GPT one retired). RULED: no clacker fight in the crook -- the colony was never fleshed out because the party would be too low for it, and he expects the clackers to figure in the Deepholm expansion.
entries.why: Griz, 10-01: 'I had a problem with the 'later' on the clacker and there's a 16 bit animation sheet available for review' (he generated the art list's Q2 head the same night). The hook horror's own block is not SRD, so a block of our own stands in (the no-stubs law: the seat drafts, the draft stands till he rules). Griz, 10-01, on 'should clackers get a real fight in the crook': 'no, and it wasn't fleshed out because it was the players would be too low level for a colony, this has changed from a tabletop truth to a game obvious falsity. I'm assuming clackers will plot at least some of the deepholm expansion.'

entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz: 'There should be someone who is already a shop in silverton that would reasonably sell the ink' -- the seat's pick of the shop

entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz: 'if not add dwarven provisioner (probably lamp 2) that sells [familiar components]. Lower price to 50 sp.' -- the name and the stock the seat's draft

entries.what: Ink for Katarina: Barley at her fire before the wagon's night ('You're with the Dominion'); she asks a bottle of ink for her vision; given, she tells it (Aurdin laughing) and gives the Sheet: Hideous Laughter -- the first unjournaled quest (EV.UNJOURNALED); her lines but Griz's two the seat's draft
entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz (verbatim in content/text.json kat.dominion, kat.ink)

RE-TAGGED 10-09 (fold: game): the branch's economy, drafting or map edge, not a realm fact (Griz 10-09: 'Edited to match is the wrong move'; the fold catches the places and people that are new).
