entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz: 'try to pick a good spell for one NPC in both the warrens (at the surface) and Galleries' -- the seat's pick (Edric the only reader at the mouth; Grease for the rails and the slick tunnels); his lines the seat's draft

entries.what: Corwen Dace as a guest (heroes.json dace: Wizard 1 by the 09-22 canon sheet, HP 7, AC 15 with mage armor, light / mage armor / sleep): asked, the party may take him down; vital -- if he falls the fight is lost (both games); the cloaker hunts him; the cloaker dead with him there, he writes up its Phantasms as the Sheet: Mirror Image and goes home
entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz: 'gotta be guest the kid to the cloaker cavern to get the spell sheet to learn it from - game over if the kid falls, cloaker focuses on kid if they bring him to that fight' -- the kid is Dace (CANON 09-22: 'Always tries to talk people into taking him into the deep gallery'); 44 by the wiki; the spell and his lines the seat's

entries.what: Katarina's vision names the spotted dogs of the tribe that laughs: the hint that sends Hideous Laughter at a hyena (the egg, #hyena-laughter-egg) 10-02: the egg is Aurdin's joke now (#aurdin-joke-egg); the vision says 'the tribe that laughs and its spotted dogs, laughing with him': the gnolls the egg asks for, and the dogs that join in.
entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz: 'Kat and the Gnoll laughter that leads to the easter egg'

entries.what: After the cloaker is dead, Dace asks again; taken down, he gives the party their pick in the deep gallery -- the Cloak of Displacement off his back ('my grandfather's', the house's original gatherer) or the Sheet: Mirror Image; hunted by the living cloaker and won through, the sheet only and he keeps the cloak; Old Wynn, asked, sends him home ('maybe we'll take you down later')
entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz: 'Let the party talk to the Grandad to back out of the escort' / 'put the cloak of displacement on him and let them choose between it and spell as reward if they escort him after, only spell if they somehow succeed with the cloaker hunting him' -- Wynn as 'the Grandad' the seat's reading (71 to Dace's 44 by the wiki: the house's elder, no grandfather of his); the lines the seat's draft

entries.what: Arrows (a bow's ammunition now: the shortbow and longbow take them) and crossbow bolts, a silver each, bought by the count, at Marko Thorne's Provisioner in Silverton and Gudrun Tallowmark's Lamp Stores; the Lamp Stores also sell a shortbow and a light crossbow
entries.why: RULED 10-01c, Griz: 'check stores and new dwarf provisioner at lamp two for bow and arrow sales' -- found: only Kessler sold a bow, no one sold bolts, and arrows did not exist; the SRD's ammunition ('match SRD expectations when possible'); the stock the seat's pick

entries.what: DEEP16: a natural 1 on an attack at a darkmantle riding one of ours (the attacker's side, or the attacker itself) lands on the one it rides instead -- the attack's damage, no critical, no riders (battle.js attack).
entries.why: RULED 10-01, Griz: 'Players should be able to target it ... if SRD says nothing about hurting ally, only hurt ally on natural 1 (ignoring bonuses)'. The SRD's Darkmantle says nothing about striking the creature it is attached to.

entries.what: DEEP16: a darkmantle that comes off the one it rode (the grip broken, pulled off, let go, either of them down) drops to the nearest open square beside that one (battle.js dismount). Pulled off by a friend: the open square nearest the puller and the one it rode together, and of those the one nearer the puller. The one it rides grown past Medium after it got on (Enlarge): thrown off, as if pulled off, to the nearest open square. On the head only while that one is Medium or smaller (an Enlarged Medium is Large).
entries.why: Griz 10-01: 'Doesn't seem clear from the SRD, but I think mechanics wise we might be best moving it off his square when he breaks free. He normally couldn't occupy the same square.' The SRD names no square. RULED 10-01, Griz: "pull off should land 'nearest available square to puller and victim' - (closer to Ly in this instance)". RULED 10-01, Griz: "only when he's Medium or smaller"; then, of it sliding to the shoulder: "treat if 'victim enlarge' = pull it off to nearby square".

entries.what: DEEP16: the roper's Reel (after its four tendril attacks, before the bite) pulls each creature it holds up to 25 ft a square at a time along the line to its nearest square -- the straight step, else a side step that still closes -- through the dragged one's friends' squares but not its foes', landing on the last square on the way it can stand in; where the line ends on a taken square beside the roper (a friend down there), the open square beside it nearest, if the 25 ft reaches it (js/ai.js reel).
entries.why: RULED 10-01e, Griz: 'yes, we've often been too lenient, 4 please' (the SRD's four tendrils and Reel, for two tendrils that each dragged its one all the way in). The SRD says 'straight toward it' and names no square where the way is blocked; passing through friends is the SRD's movement rule; the fallback square is the seat's call, after the bench's fights stalled on a fallen friend in the line.

entries.what: The roper's tendril is struck at from wherever the one it holds could be struck from: beside that one with a blade, or a shot at its square (DEEP16, 10-02: js/battle.js tendrilOn, strikeTendril). The weapon's own dice; no Sneak Attack, smite or mark on it, those being for a creature. A natural 1 lands on the one it holds, as at a darkmantle on a friend's head.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 says each tendril can be attacked (AC 20, 10 HP) and names no square for it; the tendril runs from the roper to the one it holds, and the game needs one place to click. A tendril holding no one is coiled about its foot and cannot be struck (the seat's call).

entries.what: A roper's tendril cut or broken comes back one a turn, as its action, when it has no one held and no one in reach of what it has left (js/ai.js brute, 10-02). Till then it is one tendril short, and with none to throw its reach is the bite's and it walks in. AMENDED 10-02 on his word ("1 - SRD is free but then never walks, correct?" / "go with SRD for combat"): every tendril cut or broken is back at its next turn, free (js/rules.js startTurn); the extruding as its action is gone. It walks in only when nothing it has can hold anyone: none to throw, every tendril holding, or no one in its reach it can hold (Freedom of Movement; js/ai.js usableOn, reachOf).
entries.why: SRD 5.1: 'Destroying a tendril deals no damage to the roper, which can extrude a replacement tendril on its next turn' -- one, and the seat reads the extruding as what the turn does. Griz's test, 10-02: 'have the party keep their distance and kill all the tendrils, then see if it walks to bite' -- with all of them back at once, or one back free at the start of every turn, it never would. RULED: the SRD for combat. A tendril holding no one is not struck and not targeted (RULED 10-02: "perfect, i assume also not targeted").

entries.what: DEEP16's Ready action has one trigger: the first foe that comes within reach of the readied weapon, or into sight and range for a bow, a thrown weapon or a readied attack spell (js/battle.js exec 'ready', readyHook, 10-02). The readied action is a single weapon attack, or an attack-shaped spell (an attack roll, rays, darts) cast now and held under concentration, its slot spent; a readied move is not built. 10-02 later, SUPERSEDED in part on Griz's word ("what if we use the menu you used to give 2 or 3 trigger conditions, then they navigate the wheel to what they're readying - yes closer to SRD"; "go with 1&2 - let's make 3 'an ally goes down' for readied healers. foe casts a spell you can see, if you mean foe you can see casts a spell"; "or were you letting them pick target when the trigger went off, that's probably better"): four triggers now -- a foe within reach (into sight for a bow or a spell), a foe's attack at one of us in sight (you too), one of us down (heard: no sight asked), a foe in sight casting a spell (told after it finishes: not Counterspell) -- picked from a numbered menu, then the wheel holds only what can be readied (the weapon or the other one, any spell that takes an action, by level, the tiers greyed where there is no slot, or a move up to the speed). Sprung, a player's hero aims it then (js/ui.js req.aim: the cursor on the one that set it off, X or the right button holds it and the ready waits); the AI's goes where the trigger points (battle.js readyAuto). 10-05: trigger 1 for a bow or a spell springs when a foe comes into sight OR one already in sight moves (a climb up a face, a step part way up a rope too); a hand that holds is not asked again for the same foe's same move, and the readied action stays for the next trigger till the start of the readier's turn.
entries.why: SRD 5.1's Ready takes any perceivable circumstance and any action; the grid can ask one question and answer it from what it sees -- a burrower up out of the ground, a phase spider out of the Ethereal, one walking up, the invisible seen. The handoff of 10-01e asked for this one ('when a foe comes up in my reach'). The seat's calls inside his: 'one of us' counts the readier; 'one of us goes down' is told after the blow, the spell or the turn that did it; a readied self-spell asks CAST or HOLD instead of an aim; the AI still readies only against what is under the ground or out of the world, on the first trigger. Griz, 10-05: "just OR if there's already in sight - there's times when players ready to let an ally go first - is it such that a refused 'trigger' waits for the next fire?" (Aurdin's readied Scorching Ray let the male giant climb in plain view twice). Asked once a move is the seat's.

entries.what: The bulette bites and goes under again in the same turn when it has 5 ft of its move left, leaving the reach of those beside it as any creature does -- their opportunity attacks first -- and digs on as far from them as the rest of its move goes (js/ai.js diveAfter, 10-02). The xorn stays up and fights. RULED 10-02 (Griz: "keep that, it's what people used to one will want anyway"): it dives after any blow it swung, hit or miss, never after a turn it struck at no one (js/ai.js diveAfter, turn.attacked).
entries.why: Griz, 10-01d: 'If the mechanics allow it and a smart player or AI would do it, we'll allow it.' The seat's call of 10-01d kept it up through the party's turns because nothing could answer it; Ready answers it now. The xorn, which resists plain steel and claws three times, has no cause to run (the seat's call).

entries.what: Aurdin's joke, 10-02 (DEEP16; the easter egg in place of #hyena-laughter-egg). Only in a fight the 8-bit game opened, only with a gnoll standing (a glory-seeker counts: the Snoot's young blood), only when Ink for Katarina is done (flag katVision: the sheet given), Hideous Laughter is in Aurdin's book and among the day's spells he brought: his own square is a target of it too (grimoire.js M.jokeReady, magic.js selfToo). Cast on himself: he goes down laughing (prone, incapacitated; the slot spent; what he concentrated on lets go); every hyena that hears it (any side; not one asleep, held, stunned or in the Ethereal) laughs till the end of its next turn, and every gnoll for two full rounds, from his turn to his turn two rounds on (M.jokeClock), with no save, not even when hurt; their reactions spent. Then his own fit passes (he stays prone), and the fight holds for the egg: a red pixel egg in the palette's reds, dithered, a white shine and a sweeping glint, sparks, popping in and bobbing, the line 'Guess I'm the Joke, Now' under it at twice size, about four seconds (E or a click after one goes on: the cutscene beat's own rule). Sounds: guffaw (his), gnollaugh (theirs), cackle (the hyenas), rimshot as the egg comes up, shine. The seat's calls: the glory-seeker as a gnoll; any side; who hears; the clock; prone after; the cards' lines ('Aurdin cracks up at his own joke, and goes down laughing.', 'The gnolls know that laugh. They go down howling with it'), the sounds and the egg's look are drafts. 10-02b: the gnolls' fit on their sheet's own LAUGH row, cut from Griz's gnoll sheet 2 (deep16/_src/gnoll_grok_2.webp, tools/gnoll-sheet.py): the yawn, sit/rest 2, 1, 3, 8, 3, fall/get-up 1, 2, 4, 2, then fall 5 / sit 8 / fall 5 / sit 8 over and over while it laughs (one already on the ground starts there); the laugh fires on the yawn, the fall's 4 and the first 8 of each chain (grimoire.js M.LAUGH, M.laughTick), one gnoll's at a time, so a pack laughs as one: at 0, 2.0 s and 3.0 s, then every 1.6 s; held still under the egg. Their PRONE row: Fall / Get Up 8, 7, 6, 5 (S.proneRow plays it forward to go down and back to get up). The seat's calls: each beat's hold, the quiet between laughs (the sound's own 0.83 s and a hair), a pack staggered by its place in the line-up, the fit held under the egg, the prone row's four frames. 10-02c: a cutscene first, as the darkness's: Aurdin waist up, shaking with it ('AURDIN CRACKS UP AT HIS OWN JOKE.', his guffaw); the camera tilting down to him on the floor ('AND GOES DOWN LAUGHING.', a little 'hehehe' once); the hyena's still face (his hehehe again); a gnoll's face pushed in on, then its yawn with its laugh ('THE GNOLLS KNOW THAT LAUGH.'), the camera pulling back to the fight -- then the effects as before. He picks himself up as that turn ends ('Aurdin picks himself up off the floor, still wheezing.'). Once the egg has come up, never again in that save (flag eggJoke). The gnolls' chain laughs on every other chain. Their prone: fall/get-up 1, 2 (over onto the back), and up by the sheet's own 3 to 8 (a `getup` row). The seat's calls: the captions, the hehehe, the framings and beat lengths.
entries.why: RULED 10-02, Griz: 'If and only if Gnolls are present in 16bit fight (main game only), and aurdin has done the silent quest and received and learned and selected it for the fight - he can cast hideous laughter on himself, in which case he goes into hideous laughter. As a reaction, any hyenas go into hideous laughter until the end of their next turn (not end of reaction) and any gnolls go into hideous laughter for 2 full rounds without save. after their reactions have played, hideous laughter on aurdin expires - battle pauses and big red shiny easter egg on screen: "Guess I'm the Joke, Now" for a few seconds then resume' (the silent quest read as the unjournaled one, EV.UNJOURNALED) 10-02b, Griz: 'assuming their standing I'd play 'yawn' (idle variation 6) when the laugh sound fires, then like sit/rest 2, 1, 3, 8 .. 3 to fall/getup 1, 2, 4, 2,  - 5, sit/rest 8, fall/getup 5, sit/rest 8'; 'the 4 in 1, 2, 4, 2 is great, and on the first 8 in the 5sit/8rest/5sit/8rest chain'. 10-02c, Griz: 'Aurdin gets to get up after he ends the turn he cast the spell, and him being able to cast it on himself again should be disabled when the egg appears (1 per customer)'; 'Like those cut scenes, with Aurdin waist up and laugh, the cam down to him down with the laugh and a give him a little hehehe that plays once showing him - then zoom on idol face living gnoll, then idle 6 with the sound (with the text overlaying as appropriate) then zoomed back out and the effects we currently have start'; 'oh, hehehe from aurdin again on the still face of the hyena'; '1 every other chain'; '2 yes'.

entries.what: The darkness's red egg, 10-02 (DEEP16): after the cloaker's 'Magic Missile at the darkness' cutscene and its moan, the red egg comes up with the line 'Don't Poke the Darkness' (the seat's draft), once a save (grimoire.js M.egg, flag eggDarkness, back to the 8-bit save by the seam; js/events.js EV.EGGS lists it). RULED the same day: the egg purple (the palette's violets, a violet glow and shadow) and its line 'Stare Into the Void Long Enough' (his words, set in the joke egg's case) in place of the draft.
entries.why: 10-02, Griz: the cloaker's 'attacking the darkness' easter egg 'still needs it's easter egg - which I'm hoping we're tracking somewhere in their save files' Then 10-02, Griz: 'Make the egg purple and call it "stare into the void long enough"'.

entries.what: DEEP16's Counterspell (10-02, Griz: "Yeah, that's an important one to have in there"): asked as a spell is released (js/magic.js M.cast, js/grimoire.js M.counterAsk) of each foe of the caster who knows it, has a 3rd-or-higher slot and its reaction, and sees the caster within 60 ft; a player's hero picks the slot or lets it go, the AI counters any levelled spell but a friend's blessing on a friend, with the lowest slot that makes it fail outright, else its highest. Not asked: a readied spell's release, a spell used again, a cantrip by the AI; a Counterspell is not itself countered. On the generic wizard's, sorcerer's and warlock's 3rd-level lists (js/classes.js), last. Dispel Magic takes an empty square in the area of a spell (Griz: "I like 'spell effect squares without people' as valid dispel targets for that spell"): the spell the Globe's stamp says laid it (castId) ends by Dispel's own rule; two on one square, the player's caster is asked which.
entries.why: SRD 5.1's Counterspell and Dispel Magic ("Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range"); the AI's choice, the order in the lists and the which-of-two prompt are the seat's. A creature's own power is no spell (RULED 10-02, Griz: "no to creature abilities"): the darkmantle's aura has no castId and is not a target.

entries.what: The seat's and the runners' calls inside the SRD pass of 10-02 (Griz: "SRD as we can, yes - with noted exceptions"; "yes to 1-7 and the smaller ones"): Dispel Magic on a creature ends whole (for all a spell holds) Banishment, Haste, Polymorph, Enlarge/Reduce, Animal Shapes, Mislead, Etherealness, Gaseous Form and the Dominates, whose ending does more than lift what is on the one; a readied Dash is the MOVE (a reaction's move up to the speed), so DASH is not on the Ready wheel; the bulette's leap pushes no one (it lands beside its mark, so no one is in its space); the spy's Cunning Action is the goblin's Nimble Escape for now (Disengage and a step back; Dash and Hide not read); Sleep's minute runs on its caster's turns; a bound monster weighs its attacks from the squares it can stand on.
entries.why: Where the SRD leaves the grid a choice, or the grid cannot yet do the whole of a rule: the exceptions are named so they can be found and finished.

entries.what: The Pocket DM (alpha), deep16/?pocket (10-02, Griz: "In the style of 'the ladder' create a user friendly interface that apparently does everything through the power of a URL (or build something new actually called the pocket DM (alpha)"): a scene of the grid over Solskaft's clan hall -- the dais and the empty high seat, the oath-stone with its band of gold, the Sunshaft's noon down onto it -- drawn at 16-bit for the first time (his pick: "the oathstone under the skylight of the dwarf edifice place in silverton as the backdrop"; wiki/solskaft.md, content/maps/solskaft.json beam). A party of one to six from the roster (the four, the guests, the named, Pyro locked till the trial) or of the player's own making (race, class, scores from ten with arrows 3 to 18 -- "sort of hoping people rebuild their table characters" -- level to 8, the class's kit, the class's built spells, a name; a `~` word carries the whole sheet), a map (the dark ones said so), a CR dial that rolls the bestiary to the sum (Willem and Amara in the pot when not in the party, the story's other named out: "throw in willem and amara if they aren't in the player's party (exclude if they are) - exclude the rest"), the DMG's reading beside. Every fight it makes is a ?npc= URL. The seat's: the pot leaves out CR 0 and a water-bound thing off the water; the dial opens where the party reads HARD; a made character has a max hit die a level as the heroes do, and its ASIs come with the level; Pyro on the party side is run by his own script.
entries.why: his words 10-02; a player-facing door to the class floor, the test-runs page being the engineer's
entries.src: deep16/js/pocket.js; deep16/js/classes.js NPC.spec/decode/code/heroUnit; deep16/README.md 'The Pocket DM (alpha)'

entries.what: The Pocket DM's ladder (10-02): four rungs from the dial's table, each about a third again the last in CR on a map drawn fresh; SHORT REST FOR THE WICKED between -- the fallen up at 1 HP first ("SRD + free rez for the fallen before the short rest applies is good"), then hit dice till whole or out (one a level a run), the short-rest features and a warlock's slots back, a wizard's Arcane Recovery once a run; LONG REST FOR THE TRIAL after the fourth win, then the trial, double deadly (the smallest table whose adjusted XP is twice the party's deadly threshold), which unlocks Pyro on the roster ("give them a 'long rest for the trial' after the fourth win and then do your double deadly"). On every win one character drawn at random (never Pyro) finds a magic item the class may wear and that betters what it has -- the plus-ones; the +2s, Flame Tongue, the Door-Shield and the dwarven plate from the third rung ("pick a random character on victory and give magic item appropriate to class"). A loss: quit, retry or reroll the rung, the party as it went in ("restored to what they went in with before they died"). The fights kept with notes, saved as a file, mailed, or carried to his Discord ("also put my discord link"). The seat's: the 1.3 step; the loot by kind in hand and weight worn; the trial's long rest whole.
entries.why: his answers 10-02 to the seat's ten questions
entries.src: deep16/js/pocket.js (startRun, nextRung, setTrial, shortRest, loot); deep16/README.md

entries.what: The Keeper of the Flooded Stair, ours and not the SRD's Water Weird: above the water a Slam (DC 15 STR or prone) and, each round as a bonus action, the Wave up the stair (STR DC 13 or prone) that bounces off the front wall and sweeps the prone 10 ft toward the deep, where they stand up free; one washed onto a deep square is restrained and the Keeper pours into the water around it (AC 10; its bonus action there, Active Suffocation); drowning is 1d6 less CON (at least 1) at the start of the victim's turn, twice after an Active Suffocation, and a blow to the Keeper in the water is a CON concentration check (DC 10 or half) whose failure frees the victim of the hold but not of the drowning; the Ice Wall, 3 uses, readied and sprung by a hero moving toward the exit (the SRD's Wall of Ice body: AC 12, 30 HP a 10-ft section) and a fire spell destroys a section at once; a cold area spell freezes the water (1d4 cold to the caster's friends in it, ice anchors against the backwash and is not the deep). Not the SRD's: all of it but the wall's body and the concentration DC. 100 HP on the bench's word (the four kill 58 in 3 rounds). 10-28 (Griz, "Take the leans", the difficulty lane §3.6, after his "too easy" at level 3): in the water his AC is 13, his own (K.CFG.deepAC, was 10), and his walk deeper -- the lure's and the opener's end -- takes no way that leaves a hero's reach (K.CFG.lureSafe), so it draws no opportunity attack.
entries.why: Griz 10-02/10-03 (handoff-2026-10-02-the-keeper.md; his answers: 'DC 15 STR save - using himself is more forceful than the wave', 'the roll twice, each floored at 1', row 11, 'ready the wall with a trigger of party member moves toward exit', '10 ft per wave', 'any water square next to the victim')
entries.src: deep16/js/keeper.js; deep16/data/foes.js keeper; deep16/data/maps.js floodstair (deeps, lane, wallRow); dev/keeper-probe.py

entries.what: The Spy's Cunning Action (SRD 5.1: a bonus action to Dash, Disengage or Hide) is chosen by the grid so: pressed (hurt under half with a foe beside it, or two beside it under three quarters) it Disengages, steps to the square farthest from the party with a clear crossbow line and no one beside it, and shoots; with no one in reach by the walk but one in reach by walk and Dash it Dashes to close; running for the stair it Dashes again, or Disengages first if a hero beside it still has a reaction; it Hides after its turn only where no foe sees it clearly (the same seenBy question as the Hide action). Stealth +6 on its sheet.
entries.why: The SRD gives the Spy the bonus action and no policy; the class NPC rogue's choices (js/features.js, js/tactics.js) copied for a stat block. Thresholds are the seat's (10-02 cloud seat).

entries.what: A foe with two ranged weapons and no ranged Multiattack (the gnoll's longbow and thrown spear) uses the likelier, bigger blow at the lowest AC it sees, a thrown weapon past its normal range at disadvantage: the spear within 20 ft, the bow beyond. `rangedMulti` on a sheet is its ranged Multiattack (the Bandit Captain's two thrown daggers); the melee `multi` stays the melee routine.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 gives the gnoll Spear (melee or 20/60) and Longbow, the Captain 'two ranged attacks with its daggers'; the grid's volley fired the first ranged attack once. Thrown weapons are not spent (as the javelins already are not).

entries.what: The Bandit Captain's Parry (+2 AC against one melee attack that would hit, a reaction, it must see the attacker and wield a melee weapon) is taken whenever the +2 turns the blow; never against a natural 20, a ranged attack or a spell that is not touch.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Bandit Captain: Parry. The take-it-when-it-turns-the-blow policy is the same as the class NPC's Shield (js/battle.js attack).

entries.what: Duergar Resilience (advantage on saves against spells) holds for the saves a spell already running asks of a duergar (Spirit Guardians at its turn's start, a zone's, a web's, a wall's, the charm's on a hurt): while magic.js startTurn/endTurn and the stepInto/onHurt/confusedTurn/danceAsk chains resolve on it, B.spellRun names it. A concentration save is not against a spell.
entries.why: RU.save read B.castLevel only during the cast; SRD 5.1 says 'saving throws against ... spells'. A monster-born ground with no spell behind it, resolved in the same chains, would get it too (none exists on a duergar's turn now).

entries.what: The dragonborn and the tiefling on the grid: each class figure (npc<class>_p0) with the race laid over it, npc<class>_dragonborn_p0 and npc<class>_tiefling_p0, the class's kit, weapon and attack kept (tools/lpc-compose.py RACE_LOOKS). The dragonborn is gold (LPC skin all.lpcr.amber: the gold dragon's, fire, a 15-ft cone), with the lizard head of the class figure's sex, no hair, the dragon ears and a lizard tail, and no wings. The tiefling is garnet-skinned (all.lpcr.garnet) and keeps the class's human head and hair (the druid takes the human female head for Higertha's orc one); curled bone-yellow horns are drawn over a hood or a hat, and a lizard tail matches the skin. The Pocket DM and the camp draw a made character of either race with these (deep16/js/classes.js classLook); every other race keeps the class figure.
entries.why: Griz 10-03: 'prolly should check if there's dragonborn available through the method we've used for the ones we got (free LPC or something?)', then '1 per class, 2 cloud'; 'generic kits per class'. The SRD 5.1 describes neither race's looks; the colours and the horns are the cloud seat's picks, open to his ruling (cloud-notes/deep16-race-figures-notes.md).

entries.what: DEEP16 fetches a sprite sheet only when a scene asks for it, not all 135 before the first screen (deep16/js/sprites.js S.ensure, S.gate). A fight's first frame waits for the figures on the field. The creatures it may bring on later (its casters' summons and Polymorph's beasts, a druid's wild shapes, the familiars, Guardian of Faith's guard, a split ooze's half) are fetched in the background. While a scene waits, it shows the ladder's dark and, after a fifth of a second, the 8-bit game's window reading THE FIGURES ARE COMING, with a pip for each figure that lights as it lands. After 20 s the scene goes on, and its figures appear as they land. A sheet that fails to load is drawn as the grey capsule. The camp fetches its fight's foes in the background, and the Pocket DM fetches the table's foes while it is set. RULED 10-03: the words and the pips kept; a caster's summon and Polymorph pools fetched in the background as built; and (follow-up) the ladder list fetches the chosen rung's figures in the background once it has been chosen a third of a second, so the camp opens without the beat, while a rung the mouse only runs over fetches nothing (deep16/js/ladder.js Ladder.prototype.rungSheets).
entries.why: Griz 10-03, to 'The lazy load as a later cloud job?': '4 yes'. The cloud seat's calls: the beat's words and look, the split between figures to wait for and figures fetched in the background, the 20-second cap, and the fifth-of-a-second delay before the beat shows. All are open to his ruling (cloud-notes/lazy-sheets-notes.md). Griz 10-03, to the lazy seat's four questions: 'your words' (the beat's words and pips); 'prefetch; nothing waits on it' (the summon pools); 'yes' (the ladder list prefetches the chosen rung); 'later' (shrinking the scripts). The third of a second is the seat's call.

entries.what: The 8-bit battle's reaction window (js/battle.js, 10-03): one reaction a unit a round, back at the start of its turn; two triggers and no squares -- a hit about to land (the roll known, the damage not) and a creature you can see casting a spell; no opportunity attacks (no movement). The player's hero is asked by a menu with a way to decline (SHIELD? CAST SHIELD / LET IT LAND; HELLISH REBUKE? REBUKE / LET IT GO; COUNTERSPELL? COUNTER / LET IT GO; UNCANNY DODGE? DODGE IT / TAKE IT, the blow's number shown), and B lets it go. Shield is offered only when it turns the blow (a hit by less than 5; never a natural 20) and is off the MAGIC list, as are Hellish Rebuke and Counterspell (`reaction` on the record). A guest or AI-run hero decides as the grid's AI does: Shield whenever it turns the hit, Hellish Rebuke always, Counterspell at any levelled spell, Uncanny Dodge at 6 damage or more. A foe with `reactions: { parry: N }` on its sheet (the Bandit Captain, Hask) parries one melee hit that would land by less than N, if it can see the attacker and is not helpless. Hellish Rebuke is not offered under the roost (fire wakes the roof). A hit on a concentrating caster asks CON (DC 10 or half the damage) after the blow's own rider; the rebuke comes after both. RULED 10-03 (Griz's answers to the seven questions): Hellish Rebuke IS offered under the roost, with ROOST on the item, and taken there it is spent, no fire lands and the roof wakes, as a fire spell or the oil cast there ("offered; it is fire, and the roost's law is the player's choice with the consequence"); a guest never takes it there. The dodge's shown number stays ("keep; the hit is known before the halving in the SRD"); the 'begins to cast' card stays as built; a recast's card stays ("keep"); the Bandit Captain's blade is assumed in hand ("fine; the SRD requires it"); a wizard's default day holds Shield next after Mage Armor (R.prepDefault, "yes").
entries.why: SRD 5.1 reactions, Shield, Hellish Rebuke, Counterspell, Uncanny Dodge, Parry. RULED 10-03, Griz: "Simple because of movement, but they should still get their reactions is my first impression"; "1 yes, 2 yes" (the window and concentration). The AI's choices are the grid's (deep16/js/battle.js, grimoire.js, features.js, traits.js; invented.json parry-taken-by-the-ai). The 8-bit's Uncanny Dodge was automatic (the first hit a round halved, no reaction spent): made the reaction it is. The roost call and the dodge's shown number are the seat's: cloud-notes/8bit-reactions-notes.md.

entries.what: A foe's special in content/monsters.json that is a spell on its SRD sheet carries `spell: "<record id>"` (the spell-weaver's bolt storm and the naga's bolt: lightningbolt; their and Torvald's hold: holdperson; Torvald's guardians: spiritguardians and his sanctuary: sanctuary; the drow's, the captain's and the weaver's darkness: darkness), so the 8-bit's Counterspell sees it cast and a Magic Missile special would be turned by Shield. The darkmantle's darkness is its aura, not the spell, and stays untagged; Amara's Eldritch Blast is an attack on her sheet, not a special. A countered special is spent (its recharge or its once) and nothing happens. 10-03: the Drow Spell-Weaver casts Magic Missile too (`darts`: three darts at one hero, 3d4+3 force, no save, cast as often as the dice let it), the first 8-bit foe a hero's Shield turns (RULED, Griz: "yes; the SRD's mage casts it").
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Counterspell wants a spell being cast; the 8-bit's foes cast their sheets' specials, not records (spells-two-books.md §2a.7), so the sheet says which specials are spells. The seat's call, 10-03.

entries.what: RULED 10-03 (the desk, Griz's playtests): in play=keeper the script ends the Keeper's turn and swirls at once -- no choosing -- when the Wave's backwash pushes someone all the way to the back (onto the deep: the first two flooded steps from the sealed-door end, along 1 and 2); the swirl is the Keeper's action out of the Wave's own result, and the hero is held (restrained, drowning) as if he had swirled it by hand. Not to be changed.
entries.why: Griz played the Keeper and approved it: the Wave that washes a hero to the back is the swirl; the human does not get to decline or spend the turn elsewhere.
entries.src: deep16/js/keeper.js sweep/wave (K.flood on a sweep into the deep), js/keeperplay.js; dev/keeper-probe.js

entries.what: The Keeper's deep (where a swept hero is washed in and where the swirl may take a hero) is the first two flooded steps from the sealed-door end, along 1 and 2 (CFG.deepDepth 2; &deep=1 the old: only the last step). Default on (Griz 10-03: 'swirl heroes on the SECOND step as well'); swirlAny still takes any hero in the water or in reach.
entries.why: Griz 10-03 via the desk.
entries.src: deep16/data/maps.js floodstair geo.deeps; deep16/js/keeper.js K.isDeep, K.CFG.deepDepth

entries.what: The Keeper's fight has two ways in (10-03): WADE IN starts it with the party ON THE LEDGE, the water's edge (floodstair geo.entry, the squares as they were); PUT A HAND ON IT at the mark starts it at once, the party BY THE RUNE: geo.entryRune, the seat's pick of 'the dry-landing squares beside the rune' -- lane [12,10] [11,10] [12,9] [11,9] and [12,8] for a fifth (map 12,7 11,7 12,8 11,8 12,9; along 11 is the Ice Wall's row). Won at the mark, it goes as WADE IN's win: 'The keeper sinks back into its stair... You bring the five up.' (w.keeperGone, no new words) and the five's gear; the seat's call. The rope with the Keeper asleep passes the quest with no fight, as before; awake and unbeaten (the mark's fight lost, or a save from before), the rope fights first, by the rune.
entries.why: Griz 10-03 (relayed to the cloud seat): 'WADE IN starts the fight at the ledge and spawns the heroes ON THE LEDGE ... ACTIVATING THE RUNE (PUT A HAND ON IT) starts the fight at the rune and spawns the heroes BY THE RUNE'; the rope without the Keeper woken 'must still pass the quest WITHOUT starting any fight'

entries.what: The ladder's Keeper is origin/main's old fight word for word (main at ed7be2a, before the Keeper work landed): the fight keeper-ladder (main's keeper record, its id, map and foe kind aside) on the map floodstair-old (main's floodstair: the stair running north to a pool, wade 13, no rune, no light) with the foe keeperold (main's keeper: Constrict and Drag Under, 58 HP, the keeper_p1 stand-in), none of deep16/js/keeper.js in it. The names keeperold and floodstair-old are the seat's; the Pocket DM keeps keeperold out (PK.NAMED_OUT) and leaves floodstair-old off its maps (its Flooded Stair is the new one). It replaces the ladder's K.PROFILE_OLD Keeper of 10-03 (100 HP, one 2d6 Slam, on the new hall), which stays only as ?keeperfight&old=1.
entries.why: Griz 10-03 (relayed to the cloud seat): 'THE LADDER MUST STAY EXACTLY AS IT IS ON main ... the ladder's fight to be the old fight unchanged'

entries.what: The story fights before the Deep are half again as hard: x1.5 the fight's adjusted XP by the DMG's reading (deep16/js/pocket.js PK.diff, our four at the fight's level), each addition of the fight's own kind or place, in the grid's record and the 8-bit scene's list both, nothing DEADLY x2, no fight under a 60% win for the class AI. Built 10-03: the Snoot +1 gnoll +1 hyena (840 MEDIUM to 1325 HARD, x1.58); the ettercap +2 wolf spiders (975 to 1500 HARD, x1.54). The overseer's five answers (10-03): 1, the crew keeps the scene's "Four of them" and swaps kinds instead (the seven-head crew built here, +1 crewman +2 of the night crew, x1.47, is overturned; the swap is queued, and the night crew are CR 1/8, so the swap as worded reads x0.82); 2, read the crew's HP off that version, one step lighter under 50%; 3, the chuul gets one giant frog out of the shallows, the lake's own (x1.57; queued); 4, the Wet is left, and is not benched as a fight; 5, the ladder's landlord and settling pools are left ("The ladders are not for this, as with the Keeper"). Out: the Keeper (redone), the wagon night and its road catches, the cloaker, the Deep, the 8-bit's random fights and the Hex. 10-28 (Griz, "Take the leans", the difficulty lane §3): the crew's fourth is Skell (#skell), a Bandit Captain in Hask's pattern for the second crewman -- 1700 HARD to 2400 DEADLY by PK.diff, x1.41, the scene's four kept; and the ladder keeps its old rungs 3 and 4 as the Keeper's does: ettercap-ladder, snoot-ladder and crew-ladder in fights.js hold the old foes in the old places, and the story records carry ladder: false. 10-28, answer 3 built: the chuul's giant frog out of the shallows, the lake's own (fights.js chuul, at 5,4 on the point's water) -- 1100 MEDIUM to 1725 HARD by PK.diff, x1.57, the ring's rounds untouched; chuul-ladder keeps the chuul alone on rung 4.
entries.why: Griz, 10-03: "I think we should up the CR by a 1/2 for the early fights. They're taking the slide trap down to the cloaker, we'll let that be fine." -- "CR your call, you've examined the numbers closer than I. I have found things easy." -- "The Keeper has been completely redone (almost finished) exclude. Exclude Wagon Night as well." The overseer's call: half again of the adjusted XP, not half a CR added. Griz, 10-03, on the Wet: "we should cut the Wet from benching it's got all that 'spawn in crawlers that attack corpses story stuff'". Notes: cloud-notes/early-cr-notes.md.

entries.what: On the Wet's grid the deep station's crate stands where the 8-bit's crate is (the bucket on it, half again as big), and the station's lamp -- an iron lantern on a post, lit -- two squares north of it on the 8-bit (the grid's (3, 30); one square east until 10-06, Griz: "the lantern - which sits at 5, 29 and I think would go better at 3, 30"), the one light in the dark: bright 10 ft, dim 10 more, on the lamp's own square (deep16/data/maps.js wet lampAt and lights; deep16/js/wet.js W.layCrate, W.layLamp). The pool and its rim, the 8-bit's x 3-12, y 3-8, are dressed stone: nothing burrows under them (noBurrowAt).
entries.why: Griz, 10-04, his situations ear-file: 'We should put a light nearby the bucket and double check the sprite we're using to make it more a visible draw on the grid'; 'The tiles around the Landlords pool should be switched to solid stone'; then in the pane, 'the bucket glows like its a light' when the light sat on the bucket's square -- so the lamp got a body and its own square; 'seen, good enough'. The lamp on a post and the crate's look are the seat's draft (the drafts stand, RULED 09-24). FOR THE COWORK SEAT: the deep station keeps a lamp lit by its crate and bucket (a place detail, THE TWO CANONS).

entries.what: The Keeper's fight can be left: the corridor's east end is the way out (LEAVE THE FIGHT, live on that square, greyed off it with the why), reachable once his Ice Wall thaws; one of the party out and the party goes too (oneLeavesAll, the Wet's rule, the engine's now); a run leaves him awake and unbeaten -- the rope then fights him by the rune, as after a hand on the mark. In every fight that allows running the wheel shows LEAVE THE FIGHT everywhere, greyed off a way out, and the ways out are drawn plainer.
entries.why: Griz, 10-04, from the pane: 'Keeper Fight lacks fight escape'; then 'keeper escape works, can we do the pull the rest of the party we do with the Wet escape?'; and from his situations ear-file on the Wet at level 3, 'party members are not allowed to use the flee under action (not on wheel)'. The class AI never runs, so the proof was his hand (?at=stair). The greyed command's words and the 0.7 marker are the seat's draft.

entries.what: The top of the Edifice (Sólskaft's facade) as a DEEP16 map: three 15 ft dwarven floors, about 45 ft; Fountain Street along its foot with the falls' pool and two fountain basins; a deck on top, five squares deep behind a parapet of merlons, with the falls' head at its middle; the middle ten columns of the face shelved with a sill at each floor; a stair of one-step squares cut up the east end; a rope the dwarves left hung from the parapet at the west end. REBUILT 10-04 at 40x28 after Silverton's rhythm: the third floor (the orchard) stands at 30 ft with magically-harder-than-glass skylights as its ceiling; the mountain's waterfall pours in at its back wall, runs down the middle of the orchard in a channel and spills over the lip into the street's pool; west of it the Sunshaft, a circle cut in the floor down to the first floor with a stair winding down its rim; east of it grass beds, trees, fences; the lip has piers and arches; front doors marked (walking in one and coming out up top is NOT built). REBUILT 10-04 night as the EXTERIOR, 60 wide after the 8-bit Silverton's rows: Fountain Street along the foot of the facade (the arches every four columns, the fountains along the wall, the falls' basin at the middle, the water running off east as a channel, the road north at the west end, the houses across the street, the lane south), the facade 45 ft (18 steps), and on top the roof: skylight glass with a stone rim and merlons, through which the orchard on the third floor shows -- its grass, its trees, the Sunshaft's circle; the mountain's waterfall comes down the back as a channel into an intake pool and pours into the structure. The arches' tops are sills at 15 ft (DC 18 by hand); the 30 ft above a sill takes a grapple or the dwarves' 45 ft rope at the west end; a climber goes straight up. The orchard deck, the Sunshaft stair, the shelved band and the east stair of the 10-04 build are gone (the orchard is interior). 10-05: the fountains' water 15 by 10 ft (three squares along the wall, two out) inside the one-step rim, so they reach a row less into the street; the north road at the west end four squares wide (20 ft), so a Huge giant can come down it.
entries.why: Griz, 10-04: 'can we map fountain street to the top of the ediface (outer walls of solskraft) with room to fight on top?', 'Dwarven place with high ceilings (15?) 3 floors'. The wiki gives no height and nothing on top (a reader's sweep, handoff-2026-10-04-the-edifice-top.md); the deck, parapet, falls' head, sills, stair and rope are the seat's drafts (a PLACE built for the game is realm canon too, RULED 09-26). Map id `edifice` in deep16/data/maps.js. Griz, 10-04: 'on the top a waterfall from the back of the mountain pours into the dwarven structure. The third floor is where they grow surface foods (lil orchard, etc)'; 'the orchard deck is on the third floor with magically harder than glass skylights - with an area on the 3rd floor with a circle cut out - the shaft of light descends to first floor interior'; 'the monster has to climb up the ediface ... might let players walk in them [the front doors] and come out up top for a movement cost (don't build that in)'. Griz, 10-04 night: 'I was hoping you'd redo it. It's supposed to be external and the third floor is internal tho possibly visible to the skylight glass that should make up the majority of the 4th floor/3rd floor ceiling.' Griz, 10-05: "i think 15 by 10 would do the fountains better (not as far into the road)"; the road's width is the seat's, for the giants ("Have the monsters come from the north road").

entries.what: A bucket of rope and grapples by the first house at the west end of Fountain Street (the Edifice map's `ropeBucket`, a crate at (3, 14)): anyone of the party beside it takes a Rope & Grapple out of it for nothing, one a turn, and it is never empty while the fight is on that map (TAKE A ROPE on the ring; battle.js exec 'bucketrope').
entries.why: Griz, 10-04 night: 'I was also thinking there should be a bucket by one of the fountain street houses that is an endless supply of rope and grapple while on the map...' The seat's: free (an object interaction), one a turn, the party only.
entries.src: deep16/data/maps.js edifice; deep16/js/battle.js Battle.besideBucket, exec 'bucketrope'; deep16/js/ui.js bucketObjs

entries.what: The Skylights (DEEP16 fight `edifice`, data/fights.js): a defend fight on Fountain Street under the Edifice -- two stone giants (one of each look) and two trolls come down the north road for the skylight glass over the Sunshaft; Pyro comes out of the vault doors first and the four after him, the doors shut behind them and the bars drop on the far side, then initiative; the first time one of them is up the facade Pyro calls "They're going for the skylights!". Off the ladder, at level 9 (the seat's lean). The entry card's words ("Word comes down to the vault: giants on the north road, and trolls at their heels -- and they are not looking at the street. They are looking up at the glass.") and the walk-in cards are the seat's drafts; Pyro's line is Griz's. 10-05 later: at level 8 (the party most likely 8); the foes spread along the facade's foot after the road -- the male giant at the foot between the first two fountains goes for nothing but the window (no blow or opportunity attack at anyone, two rocks to throw, at the glass alone), the female and the two trolls guard him (whoever comes within 30 ft of him, the nearest first); the entry card redrafted for the story: word reaches the king on the road and the held lamps carry them back up to Sólskaft ("Word reaches the king on the road: giants on Silverton's north road, trolls at their heels, and they have not come for the street. Back up the lamps to Sólskaft, down through the halls to the vault door." -- the seat's draft). 10-05, third pass: Pyro fights at full here (his own city), not taking the party's measure, inside the 8-bit game too; both giants carry two rocks; the male, once at the window, throws his at whoever stands on an edge where the blow knocks them off -- the rock's STR DC 17 save is against going over (5 ft straight back from him and down, the fall's 1d6 a 10 ft, prone); anywhere else his rock is never thrown and his clubs go at the glass.
entries.why: Griz, 10-05: "2 stone giants (each model) and 2 trolls and see how that goes"; "Have pyro come out followed by the party then the doors lock behind them. Have the monsters come from the north road, the team pop out and then initiative. Have pyro say 'they're going for the skylights' when the first one climbs?" The level and the drafted words are the seat's (10-05). Griz, 10-05: "1 spread them along the facade"; "Male stone giant nothing but window, female leads trolls against anyone that tries to stop him?"; "be problematic if the male has infinite rocks - two max"; "most likely the party will be 8, so test 8 & 7"; "I was thinking we end pyro walking them down the road with him getting emergency word and the using the magic teleporting lanterns the 8 bit added... or other handwaving"; the 30 ft guard radius is the seat's. Griz, 10-05: "3 - pyro full serious business mode"; "1 - yes" (two rocks for the female); "can we make it so the male throws his two rocks at people on the edge (once he's made it to the window) with a save vs knockback off the edge?" The 5 ft push and the SRD rock's DC 17 as the save are the seat's.

entries.what: The Edifice's vault doors as DEEP16 draws them: two leaves in the two dressed doorways at the facade's foot, planked wood with a dark X of braces corner to corner and a gold ring on a dark boss at the middle, after the 8-bit Edifice's doors; drawn shut unless the fight opens them, and open while the party comes out of them.
entries.why: Griz, 10-05, with a picture of the 8-bit Edifice: "see if you can cover those doorways with these"; "those doorways are good if we can put those doors over them as closed".

entries.what: Throwing a Rope & Grapple up a face in DEEP16: as far as the rope is long (fifty feet), to the top of a face the thrower can see -- read from where the thrower is (a hanger's eye at its hang), and the top's edge counts as seen when the square under it the rope would hang to is -- a Dexterity check, DC 10 to 30 ft and 2 more for each 5 ft past (35 ft 12, 40 ft 14, 45 ft 16, 50 ft 18); missed, it clatters back and the action is spent. The SRD 5.1 lists a grappling hook (2 gp, 4 lb) and gives it no rule.
entries.why: Griz and the rope seat, 10-04 (30 ft at most, DC 10: his lean and the seat's); 10-05, Griz: "2 yes" (the sight from the thrower's own height; the lip of a face you stand under seen) and "go with +2 DC per 5 beyond 30", the reach the rope's length (the seat's, after its 50 ft in content/items.json).

entries.what: The two stone giants of the Skylights named on Griz's delegation (10-05, 'Name the Giants for me'): HRUNGNIR, the male at the window (nothing but the window, two rocks, cuts no rope); HYRROKKIN, the female who leads the trolls and guards him. The Eddas' jotnar: Hrungnir the stone-headed, stone-hearted giant who fought with a thrown whetstone and rode into the gods' hall; Hyrrokkin the giantess fetched when no god could launch the ship, who rode in on a wolf with serpents for reins. An alternate pair offered in the garrison's quieter register: Steinarr and Hallvor. The Cowork seat's draft stands (RULED 09-24: no [GRIZ] stubs); his one word re-cuts it. RE-CUT 10-05 on Griz's word ("second names"): the giants are STEINARR (stone-warrior), the male at the window, and HALLVOR (rock-guardian; Hallvör on the cards), the female who leads the trolls and guards him -- the garrison's quieter register; the Eddic pair declined. On the fight's cards (data/fights.js edifice: the foes' `name`). MOTIVE RULED 10-05 (Griz: '2 - nailed it'): the two are the first things the one-eye -- the Old One's vessel walking north to the Doors as an Ancient Power Player -- took on his way up; Hrungnir's 'nothing but the window' is the vessel's own single-mindedness, and Hyrrokkin is there for him. The Edifice fight is the first seam between the game and the ending's spine (the Great Old One in the gnoll on his way up to the Doors to take the Seat).
entries.why: The SRD 5.1 carries no naming lore (stat blocks only); the realm's giants already sit in the Norse register (the Doors' frost-giant hold, the jarl's throne), so the public-domain jotnar are the convention we own. His 10-05 word in the Skylights handoff: 'giant and stone giant are distinct, but they'll probably get names when we work in the lamp storyline'. Where these two come from down the north road is OPEN -- the lamp storyline's, not minted here. The line is uncommitted in the shared checkout: the code tab commits it by name with the cards' build. Griz, 10-05: "second names"; the code tab built them into the Skylights the same hour. The realm fact it implies -- that the vessel's road north passes through Silverton -- is raised on the wiki's ear-queue as SK-14, not minted; the game's event stands by the two canons.

entries.what: The Skylights (DEEP16 fight `edifice`, data/fights.js): when the trolls come down the north road, the street's people run down the south road to the Hex for the stables; only Bloodsnout's four come up, a round late. Captain Ferris Dunmore's human stable (CANON 09-11/09-19c: hires out at a gold a man a day, two the sergeant) stays in its yard because nobody has paid the hire. The card: 'Up the south road at a run, the street's people behind them: Bloodsnout's four, out of the Hex. Captain Dunmore's yard stays shut -- nobody has paid his hire.' The second four had been labelled 'Talmok's' (10-05, the waves' seat) -- Talmok is Bloodsnout's champion, not a stable master; the label is gone with them. The party out of the vault a round after that (the third), the fight already under way.
entries.why: Griz, 10-05: 'handoff should have stuff about thinning the towns defenders (losing the human group that wasn't paid). I'd also like to stall them another round (citizens go get them) and stall another round before the heroes show up (word went down the road quick and a teleport is fast, but the action should be in play before they get there - potential lever)'. The event is his; the card's words and the round numbers (stables 2, party 3) are the seat's draft.

entries.what: The Skylights after Griz's second play (10-05, DEEP16 fight `edifice`): the first two trolls run down the south road after the street's people in the first round, and Talmok -- Bloodsnout's champion, not property -- comes up it at the head of Bloodsnout's four in the second to meet them there; the garrison of Solskaft comes out of the falls' curtain at the back of the roof in two -- two troopers with light crossbows at the third round, the Drill-sergeant and two more at the fourth -- each with a Rope & Grapple of its own; with no rope down and two of them on the roof, one ties a rope off at the lip over the street; Pyro, who came out of the vault with the party, goes back in through its doors when one of the foes makes the roof, and comes out of the falls' curtain onto the roof the next round (the card: 'Pyro goes back in through the vault doors, for the stair to the roof.').
entries.why: Griz, 10-05: 'Do bring him and have the first trolls chase the civilians more'; 'at least the first two out (of the waterfall now, ya?) should have crossbows and bolts'; 'drill sergeant in the 8 bit'; 'come out the door with the party and in the door when one actually makes the roof, out the waterfall next turn?'; 'if no ropes down and two on roof, maybe have a dwarf run to the ledge and set a hook/rope down?'. The events are his; the squares, the rounds, the light crossbow and the card's words the seat's draft.

entries.what: Pyro carries one handaxe +3 (10-05 evening, Griz, on 'Pyro cannot reach any of them from here' in the watched Skylights: 'one handaxe +3 magical return the at the end of his next turn (turn without it) (i figure the logic will still use it rare given normal action damage...)'). The SRD 5.1 handaxe (1d6 slashing, light, thrown 20/60) as a +3 weapon (SRD: Weapon, +1, +2, or +3); thrown only when nobody stands in his reach after his walk, at full (never while he takes the party's measure), at the one highest up the face first, else the nearest he sees. It returns to his hand at the end of his next turn, the one he is without it -- ours: the SRD's returning weapon (the Dwarven Thrower) comes back at once. deep16/js/pyro.js S.axe
entries.why: Griz's design, built as he said it; the return's timing is his, not the SRD's

entries.what: When Steinarr falls in the Skylights, Hallvor rages and turns on the glass herself (10-05 evening, Griz: 'and lady giant (rages?) and goes for window if her man goes down', then 'yeah, regular rage she shouldn't have - storyline can cite unknown deific intervention or lady giant hormones'): the barbarian's Rage as the grid runs it -- +2 on her STR blows, bludgeoning/piercing/slashing halved, STR saves with advantage, a minute -- her roof guard and her ward dropped, the glass her target with anyone in her reach on the way struck first. A stone giant has no rage by the SRD 5.1. deep16/js/ai.js brute
entries.why: Griz's ruling; the story's reason left open by his word

entries.what: Hallvor's whistle (10-05 evening, Griz: 'when/if Hallvor makes the roof, "whistles and says 'come on down'" as a free action, then 2 spiders come down each side of the waterfall and target her foe-climbers'; 'Two spiders, one comes down centered between the falls and the edge *each edge of edifice'; 'can she whistle and call them?'): the end of her first turn standing on the glass's roof, a free action, she whistles and calls 'Come on down!' and two giant spiders (SRD 5.1 Giant Spider) come down the mountain's face onto the roof's back rim, each centred between the falls and its edge of the roof (x 19 and x 39). They hunt any of the party or the garrison on a rope or the face first -- known by her call, seen or not -- going to the lip over the nearest; the rope's grapple cut from its top, the web at a climber in sight, the bite at one in reach; no climber, the brute's way. Never, if she never makes the roof. The whistle is the chip synth's; her call plays deep16/audio/come_on_down.mp3 when a clip is there. deep16/data/fights.js edifice, deep16/js/ai.js whistle 10-05 night (Griz: 'get the spiders wall-crawling climbers (particularly webbed ones) - spider spiderclimb faster on web per SRD'): a spider with prey on a rope or the face goes over the lip and down the face beside them (the column next to theirs, on a 5 ft mark at their height) and bites there; through their turns it holds the face and scuttles up or down after them; the webbed climber is its prey first, then the nearest; with its web ready and the prey unwebbed it shoots from the lip first; it no longer goes for the rope's grapple (ai.js downFace, alongFace, climbersOf). Its descent provokes no opportunity attack from the lip and is not held to the foes' three-apart climb spots.
entries.why: Griz's design; the spiders' answer to her whistle and their hunting the climbers by her call are the seat's reading of 'target her foe-climbers' The seat's read of 'faster on web per SRD': the SRD 5.1 Giant Spider has Spider Climb (no check) and Web Walker (webbing never slows it) and no faster climb on a web; built as those two, plus the hold below.

entries.what: The Skylights' second garrison wave (the Drill-sergeant and two troopers) comes out of the falls the second round after Pyro does -- never, if he never goes up (10-05 evening, Griz: 'Stagger the dwarves up top. First two as now, second two and the captain the second round after pyro shows up.'). The first two crossbows still at round 3. deep16/data/fights.js `king: 2`, js/pyro.js S.toRoof
entries.why: Griz's ruling; 'shows up' read as his coming out of the falls' curtain up top

entries.what: Spider Climb's hold (10-05 night, ours): a creature with Spider Climb (data/foes.js `spiderClimb`, the giant spider) hit while clinging to a face keeps its hold with no DEX save (battle.js hurt skips clingSave); a push still knocks it off.
entries.why: The SRD's Spider Climb needs no ability check to climb; the grid's cling save is ours (10-04 night), so the seat read the trait as the hold no blow shakes. The seat's call, his to overrule.

entries.what: The way down by a climb speed (10-05 night): a creature with a climb speed stepping down a face of more than 5 ft pays the height from the turn's climb as it does going up (grid.js stepCost), and short of the ground it clings part way down (battle.js moveAlong, `hang.down`) and climbs the rest next turn (ai.js climbRest); no fall. Before, it dropped the whole height for one square's 5 ft.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 Climbing costs the same down as up; the handoff's item 5 (Griz: 'get the spiders wall-crawling climbers') needed a spider that could stop at a hanger's height.

entries.what: The call from the surface (10-05 night, Griz: 'a fella running in after lamp 3 is clear, saying there's an attack on the surface - chance to save - them lamping from 3 starts this fight - with xp reward hand back to 8 bit after the battle'): at the end of the Third Lamp raid (or at the next lamp touched, for a save already past it) a runner from Solskaft comes down the road -- giants and trolls at the Edifice, climbing for the skylights, the king gone up to the roof -- the save is offered, and while the call is out a lamp's road menu leads with TO THE SURFACE! in place of BACK UP TO SOLSKAFT (the gate, reached on foot, starts it too): up the lamps, out through the vault onto Fountain Street (solskaft_deep), and the Skylights on the grid (DEEP16 'edifice', its own cast: fights.js ownCast). Won: the 8-bit's ending pays two stone giants and four trolls (13000 XP, their silver), flag skylightsWon, two closing lines; lost: GAME OVER, the save the runner offered. Flags surfaceCall, skylightsWon. The runner's and the closing lines are the seat's drafts (content/text.json deep.surface*, deep.skylights*). Playtest: ?at=skylights. (10-20: LEFT THE FIRST GAME with the Skylights -- RULED 10-20, Griz: "Revert to the old ending in 8-bit before the edifice fight was added and call it the first game"; the 8-bit's ending is the raid, the road held, the consult and THE ROAD IS HELD again; the Skylights is the second game's, deep16/data/fights.js edifice. The first game lane.)
entries.why: His ask, built in the session; the lines drafted under RULED 09-24 (no [GRIZ] stubs), his to rewrite.

entries.what: The story's fighting styles on the sheets (content/heroes.json `style`): Barley and Brann Great Weapon Fighting, Lymen Defense; the other fighters (Hedda, Halldor, the trooper, Pyro) none recorded.
entries.why: RULED 10-06 (Griz: Great Weapon Fighting in the 8-bit by class and weapon, '1 - yeah'; 'yeses. Pocket DM is meant exactly for that type of character building'). Barley's and Lymen's were already theirs (by name and by class); Brann's follows from the ruling (his battleaxe in both hands). The shield-bearers' styles undrafted on purpose: a Defense or a Protection would change the guests' weight.

entries.what: MPMon, the Monster Party Monster: a class of the game's own for Griz's Monster Party PCs (his stream table, they live/monster-party-prep), kept in deep16/js/mpmon.js clear of the SRD classes' machinery. THE SPECIALS: 2 a fight, shared, back on a short rest (MP's '2 specials per encounter'). Monster Party's numbers come to the SRD's scale by 0.27 (its PCs' HP against an SRD fighter's and cleric's at 4), HP by the SRD's average of each build's die, an ASI at 4 and 8; two builds so far, Denny and Beholda, any level 1-9 by name (?npc=, the Pocket DM's seats). Design: they live/beholda/deep16-translation.md. AMENDED 10-06: THE SPECIALS grow with the level -- 1 at 1st, 2 at 3rd, 3 at 5th, 4 at 7th, 5 at 9th (MP.specialsAt).
entries.why: RULED 10-06, Griz: "MPMon (MonsterPartyMonster) as a separate class to keep our hands clear of the other machinery"; "Build now". RULED 10-06, Griz: "3 at level 5, 4 at 7, 5 at 9 down to 1 move at lvl 1".

entries.what: DENNY (MPMon), a Lobstamonkee -- Griz's red monkey in a denim jacket: climbs 30; MONKEY FISTS (1d6 + STR, 1d8 with both hands free); the denim jacket AC 12 + DEX; d10. TAUNT: his swings, +1d6 on the first that lands (2d6 at 5th, 3d6 at 9th), then the one swung at and up to his proficiency bonus more within 15 ft save WIS (8 + prof + STR) or are TAUNTED till their turn ends (the AI goes only at him when it can; disadvantage on attacks at anyone else). DENIM DAMAGE: his swings, the first that lands +1d8 (2d8 at 4th, 3d8 at 6th, 4d8 at 8th), doubled on a critical. At 5, Extra Attack and CANNONBALL: a leap of up to 20 ft beside a foe (no opportunity attacks), every foe beside him DEX (8 + prof + STR) or 2d8 bludgeoning and prone (half, standing, on a save; 3d8 at 9th), then a swing -- set against what the classes get at 5 (a fighter's Extra Attack, a monk's Stunning Strike, a Fireball).
entries.why: Monster Party's Denny (Taunt: 15 + 5/level, +1 taunted per success; Denim Damage: 15 + 5/level + 10 per success) at the SRD's scale; Griz, 10-06: "Denny Race Lobstamonkee", "Come up with a level 5 for him that is loosely 'balanced' with what player classes get at level 5".

entries.what: BEHOLDA (MPMon), an EyeGregore -- 'the Benevolent Beholder', Griz's (the book's beholder is not in the SRD; the kind is his word): hovers at 25 ft, darkvision 120, no hands (a potion held to her, nothing she must hold); hide AC 12 + DEX; d8. DICE SLAM: her three dice swung on her will, 1d8 + WIS. VNA BUBBLE (a bonus action): 10 ft + 5 a level (at most 30), +1 AC and 1 more for every two levels (at most +5) to her and her friends inside, till her next turn; pops when she is stunned or down; Griz's bubble art. BALEFUL GAZE: one she sees within 60 ft, WIS (8 + prof + WIS), 1d8 psychic a level and DOMINATED till the end of its next turn (it goes at the nearest of its own side it can reach), half on a save; charm-proof takes the damage only. At 5, THE BIG SCREEN: the projection, a 30-ft cone, (level - 1)d8 and dominated, half on a save.
entries.why: Monster Party's Beholda (VNA Bubble: 10 ft + 5/level, +1 +1 per success; Baleful Gaze: -1 def per level and per success, inverted to 10 damage a point against the Algorithm) at the SRD's scale; Griz, 10-06: "projection attack as baleful gaze", "mind domination high hp damage", "Make the projection a 3rd ability/feature that unlocks at level 5", "EyeGregore".

entries.what: RASCAL (MPMon), a Lobstamonkee -- Griz's needle-felted lobstamonkee in a black cowboy hat, his right arm a giant claw: climbs 30; MP's Social PC, so CHA is his stat (his DC 8 + prof + CHA, his blow by it); d8, CON 10 (MP's 70 HP against Denny's 120); the lobster shell AC 12 + DEX. FIRE BOLT his regular blow, a cantrip (1d10 fire at 120 ft, 2d10 at 5th); PINCH the claw, 1d6 + STR, when something is on him. SOCIAL SHARING (an action, a special; MP's Dice-Share): the hat comes off and he bows -- up to 1 + prof friends within 30 ft each get a Social die (d6, d8 at 5th, d10 at 9th) spent where it turns a miss into a hit or a failed save into a saved one. SOCIAL FLAME (an action, a special; MP's Range Fireball): a ball of fire round one he sees within 60 ft, 10 ft out (15 at 3rd, 20 at 5th), everyone in it DEX or 1d6 fire a level, half on a save. At 5, SOCIAL DISTANCING (an action, a special, the game's own): a 30-ft cone, each foe in it WIS or 2d8 psychic (3d8 at 9th) and FRIGHTENED of him till its turn ends (it gets away; disadvantage while it sees him), half and unshaken on a save, the fear-proof take the damage only -- set against Fear, the wizard's 3rd-level spell at 5.
entries.why: Monster Party's Rascal (Range Fireball: 60 ft, 10 ft + 5/level, 10 + 5/level + 10 a success; Dice-Share: his action dice to the others at round start) at the SRD's scale by 0.27; the third special the seat's, on Griz's word 10-06: "please invent a third special for rascal", "He'll range attack with a cantrip like Aurdin", "1 - love it", "2 - they get two specials per fight and that's a usage - action seems right", "Build it"; the looks his: "Social sharing as a hat removing bow", "Social flame as dancing with claw clapping".

entries.what: THE MASCOT (10-06 night): the MPMon as the SRD's shape -- races (the Lobstamonkee, humanoid, climbs; the EyeGregore, fey, floats, a 5-ft ceiling), the class Mascot, four subclasses as Monster Party's roles (Tank STR, Buffs WIS, DPS CHA, Heals WIS). The levels: 1 two core specials, the setup one a bonus action; 2 a free bonus move (Monkey Flurry, Eye On It, Scuttle); 3 a passive (Stand Firm, Lucky Dice, Spicy); 6 a reaction (Bodyguard, Eye Contact, Hot Take); 7 a fourth special (Lobstah Hug, Spotlight, Going Viral); 9 the Hivemind (the Tank's ward, Buffs' aim, the DPS's heat, Heals' temporary hit points, each 1d6 for a Mascot's next special). Every special grows a step a level, power on even levels and reach on odd. Social Distancing is the ring round Rascal cleared. Goose (Heals) drafted: a sling, a single heal (bonus), a group heal, Honk, Big Heart, Fountain, Not Today, Lifeline (its half to a chosen ally).
entries.why: Griz, 10-06 night: 'What would be your instructions for adding a character race and class set to the SRD races and classes?'; his rulings verbatim in the MPMon lane section 6 and PATCHLOG; the moves past his words are the seat's drafts ('Those are good', 'I trust your plan, you can start building'); deep16/js/mpmon.js

entries.what: GOOSE (the Mascot, Heals), a Lobstamonkee -- built 10-07 on his sheet goose_p1: climbs 30; WIS his stat (his DC 8 + prof + WIS; the sling 1d4 + WIS, 30/120); d8, CON 10 (MP's 65 HP to Rascal's 70: 8/23/28/48 at 1/4/5/9), AC 14 in shaggy fur. The seat's names for MP's two heals: HEART TO HEART (the single heal, a bonus action: a friend within 30 ft -- 60 at 5th, 90 at 9th -- or himself, 1d6 + WIS, +1d6 on each even level: 3d6 at 5th, 5d6 at 9th) and GROUP HUG (an action: every friend within 15 ft of him -- 25 at 5th, 35 at 9th -- 1d4 + WIS each, 3d4 at 5th, 5d4 at 9th); the down get up. The draft's moves as built: HONK (2nd, free bonus: a foe within 30 ft that can hear him, its next swing at disadvantage -- Vicious Mockery's mark); BIG HEART (3rd: his level on each heal); FOUNTAIN (5th: within 30 ft -- 40 at 7th, 50 at 9th -- the worst of Lesser Restoration's ailments ended and 1d8 + his level, 3d8 at 8th); NOT TODAY (6th reaction: a friend within 30 ft, not himself, whose blow would drop it stays at 1, once a fight, on its own); LIFELINE (7th: a friend within 30 ft -- 60 at 9th -- tied the fight long to a second, himself or another, who takes half of every blow on it; it lets go when either drops or they part past twice the reach; at 8th the one tied +1 AC and saves). The seat's sizing: MP's numbers at 0.27 beside the SRD's heals (Healing Word, a Life cleric's Disciple of Life). His specials green (the heal's look).
entries.why: Griz, 10-06 night: the skeleton 'that's good, yes', the drafts passed ('Those are good'), 'Cleanse as Fountain', 'LifeLine chooses recipient ally (can tie denny instead of self)', 'yes, historically a sling', Heals on WIS ('Wisdom it is'); 10-07: his sheet picks, 'his specials should mainly be green energy', and on building: the other window's kit table pasted (the draft itself recovered from its 10-06 23:33Z message). Names and numbers past his words are the seat's; deep16/js/mpmon.js, deep16/README.md 'THE MASCOT'.

Third Lamp's lies three squares across, north-west of the tower (the 8-bit's (64, 6)). MOVED 10-07: Third Lamp's circle is the big one (five across), centred in the station's south room at the grid's (31, 13); the small one lies nowhere yet.

The dwarves have put teleportation circles at the lamps, and we'll use this for the one at the third lamp they use to get to the battle at the edifice." The placement in the station is the seat's. Griz, 10-07: "lamp map: go ahead and use the big circle centered in the room south of the map".

entries.what: THIRD LAMP STATION (deep16 map `lampcircle`): the 8-bit's road square for square, highway_3 x 36-75 and highway_4 x 0-42, rows 3-20 (83 x 18; 606 open squares, 497 to stand on): 24 squares of hall up from Second Lamp with its south alcove, the station whole (the tower lit, the cistern's pools, the cots, the season's stores as cover where the 8-bit stacks its raid crates), then 43 squares of hall on toward Deepholm out to the causeway over the black water. Both ends open (ways out, and where a wave comes in). The tower drawn as a dwarf-cut column with its lamp burning (js/circles.js), bright 30 ft.

Aim for as many squares as we use in the wet 'give or take' - we'll have waves of attackers - have more of the hall past the 3rd lamp than hall between the second and third lamps". The cut (where each hall ends), the stores as cover and the tower's look are the seat's.

entries.what: THE LOBSTAMONKEE LIGHTHOUSE, the room under the light (deep16 map `lighthouse`): a round room 13 squares across inside a wall of grey built stone; the big circle (his zodiac wheel, five across) flush in the middle of the floor, the party round it; a stair up the west wall to the light (five steps to the hatch), the way down by a door on the south side, crates against the wall. entries.why: Griz, 10-07: "this is a special side-project for the livestream folks, we used to do monster party monster fight on an owlbear table ... make a map for the room under the light at the lighthouse with the big portal they jump into"; earlier: "the big one is at the lobstamonkee lighthouse and is the entrance". The room's size, stair, door and crates are the seat's. RULED 10-09 (Griz): "The Lobstamonkee Lighthouse is Stream stuff making a Cameo, not realm" -- fold: game, never to the wiki.

entries.what: THE GAME SHOW'S WORDS (deep16/js/gameshow.js), the seat's drafts round his: Pyro's opening line "The lamp is under heavy pressure, and Sólskaft is under attack on the surface. entries.what: THE GAME SHOW'S TUTORIAL, DENNY'S LESSON (deep16/js/gstutorial.js GS.LESSONS.denny), his words, the seat's drafts: "Name's Denny. I'm the tank: I stand in front and make them hit me instead of my friends." / "Goblins, up from the door, and they want Goose. Watch my turn." / "Every turn I get a MOVE, an ACTION -- the yellow A -- and a BONUS action, the blue B. The bar at the bottom keeps count." / "First, the feet. The pale-blue squares are as far as I can walk. Point at one and the dots show my way; click, and I go. Right in front of the trouble." / "Click me and my ring comes up." / "My specials live under SKILLS." / "TAUNT is a bonus action, the blue B. The 2 nearest that fail their save have to come at me, not at Goose. Use it when they're going for my friends." / "At this level that's my one special for the whole fight. A short rest brings it back." / "My action's still here, the yellow A. ATTACK on the ring, then click who to punch. Monkey Fists: no special needed. Most turns, that's the job." / "Nothing left I want? END TURN, bottom right. Then it's their go." / "See? Taunted, they had to come at me. That's the job: they hit the denim, not my friends." (or, both saved: "They shook it off. It happens -- the dice are real out here. Next time, they won't.") / the aside "(The tutorial hands Denny his special back. In the run, a short rest at the bed between waves does that.)" / "DENIM DAMAGE is my other special, and it takes my action: a punch, and the first one that lands hits extra hard. Save it for the big one." / "That's me. Stand in front. Taunt the ones going for my friends. Denim the big one. Punch the rest." The stage is the seat's too: two goblins and a hobgoblin in at the lighthouse door after Goose; their blows soft in the lesson (every d20 a 12, every other die a 1). 10-07, the second pass (the two pools of specials, his reaction ask): Taunt's line ends "...have to come at me, not at Goose, till the end of my next turn. Use it when they're going for my friends."; after it "Specials come two ways: bonus ones and action ones. This fight I get one bonus and one action special -- that Taunt was my bonus one. A short rest brings them all back."; the punch "My action's still here, the yellow A, and I'm keeping my action special for the big one. So: ATTACK on the ring, then click who to punch. Monkey Fists, no special needed. Most turns, that's the job."; the hand-back aside cut; Denim "DENIM DAMAGE is my action special: a punch, and the first one that lands hits extra hard. That's what I was keeping it for -- the big one."; the reaction's beat: "One more kind of move: a REACTION. It happens on THEIR turn, one a round -- the R on the bar." / the aside "(The tutorial lends Denny BODYGUARD, his reaction from 6th level, for a look.)" / "When something swings at a friend right beside me, the game asks me. STEP IN, and its roll is at disadvantage: two dice, and it keeps the worse." / "It rolled a 15 and a 4. With me in the way it had to keep the 4 -- a miss on Goose. That's a reaction: on their turn the game asks, and you answer." (the blow's d20s pinned 15 then 4).
entries.why: Griz, 10-07: "tutorial 1 isn't done - i should see text like the lines Pyro and Ingrith give from Denny about his ability and when to use it, then the wheel popup - highlight - like you click it - show the cursor moving to the target. Him having to move into position kinda just makes it better". No [GRIZ] stubs (RULED 09-24): the seat drafts and the drafts stand. Griz, 10-07: "if you're in his tutorial, we gotta fake it enough so noobs get reactions (even though he won't be level yet)"; the pools RULED as a trial the same hour.

entries.what: THE GAME SHOW'S WAVES (deep16/js/waves.js WV.TIERS, the seat's draft, 10-07): nine tiers of SRD monsters, surface kinds in from the west (the road up from Second Lamp), cave kinds from the east (the causeway from Deepholm): 1 goblins, then goblins and giant rats; 2 hobgoblins with goblins, a giant spider and rats; 3 a bugbear's goblin war band, duergar and darkmantles; 4 gnolls and hyenas, an ochre jelly with grimlocks, an ogre and worgs with grimlocks; 5 two ogres and bugbears, phase spiders and giant spiders, a war band and gricks; 6 an ettin and two ogres, a chuul and gricks, a troll and worgs with gray oozes; 7 two trolls, a xorn and an earth elemental, BOSS a drider and its spiders; 8 trolls and an ogre, an otyugh, a chuul and gricks, BOSS a cloaker and darkmantles; 9 trolls and an ettin, a drider and its spiders, BOSS the Edifice team (two stone giants, two trolls). The cards' words: 'Goblins, up the road from Second Lamp!' · 'Goblins behind -- and giant rats over the causeway from Deepholm!' · 'Hobgoblins, in step, with goblins at their heels.' · 'Something on eight legs comes over the causeway, and the rats run ahead of it.' · 'A bugbear drives a goblin war band down the road.' · 'Duergar out of the Deepholm dark -- and the ceiling moves.' · 'Gnolls, laughing, and their hyenas with them.' · 'Grimlocks feel their way along the wall. Behind them the floor oozes.' · 'An ogre and its worgs from the road; grimlocks over the causeway.' · 'Two ogres, and bugbears in their shadow.' · 'Phase spiders blink out of the rock; giant spiders come down after them.' · 'A war band from the road, gricks from the dark.' · 'An ettin, both heads arguing, and two ogres.' · 'A chuul hauls itself out of the black water. Gricks follow.' · 'A troll from the road; the causeway grows slick.' · 'Two trolls, hungry.' · 'The rock itself comes for the lamp: a xorn, and the earth walking.' · 'A drider climbs out of Deepholm, its spiders before it.' · 'Trolls, and an ogre, all teeth.' · 'An otyugh and a chuul out of the water, gricks on the walls.' · 'A cloaker unfolds from the dark, and the darkmantles drop.' · 'Trolls and an ettin, down the road at a run.' · 'A drider and its spiders -- the deep is emptying.' · 'THE EDIFICE TEAM: the stone giants, and the trolls they brought.' The rests: 'SHORT REST at the cots.' · 'LONG REST: the night at the cots, and the dwarves' wardens mend the lamp.' The ends: 'THE LAMP BREAKS.' · 'NO ONE IS LEFT STANDING. <villain> turns to the lamp.' · 'The rest of them melt back into the dark.' (a wave past 40 rounds) · 'THE LAMP HOLDS' (tier 9 held, js/gameshow.js GS.victory). The road's own lamps, dim, along both halls (WV.CFG.roadLight). 10-07 later, his rulings: the road lamps kept; THE LAMP HOLDS cut -- past tier 9 the run goes on, tier 10 and up tier 9's waves with one more of each wave's smallest kind a tier (WV.tierWaves), its card 'PAST THE NINTH. The deep keeps coming: every tier from here, more of them.' and each wave's card '... And N more of them.'
