entries.why: Griz, 10-07: "the most famous monsters that fit the CR requirements (i.e. goblins) - surface monsters from the back, cave types from the deepholm side"; "7-9 we'll aim for third is a 'boss monster' (tough CR, not our customs - save 9 - which can be the edifice team)"; the lane's §3 D, seat 2. The words are the seat's, standing as drafts (no [GRIZ] stubs); the roster his to recut. Griz, 10-07: "1 - keep, 2 bench, 3 keep going, 4 yes".

entries.what: THE GAME SHOW'S SUPPLIES (deep16/js/supplies.js; the items in content/items.json, 10-07, seat 3): the names and lines of the tier 2 +1 weapons (Play-Button Knuckles, Loaded Dice, Flame War Claw with +1 on Rascal's spell attacks, Heartstring Sling) and armour (Double Denim, Janny Jerkin -- his name --, Thermidor Plate, Puffer Plate: AC 14 + DEX, no plus), tier 3's Fresh Fit and Rivet Job (laid over the armour worn), Gains Ring, Mod Cape, Lag Cloak, tier 4's Hard Carry (+4 on each one's own blow; Rascal's is the Hot Take), the Ban Hammer (Denny's, thrown 20/60, back at the end of his next turn), the Hot Take (+4 claw and spell attacks), Sponsored Skin, the Boiled Shell's four resistances (Denny piercing, Beholda poison, Rascal slashing, Goose bludgeoning: the waves' damage tallied off WV.TIERS -- piercing 348, slashing 231, bludgeoning 222, poison 48, acid 11), Dwarven Denim (+2, poison out at the turn's start), the epic amulets Virtually Invulnerable (resists nonmagical weapons) and the VNA Amulet (+2 saves within 10 ft); Sling Bullets; the empty sling's bonk (1d4, the SRD's improvised weapon) when Goose runs dry; the hand-out lines (Goose ties the cloak round Beholda, the ring on an eyestalk); the roll-off panel's words. The seat's readings of his rules: who has had an item does not roll for it (tier 2's +1: any weapon as good), a tie rolls again, a solo natural 20 is +3 on that one's next roll-off won or not, no one left to roll -- all four roll for an item of the tier up; tiers 3 and 4 the roll-off first, then a die for the winner's item among what fits it; the plus laid over the armour one piece at a time; the epic amulet's winner by a roll-off; the chest's armour goes on at the bed; the LAMP box in the corner opens the buttons too.
entries.why: Griz, 10-07: "might have sonnet runners invent them" (the drafts, deep16-gameshow-supplies.md) and his picks of them, RULED: "Tier 1 - roll 1d4 and add one of them, unless Goose is <10 ammo ... 2c, 2e, 2g - add small rule, 2j - beholda 'Janny Jerkin' ... 23a +4 / 23b - check pyro's handaxe code (comes back next round) / 23c +4 / 24b - each hero diff resist, choose wisely ... 24c - cures poison start of turn, no shove modifier"; the readings his to overrule (the lane's §3 C).

entries.what: the Harbinger (10-08): the made gnoll -- a gnoll Mr. Ripples thumbed on his walk to the Doors, mirror eyes in both sockets, the Skull-Gate chief's right hand before the vessel took him (Griz's lean); the seat's kit on his leans: Backhand x3 (reach 10), Pounce (the SRD lion's shape, 3d10, STR DC 17 or prone), Kneel (Hold Person, the word said), Drink Light (a reaction counter that heals 10 a level and grows him a step; above 3rd a CHA check, failed he Overfills), Foretell (no one in reach at his turn's end: Mirror Strike readied), the Mirror's eye; CR 13 Large monstrosity, AC 18, 310 HP, speed 40 (deep16/data/foes.js harbinger)
entries.why: Griz, 10-08: 'He's yours my dude. Take the seat.' -- his leans 'Harbinger', Drink Light 'a counterspell/heal', Kneel 'Hold Person with flair'; tuned to his 'Try and get him 6/10 on a solo vs Aurdin Party 7 on the ladder' (61 of 100 on the Gnoll Hills)

entries.what: The Grey Road, the ranger's archetype of our own, made on GreyFang (the pit-master's way: guard the one beside you, give the ground you choose, answer from the bow). 3rd: TURN IT ASIDE -- when a creature he can see attacks one within 5 ft of him while he holds a melee weapon, his reaction adds his WIS modifier (1 at least) to that one's AC against the attack; PIT-WISE -- climbing costs him no extra movement, and standing up costs him only 5 ft. 7th: GIVE GROUND -- when a foe moves within his reach, his reaction takes him 5 ft away without provoking; if that leaves him out of its reach, his next bow shot at it before the end of his next turn has advantage. 11th (GreyFang by name; players stop at 9): an action, one of SWEEP THE RING -- a melee attack against each of up to three creatures within 5 ft, each one hit, Large or smaller, makes a DC 15 DEX save or falls prone -- or COVERING VOLLEY -- up to three arrows, a ranged attack each at a different foe within 10 ft of an ally he can see, each one hit has disadvantage on its next attack roll before his next turn. Built on the grid (deep16/js/features.js the Grey Road; rules.js RU.riseCost; grid.js stepCost; battle.js attack and moveAlong), AI-run (buttons later); rows from his sheet: parry, backstep, climb, whirlwind, volley.
entries.why: Griz, 10-08: 'If we do not already have a subclass option for folks to choose, please invent one based on this fellow and request any accompanying animation rows it would need' (the ranger had only the Hunter); after a side-by-side of the Hunter, the draft and a copy that fails the 09-28 'sufficiently distinct' test: 'Turn it aside is good'; 'Clear the ring as sweep the ring attack up to 3 within 5 ft, DC15 dex save or prone'; Large or smaller: 'yes, less the rules lawyers try to trip a dragon'. Give Ground and Covering Volley stand as the seat's draft (the game's law, 09-24). Not pickable by players yet: on his 'ask Lanes who gets the picker' the lanes window filed it in the level-up pick lane (handoff-2026-10-06-the-level-up-pick.md §5) -- widen the rogue's archetype pick at 3 (the 8-bit's pendingChoice, the climb) to every class at its subclass level, the SRD's and ours as the rows; the Grey Road stays on GreyFang till then.

entries.what: GreyFang on the grid: ranger 11 of the Grey Road by name (maxLvl 11, as Pyro stands at 12), STR 12 DEX 18 CON 14 INT 10 WIS 16 CHA 10, the SRD's average HP (92), leather, a longbow and a shortsword, Archery; a Lupine -- darkvision 60 and keen hearing and smell (advantage on the Search action's Perception) -- kept on his own record, not a race in the Pocket DM maker's list (the races are their own lane). His sheet greyfang_p1: two side sheets and four isometric (deep16/js/classes.js greyfang; tools/greyfang-sheet.py).
entries.why: The seat's draft of his numbers, for his story fight with the Harbinger (Griz, 10-08: 'This session is for that and to do his character animations and whatnot for a story fight with the Harbinger'); who he is: TarlynsPit/wiki/greyfang.md.

entries.what: GreyFang's pit, the story fight (deep16/data/fights.js greyfang): the four at 7th and GreyFang lent to them, the party CAUGHT OFF GUARD (the Harbinger comes for him first; his hunt and his blows take GreyFang before anyone -- the fight's `quarry`), GreyFang `fated` (at 0 he goes down, never dies in the fight). Won, the ending plays on the map's camera (deep16/js/trophy.js): 'The Harbinger lies still. The crowd on the tiers lets out its breath.' -- 'The mirrors in its eyes turn over, and something else looks out of them.' -- the Old One through the Harbinger: '"Not yet. You were sent for something."' -- he stands up whole (the ripple, his ascend row), leaps to GreyFang ('"Kneel."' if he stands; else 'GreyFang lies where he fell. It stands over him.'), the blow and a flash, the body headless (his Fall without the head, cut in tools/greyfang-sheet.py) flung across the screen onto the sand, 'The Harbinger has what it came for.', the leap out over the rim ('It is over the rim and gone, and the pack with it.'), 'His bow lies on the sand beside him.'; the win: 'GREYFANG IS DEAD. THE HARBINGER IS GONE.' The pit itself a stand-in (deep16/data/maps.js greyfangpit: a sand floor in a bowl of four 2.5 ft tiers, 10 ft deep). RE-CUT 10-08 on his look: the Old One is no ring now -- the mirror passes over the Harbinger's whole body faster and faster as he rises from the dead, stands and floats up off the ground; the climax (the light over everything); the drop into a cloud of dust and mirror glints; his face close, the mirrors flaring: '"The Mane is mine."' (deep16/audio/the_mane_is_mine.mp3, the Kneel's voice: David, -5, slow 0.85, a 220 ms echo; the Mane the gnolls' paramount relic, wiki gnoll-hills); the Pounce onto GreyFang ('It has GreyFang by the throat.' / 'It takes GreyFang up off the sand.'); up into the sky (a blue screen over the world, the map's last picture sinking away under them, its edge the horizon); 'High over the pit, it looks GreyFang in the eye.' -- the two faces close; the flash; 'The Harbinger has what it came for.'; the camera down through the sky after the body, the body falling faster; on the sand, 'It is gone into the sky, and the pack scatters after it.' The '"Not yet. You were sent for something."' line and the leap over the rim are gone. RE-CUT AGAIN 10-08 on his second look: the mirror passes on the body while it lies, before a word ('Mirrors run over the body, and over again. Something else is looking out of it now.'); as he stands, a ring of mirrors over the pit and the whole party held on its knees till the end ('A ring of mirrors runs out of it across the pit, and every one of them goes down on their knees.'); the drop onto his Pounce row's landing (its own dust) with the mirrors over it; the close-ups the big faces off the sheets (tools/faces-sheet.py: GreyFang's from his first sheet, the Harbinger's from the made gnoll's second with its amber eye painted a mirror), GreyFang's turned to look back at it. The fight itself: no surprise round and no hunt -- he is stomped (19 of 20) with GreyFang standing at the win.
entries.why: Griz, 10-08: 'Scripted, presently leaning toward direct old one intervention after apparent party victory - cutscene type Harbinger revive, obtain trophy, escape'; 'I was thinking a headless sprite falling across the screen onto the grid prone'; 'you're kinda the GreyFang sprite guy, no window better suited to finish him off'; '7th is good'; the reward his bow ('Yes'); the map 'goes in the map lane - might have to pull the whole town map out of our collective heads first'. Wiki rulings 10-08 (TarlynsPit/wiki/greyfang.md): 'The Harbinger hunts him down', GreyFang 'is not going to make it', staged in public. Every card's words are the seat's drafts (the game's law, 09-24); the bowl is the seat's stand-in. Griz, 10-08, seeing the first cut: 'The Old One's intervention is not a thin purple oval'; 'Rapid mirror effect over his whole body, dead to standing to floating up in the air (increasing speed mirror effect) - climax - mirror effect in (or applied to pounce cloud on drop back to the ground - face zoom "the Mane is Mine" eyeflash ... try same voice as "kneel"'; 'Pounce onto GreyFang. Leap into the sky with him holding onto a living or down GreyFang as appropriate. "Into the sky" is blue background with map tile horizon to only blue background. Zoom in on faces. Camera to blue sky panning toward the ground, body sprite falls faster than pan. Pan down on end scene as present'; 'I like how his body lands in different places'. Griz, 10-08: 'Saw text about his eye flash while he was lying as a corpse, start the mirror effect while he's still down please'; 'We need to put the players under dominate (or something to explain their stunned inactivity lack of initiative), maybe AOE mirror effect when he rises?'; 'He drops from the sky onto his feet, can you try the pounce land with mirror dust clouds it comes with'; 'I remember a lot of the art sheets starting with a big ole face in the top left..'; 'for the story battle he has to get stomped, funner if they can have GreyFang up when he's dead'.

entries.what: A Ring of Flying: while worn, a flying speed equal to the walking speed; put on in a fight as a free object interaction (content/items.json ringofflying), handed out only in the ladder's testing room Rings of Flying (deep16 fight flyingrings).
entries.why: Griz, 10-08: "rings of fly or flying rings" -- the SRD 5.1 has no ring of flight (Winged Boots carry the rule), and his ask was a ring.

entries.what: THE FEAR SCALE (deep16/js/rules.js RU.FEAR): 1 shaken (-2 on attack rolls, saving throws and ability checks), 2 frightened (SRD 5.1's condition), 3 panicked (SRD 5.1's Eyebite word: frightened, and the Dash away each turn); cumulative, a level at a time, each level carrying the ones below; a WIS save at the end of each of its turns takes a level away; under Mindless Rage it lies still.
entries.why: Griz, 10-08: "No fear scale currently exists in the game, check SRD, there's frightened and then more severe versions / panicked might be the top" -- the d20 SRD's cumulative ladder (shaken, frightened, panicked) read through SRD 5.1's words where it has them; the step-down save is the seat's call.

entries.what: The mirror hyenas' laugh (data/foes.js mirrorhyena `laugh: { dc: 13 }`, deep16/js/traits.js packLaugh): one of the party on the ground (prone, or dropped) and two or more of them standing -- after that turn the nearest that sees it laughs ('The Mirror Hyena laughs at <name> on the ground.'), a beat, the rest take it up ('The pack takes it up, N of them.'), and every one of the party standing saves WIS 13 or goes a step up the fear scale; deafened, Heroism and fear-proof hear none of it; once a round. The cards' words are the seat's drafts. (10-08 later: the DC 13 is for the pair it takes to start the chorus, +1 for each hyena past two -- four make 15, eight 19.)
entries.why: Griz, 10-08: "For the hyena I was thinking something like reaction to party member falling prone, play one laugh, beat, play the others - when the others go everyone makes an intimidation check or gets one level on the fear scale" -- the check read as 5.1's Wisdom save against a fright; once a round the seat's call. Griz, 10-08: "+1 DC for each additional hyena (more scary)".

entries.what: The Harbinger's levers on a party read (a fight's callN: 'read'; deep16/js/traits.js): under strength 20 he toys ('The Harbinger looks the party over, and smiles.' -- no Pounce, Kneel and Foretell, 'circles the one who kneels, in no hurry.', no blow at the held) till he rises; over 32, as he rises, his MIRROR DOUBLE steps out ('The mirror in him opens, and another of him steps out of it. Its eyes are purple.'): the Mirror Harbinger, a quarter of his hit points and his damage, his eyes purple by code, breaking like glass when he falls. His laugh on the Ascend is the deep chorus (deep16/audio/hyena_chorus.mp3), the pack's the eggs' synth laughs after it. The cards' words are the seat's drafts. (10-08 later: the quarter RULED; GreyFang alone stays hopeless, RULED.)
entries.why: Griz, 10-08: "I like your mirror image for him - but instead of 'which one is him' it's from the mirror realm and has purple in the eyes (by code?) and does some fraction (1/2, 1/4 - not variable by party threat) of HP and attack damage"; "I also like the small party adjustment being a script to use the lesser used powers more often"; "Can you string the laugh you made for him in front of the hyena chorus playing? Him on cast, them on effect?" -- the quarter the seat's call on the bench. Griz: "1/4 looks great"; "It should stay hopeless."

entries.what: THE DM'S POCKET DM (10-09, deep16/js/pocketdm.js): on the Pocket DM's title, a click on the high seat, then the right tomb lamp, then the left opens the DM's table (st.dm), and the same three put it away; each answers a click (a lamp flares, the seat glints) and nothing says the order. Its egg: 'THE DM'S POCKET DM' -- 'The high seat takes you.' / 'Every creature on the shelves, every door of the game, and a campaign of your own: CAMPAIGN and DOORS, on the left.'; put away, 'THE RELEASE EDITION' -- 'The high seat is empty again.' The table: the cap 12, Pyro without the trial, GreyFang and every Mascot on the roster, the story's named in the dial's pot, the class floor's knobs on the foes screen, DOORS (34 of URLS.md's). THE CAMPAIGN: five shops by creature type with icons drawn for them (a paw, a claw, a sword, a boulder, an eye), 100 sp a CR kept in copper (1/8 is 12 sp 5 cp), a purse of 1000 sp that takes in twice a ladder fight's CR won or lost, the units newest first, a unit let go paid back in full, three floors struck from the random draw, a ladder of five slots (four rungs and the trial) filled units-first. RE-CUT 10-09b on his word: a purchase is a RECEIPT; receipts picked (a click one, shift+click a run, ctrl+click one more or less, E a row) and bound with BIND AS UNIT are one UNIT at their CRs summed, UNBIND gives them back, LET GO pays a receipt back; a table's CR (a built slot, or a dial ladder's rung at its rolled CR) is filled with whole units newest first while their CR fits and their heads fit the floor, each once a table, the rest rolled; CR 0 on the shelves at 10 sp, a unit of CR 0s riding only with a table that has CR left.
entries.why: Griz, 10-09: "if you click the throne and then the right lamp and then the left lamp, it takes you to the DM's Pocket DM where the cool new stuff in URLs and the stuff in test runs unlocks"; "each of the icons (and humanoids) is it's own shop and CR is in silver, i.e. 50 silver = 1/2 CR"; "they start with 1000 and get double the CR of the ladder encounter for each fight on the ladder (always able to create units)"; "build a ladder. Next to each map a CR up/down ... fills CR with units first, from most recently created units first". The seat's calls: the lines, the icons, copper for the eighths, the refund in full, CR 0 and the stone giant's second look and the old Keeper off the shelves, a struck floor only at the DM's table. 10-09b, Griz: "I went to the store and got Visiting Barbarian and two stable fighters - that was supposed to make a 'unit'. click, shift click and ctrl click to select units then a 'bind as unit' button?"; "CR 0 at 10 SP or something, should be able to include them".

entries.what: The Pocket DM's three Mascot eggs (10-09, deep16/js/pocketdm.js PD.EGGS; js/mpmon.js MP.unlock, once a save): DENNY on the first character made -- 'A Lobstamonkee in a denim jacket drops off the high seat.' / '"Somebody new at the table? Make room. DENIM DAMAGE!"' (his Denim Damage clip); BEHOLDA on the release edition's first SAVE CAMPAIGN -- 'An eye opens in the Sunshaft's light, and floats down to the stone.' / '"A whole campaign, saved? Oh, I have to watch this one."'; GOOSE on the first SITUATIONS notes saved -- 'HONK.' / '"You wrote it down! Somebody reads these, you know."' (the honk). Each ends '<Name> is on the roster now: cycle a seat at THE PARTY.' RASCAL (10-09b) on the first unit bound -- 'A Lobstamonkee pops up from between the receipts, grinning.' / '"A unit of villains? Every unit needs a rascal."'
entries.why: Griz, 10-06 night: "'make your own character the first time' = unlock denny" (ruled then, built 10-09); 10-09: "Making a campaign should unlock Beholda when you haven't bothered to do the 3 clicks" (this takes the place of her 10-06 egg, which was never built); "let this unlock a lobstamonkee - flash an easter egg the first time they've actually typed something in and pressed the save button", "Goose is the only one I personally can't select at the moment". The words are the seat's drafts (CLAUDE.md: drafts stand). 10-09b, Griz: "3 Creating first 'unit' ;)".

entries.what: Leg one re-cut (the story review, 10-14): the road to First Lamp is solidly warded, with one goblin breakthrough on the way that opens on its own cavern area with the tribe at its back. Pyro's line at the proving is 'meet me at the first lamp'; he is not happy only if the party does not wait there and reaches Second Lamp first. A full clear of the lair finds its back somehow impassable and earns a magic-item reward at First Lamp (his lean a spell sheet) that is NOT there if the party comes back with the dwarves to clear it; the full clear is why the party gets to carry a Ledger-Lamp. The first rest at First Lamp carries the talk of why the party holds a dead dwarf's shield (Audun's line ended; the ledger released it). Ingrith arrives in the morning; the party clears it deep and returns and she seals and runes it; on the way back the Grick Den or another leg-one cavern. On that return (or on a first clear made with the dwarves) a hobgoblin scouting party has checked in through the back: there if the first clear is with the dwarves; more of them if it is the second clear, with the goblin corpses as the proof of the breach. She spins up the First Lamp circle; Pyro comes through it and takes the party's measure from First to Second Lamp. 10-14 at the close, Griz: the sheet is Tiny Hut; hobgoblins over goblins is not slavery but intermingling and pecking-order dominance -- the intermingled tribes shoved to the dangerous fringes.
entries.why: Griz's pour and three rulings, verbatim in handoff-2026-10-13-the-story-review.md section 5 (the Cowork seat, config echo claude-fable-5-1). The hobgoblin scouts as the forward element of leg two's hobgoblin force is the seat's inference; which sheet, and how the back is impassable, OPEN. His words verbatim in the lane section 5 at the close.

entries.what: Between First and Second Lamp, off the highway, the entrance to a cave system that leads to the warded place on the Coldridge route (the Doors road) -- where Marko Thorne's father's caravan was lost. Second Lamp and lower is the Underdark's register.
entries.why: Griz, 10-14, verbatim in the story-review lane section 5: 'Between lamps one and two will be the entrance to the cave system that leads to the warded place on the coldridge route.' Joins fountain-street HD-1 (CANON 09-22: the warded place 'will eventually connect to the Silverton mine breakthrough'). A PLACE: realm canon by the two canons, owed the realm wiki.

entries.what: The Burial's law: a family's gear stays on its dead while the line lives, whoever is living and whatever their class; it passes only when the last of the line dies without heirs. That is why valuable items lie on the dead with living family above them -- ripe for grave robbing. Audun's line ended at Third Lamp, so the ledger releases the Door-Shield; Asmund has an heir (Signy), so his hammer is a theft and a fight with the dwarves.
entries.why: Griz, 10-14, verbatim in the story-review lane section 5: 'they wouldn't pass unless that wrong-class dwarf passed without heirs (why valuable items on dead family with living members ripe for grave robbing)'. Lore of a place that is realm canon by the two canons.

entries.what: The Black Water (leg four's causeway): two water elementals rise either side of the stones in the spirit naga's place (10-14). Lines drafted: 'It stands up on both sides of the stones at once, two of it, and neither has a face.' (content/text.json deep.naga) and the grid fight's intro (deep16/data/fights.js naga).
entries.why: Griz 10-13: "re spirit naga - we got water elemental art waiting, we'll swap them out - text sounds more like them than naga as I recall anyway"; 10-14: "Naga Swap (might need 2 or more to approx CR) go". The old line ('It has a woman's face...') was the naga's; two benched to the naga's difficulty at the leg's level.

entries.what: Searing Scourge, a 2nd-level evocation (ours, not the SRD's): the caster twirls and tendrils of fire lash every creature within 5 ft of them (the grid's eight squares round a Medium caster, never the caster) -- 1d6 fire, DEX half, +1d6 a slot above 2nd; Sculpt Spells spares friends. On the wizard list in the Pocket DM; in the story Aurdin finds it as a spell sheet (sheet_searingscourge, ready, given nowhere yet). In the 8-bit, with no squares, it takes the foe in front and up to two beside it, no picker.
entries.why: Griz, 10-14: "I need to add a custom spell and its effects. Searing Scourge - it's 'like' burning hands magically, but tendrils of fire and the wizard twirls - lvl 2 with 1d6 to all creatures in the surrounding 8 tiles (works with sculpt)." His answers the same day: DEX half; "1d6 per slot"; "Pocket DM can include, in game Aurdin will find spell sheet or easter egg spell sheet when I figure out the trigger for him to do so"; the 8-bit "do 1 and 2" (grid squares, and the front foe and two beside it). The look on his eye: "lower it and don't overlay the wizard - his hands can be at his sides when he twirls in those frames".

entries.what: Deathhand's Searing Scourge, Garland Rosen's own working of it (ours): 1d4 fire + 1d4 necrotic to every creature within 5 ft, DEX half; from a 3rd-level slot 1d6 + 1d6, then +1d6 of each a slot (the reading of his words the build took: both kinds step to d6 at 3rd and each grows by a d6 a slot). Sculpt Spells spares friends. In the Pocket DM's wizard list; in the story an easter-egg spell sheet (sheet_deathhandsscourge, ready, its trigger his to find). On the grid one hand lashes fire and the other necrotic as the caster twirls. RULED 10-14 at the close: the upcast as built, each kind growing a d6 a slot from the d6 step (3rd 1d6 + 1d6, 4th 2d6 + 2d6); the 8-bit's narrow lists name it "Deathhand's Scourge"; his left hand is the necrotic one.
entries.why: Griz, 10-14: "Signature variant 'Deathhand's Searing Scourge' - 1d4 fire and 1d4 necrotic to all creatures in the surrounding 8 tiles (works with sculpt)"; "deathhand's goes from 1d4 to 1d6 then 1d6 per slot"; on the grid's look: "can grid do one hand purple (necro) one hand fire in that few frames?" The close: "1 & 2 - correct reads", "3 - yup".

entries.what: Garland Rosen, called Deathhand: Tarlyn's old adventuring pal. He lost an arm in a fight and kept it -- the DM made it all magical necrotic -- and the necrotic Searing Scourge is his. Probably not in the game himself; his spell is. The necrotic arm is his left (RULED 10-14).
entries.why: Griz, 10-14, verbatim: "Deathhand is Garland Rosen, Tarlyn's old adventuring pal. A generous DM, I let them free action bite down on the bags of healing potion in their mouths and let him keep an arm severed in a fight, but made it all magical necrotic. Probably won't be in the game." Not in the realm wiki yet (grep 10-14): owed to it by the fold. "1 & 2 - correct reads" (the seat's question 2: which arm).

entries.what: The Halls Are Yours, while Halldor mends (10-14, content/quests.json halls): the journal's step and the arrow go first to Ragna Copperbottom ('While Halldor mends: Ragna Copperbottom, by the pool at the foot of the halls, has work that wants doing.'), then, once she has asked, to the drained stair ('While Halldor mends: the drained stair in the Warrens' wet. Hold it three nights while Ragna turns the siphon.'), then to Halldor's bunk as before. Drafted by the bug-fix seat.
entries.why: His note of 10-11: "The arrow keeps pointing at the fella who is mending - give a handoff to the flood the stairs mission".

entries.what: SECOND LAMP'S NIGHT (a hearth scene under STAY THE NIGHT, once per pass): first pass with the king -- Thyra, Gudrun breaking tallow into lamp-lots ('a lamp that gutters at Second gutters at all three'), the shaft-crew's file-leader on the two-day stage and the empty crews' cots, Pyro saying his measure of leg two aloud ('You went under it. I'd have gone round. I'm older.'), Thyra's report of Halldor, the sealed way to the Doors road off this leg ('the marks on it are older than the road'), and the silence ('Decline.'). Second pass: Hedda sits up; Brann carries Third's tallow.
entries.why: Griz 10-14: 'plot out a lamp night dialogue for the other two'; the lane handoff-2026-10-13-the-story-review.md §6.8; the lines the seat's drafts (RULED 09-24); the stage-swap and the lamp-lots CANON 10-14 (wiki/solskaft.md). Nothing of the vigil in any dwarf's mouth (CANON 07-25).

entries.what: THIRD LAMP'S NIGHT (a hearth scene under STAY THE NIGHT, once per pass): first pass with the king -- Geir on the bonded crates ('for what's coming up, not what's going down'), the road on (the draught, the black water's causeway, the troll hole, the made road Deepholm laid), the drow as the dwarves know them (they come up when a lamp is dark; a blade-captain and a voice that weaves; 'They don't raid for crates' -- what they want is not his to know), the litters and the line of names ('we sent nine up from this station. I cut the last three names myself' -- Brann's family), Pyro on the door he holds. Second pass, after the raid: Brann reading his own family's names; Hedda and the captain's ward-knot knife, turned over and put back without a word (owed to the assassins' thread, spec §7).
entries.why: Griz 10-14: 'lamp three might be about the drow or things further up the road' (read as further along, toward Deepholm); the lane §6.8; the seat's drafts (RULED 09-24); the depot, the border and the dead's road CANON 10-14 (wiki/solskaft.md).

entries.what: The Weigh-House board posts true word on the mirror-eyed after the lake ('FIFTY GOLD for true word on the mirror-eyed: what wears the glass, who put it there, and which road it is walking'); Hessle pays 10 GOLD a drop for drops from the creatures Mr. Ripples is making (the made things with mirror eyes); Winters after the Chuul: 'You're local heroes now, the world is calling.' (his words verbatim) and, if the board posts, 'Hessle has a new notice up. Read it before somebody else does.' (the seat's).
entries.why: Griz 10-14: '5 - You're local heroes now, the world is calling. - note to add true-word of mirror creatures to the silverton mission board'; '5 - drops from the creatures Mr. Ripples is making - 10 gold' (RULED). The lane §6.2-6.3, §6.6. What the drop is and which made things carry it: the seat's to propose. Whether the council would post it that early: OPEN.

entries.what: The lamps' circles are rune-work and no free ride: a crossing eats one charge of a Ledger-Lamp or one lot of the ingredients (50 gp of silvered chalk and ink). A Ledger-Lamp holds 3 charges and recharges on the ingredients, 50 gp for 3 (the quartermaster's counter; Gudrun's stores). A lamp's warden spins a station's circle from its store with no lamp. For the build: ledgerlamp carries charges (3); the road menu's TO <LAMP> spends one and says so; a warden's spin (Geir's call up to the Skylights; Brann's after the raid; the wounded lamped out of Second Lamp) costs the party nothing.
entries.why: RULED 10-14 (Griz: 'Approve runework circles and no free ride. A Ledger Lamp holds 3 charges - lamp warden can use ingredients without ledger lamp, lamp needs ingredients to recharge (50gp for 3 charges)'); the SRD's Teleportation Circle as the shape (srd/spells/level-5.md); the lane §6.11; wiki/solskaft.md.
entries.folded: 2026-10-14 wiki/solskaft.md (the circles and the Ledger-Lamp bullets)

entries.what: The wheelwright's fork re-cut (replaces the forge scene EV.wheelwright and HAND HIM TO INGRITH / THE LEDGER / LET HIM HIDE): the first time the party goes out the front door after the king (frontDoor, crewDealt), Pyro comes outside with them and Papa Urtusk is on the street with the wheelwright. VOUCH FOR HIM (coerced by Hask's crew) or SAY NOTHING. Silent: Pyro takes him into custody; later the party finds him in Solskaft making amends on the old lift. Spoken for: Pyro says he can make it up to them by working on the old stuff. Both roads end at the old platforms; whether the lift runs a season later is never shown as a fact.
entries.why: RULED 10-14 (Griz: 'have pyro come outside with party first time they go out the front door, Urtusk present Wheelwright to Pyro - party can vouch he was coerced or remain silent ...'); the lane handoff-2026-10-13-the-story-review.md §6.13-3, §6.14. The old lift PLACE: wiki/solskaft.md (SK-1 kept, re-cut 10-14). Papa's and Pyro's lines are the seat's drafts (RULED 09-24).

entries.what: The count's premise re-cut: Ingrith's ledger has what the treasury sent down; what it lacks is the SURFACE's side -- what the town took out of the dwarves' vein after they went down (the human shafts from ~68; Fane knowing the vein was never mined out). Her petition to the trader clan needs both sides of the account before trade reopens with the town that robbed the seam; Androit's father's mine records are the only count of what the Rows took; Idony's page and price unchanged. Her ask re-cut: 'My ledger has what we sent down. It has nothing of what they took out after we went. Somebody up top wrote that down, because somebody always does.'
entries.why: RULED 10-14 (Griz: 'Still don't get why Ingrith would need Silverton's count' -> '1'); the lane §6.13-1. The clock lines are wiki/silverton.md's.

entries.what: The heir's premise re-cut: Asmund of the Silversands was dead before the gate sealed -- on the road, the lamp on his niche (the seat's lean: Third Lamp, the withdrawal's last season) -- and never knew of a child; Wenna, above with a half-dwarf child in a town about to start throwing people into shafts, hid her from the ROWS, not from him; the dwarves closed the wedge believing the line ended. 'The row above him stops short. Somebody meant to come back for it' is Wenna. The rite ('The ledger records an heir. The wedge did not end'), the hammer and the renown stand; Aldwin's and Signy's lines take the re-cut.
entries.why: RULED 10-14 (Griz: 'Asmund wouldn't have been the abandon an heir type, that's human behavior' -> '2'); the lane §6.13-2; the Burial's law of the line (CANON 10-14, wiki/solskaft.md). Asmund's death before the sealing is lore owed to the Burial's families (PROPOSED 09-26b).

entries.what: The tariff board's second half: once Deepholm's door opens, the tariff copy shown at Dagny's grille claims the Coldridge caravan's one crate (the toll was paid seventeen years ago; the bond is Tobin's by his line); it comes up to Third Lamp's bonded crates, and Tobin opens it -- the Thorne shop's last stock, GEAR FOR WHOEVER OF THE PARTY IS LOWEST (the hired heroes who lag), his gift for the history set right. The first half (Mical, the manifest, 'somebody's son should know', Tobin stays) stands.
entries.why: RULED 10-14 (Griz: 'an opportunity to give some magic gear to characters who need to level up - like, kid had his history wrong or something?' -> '4'); the lane §6.13-4; Third Lamp as the bonded store for the deep end (CANON 10-14, wiki/solskaft.md). What the gear is: the seat's to propose by the level-up lane's class floor.

entries.what: The Snoot mode (snoot-mode/): three Dominion units come in on the west road (the Castegut road) two days after the Harbinger begins his hunt -- Kat's wagon as the serial has it (Suada's patrol: the patrol lady, an elder sergeant, a dozen soldiers, the wagon), each a CHAINMAIL warlock (p.30, -2 on the Fantasy table, a fire ball a fight) with a figure of troopers and the wagon; they walk to the inn and watch, strike only at what is small and next to them, and the battle ends when they are mopped up after the head.
entries.why: Griz, 10-14: "2 days after the Harbinger starts head hunting bring in 3 dominion units from the west road - kat's wagon loadout"; "(I expect the dominion to be mopped up after he claims the head - not cannon for mode test)".

entries.what: The Snoot mode's readings of CHAINMAIL and OD&D (snoot-mode/js/rules.js, the seat's): a hex 5 miles and a turn a day (Book III), a figure 20 men; moves at CHAINMAIL's ratios to Book III's foot 3 (armored foot 2, heavy and light foot 3, heavy horse 4, medium 6, light 8); hills and Web Gulch cost 2, a road 1; the Combat Tables (p.40) with impetus and standing horse (p.17), post-melee morale doubled under twenty figures a side (pp.15-16), instability (p.17), rout by contact and the rally table (p.16), fatigue after three rounds (p.11); heroes +1 to their unit's dice, super-heroes +2 and eight figures, wraiths and warlocks two, a hero killed by regular troops only on four hits at once (eight for a super-hero); the super-hero's or wraith's charge makes the units it reaches roll their instability number or fall back (p.30, p.34); a wraith walks through any unit with no hero in it (p.44's withdraw note, p.34) -- so only a paladin, GreyFang or the four hold the hunting Harbinger; Newland's paladin a Hero with the unit, its cleric a religious order (+1 morale, never surrenders, p.19) that mends a figure a day; the barbarians berserkers (+2, charge on sight within two hexes, never check, p.20); the four's fight with a unit is DEEP16's road fight with a war-band sized from its figures (a hard fight for four at 8), a win routs the unit and costs it figures by the share of the band that fell; the Harbinger beaten anywhere but at GreyFang is carried by the mirror to the moot ground and comes again two days on; the score is CHAINMAIL's points (p.27), a gnoll 2.5. RULED 10-14 night (his "sounds great"): no hex ends the day shared -- three rounds with both standing, the lower morale total backs off a hex in good order (the side that never yields makes the other back off; both never, the fewer figures); every fight played as a show of its own beats on an isometric patch of its hex's ground (snoot-mode/js/show.js), about five seconds, a round's dice together; the move's pop-up (SN.preview: the tables both ways, if they hold). RULED 10-15 (his "Book basics for sure"): the Dominion's warlock by CHAINMAIL pp.30-33 -- two Armored Foot, her charge makes the enemy check, impervious to normal missiles, a missile every round chosen per lady (fire ball or lightning bolt), the fantastic saves 9+/6+/7+, morale 30 and 80 points; only heroes add to a unit's dice (a wizard and a wraith work on morale); the seat's readings at this scale: a fire ball kills one or two figures of one unit, a bolt one figure in each of up to two, the save rolled by one fantastic figure of a struck unit, a wizard's two figures at her own rating in the morale pool, a wizard alone checks morale at 30.
entries.why: His rulings 10-13/10-14 (build for all, Chef's dice, written orders, the witness and collision rules, "the rest as lean"); the numbers the books' own, the mappings the seat's, PROPOSED -- the lane handoff-2026-10-13-the-snoot-mode.md §10. His notes after his first play, 10-14 night: "isometric - animated combat where enemies can't end the day on the hex?", "the resolution should be a show"; the pop-up his question "is 'if moving here is likely to make combat pop-up info a player would want to know'". His word 10-15: "1 Book basics for sure"; "3 yes" (the warlock's 80 points; the super-hero's 6+ save, rules-source.md corrected).

entries.what: THE SNOOT from the road (10-15, Griz: "we're going to move that to the half-way inn and start the snoot from there. For now, just auto-pin it as a mission in the journal that pops after the edifice fight"; then "yeah, we'll add some story scenes in later"): the Skylights won, a line and THE SNOOT pinned in the journal; a runner from Tarlyn's Pit in the Halfway Inn's yard (look: the guard) asks TO THE SNOOT / NOT YET, offers the save and opens the Snoot mode (snoot-mode/?from=road, its own four at 8th, BACK TO THE ROAD on its title). The mission stays open till the inn's own start is built (snootBattleDone). The runner's and the call's lines are the seat's drafts. (10-20: LEFT THE FIRST GAME with the Skylights it hung off -- the runner, TO THE SNOOT and the quest are out of the 8-bit; the Snoot mode is the second game's. The first game lane.)
entries.why: His ruling via the lanes desk; the seat's lean (open the battle from the inn, the mission open till its own start) on his "yeah". A pinned arrow that led nowhere would read as a bug.

entries.what: DEEP16's patrollady (deep16/data/foes.js): a Dominion patrol lady on the grid, a warlock of the Mirror at Amara's numbers (warlock 5, 45 HP, two beams of Eldritch Blast, the Mirror's eye), unnamed and without Amara's list; she does not flee. The Snoot's band sends one for each wagon whose lady lives, and one killed on the grid dies on the map. 10-17: built as a warlock 5 of the Mirror (NPC.NAMED.patrolladyw) with the Pact of the Blade -- a longsword called to hand -- and a list of her own: Eldritch Blast, Chill Touch, Poison Spray, Hellish Rebuke, Command, Hold Person, Scorching Ray, Vampiric Touch, Mirror Image; Amara takes the Pact of the Tome.
entries.why: His note 10-15: "there wasn't any warlocks when I ran the party into a dominion fight" -- the band sent only the soldiers. No generic Dominion warlock existed (Amara is named). RULED 10-17, Griz: "go on those opens, good with your leans" (the seat's lean: Amara Tome, the patrol ladies Blade), after "yeah, but the patrol ladies only eldritch blasted".

entries.what: The Snoot mode's Gray Keeping (snoot-mode/js/data.js gkw, gk1, gk2; rules.js SN.pray): the death-watch is the Eldest -- a Super-hero at -1 on the Fantasy table, OD&D Book I's Patriarch of 9th ("Superhero - 1") -- and eleven matriarchs who attack as Armored Foot and defend as Armored Foot ("larger and fiercer"), never check morale, mend 1d3 at dusk; the tribe's band carries a matriarch, a Hero (Book I's Lama), and the young blood go out with clerics (+1 morale, the mend). Their prayers at a day's scale, each once a day by who prays it, only where a relic is: Bless (Book I 2nd: +1 to the unit's dice and morale for the day, as its fight begins); Insect Plague (Book I 5th: from the moot into a fight on it or next to it, the biggest unit of men there routs -- no morale check, berserkers too -- and its heroes stand); Entangle (on the moot: the biggest unit of ours left is held for the day -- no charge die, struck as from the flank, no falling back, nightfall lets it go). A routed berserker runs to its own people (SN.breakUp). The witness never fills the death-watch (the seat-tribe's women). The seat's drafts from 10-15 recorded here too: the death-watch's twelve, the Wall-Laugh's eighteen and its young blood's twelve, the Harbinger's six mirror hyenas, the Dominion's dozen a wagon, a fire ball 2d6 men and a bolt 1d6, a cleric's mend 1d3 a day.
entries.why: Griz, 10-16: "I found it a little easy to clear the moot point - let's give one group a superhero matriarch and the other hero, with clerics with the gray young ones. Give the superhero entangle? There's good cleric stuff high level that didn't exist in chainmail I think. Thoughts?"; on the values, "check the superhero and hero values, we scaled down to smaller fights with regard to 'figures'"; then "all 8 leans are go". The ranks are Book I's; the hex-scale readings the seat's. Benched 10-16: twenty outriders at the moot, held 100 of 100 with her prayers and 76 of 100 on the tables alone (it was wiped in a round); the sixty of the horse escort take it every time on the tables alone and never once she prays.

entries.what: The Keeping: the cleric domain of the Gray Keeping's matriarch-clerics, Rhollor's, prayed through the relics (gnoll-hills.md: the relic-tether; his dead call through the female voices). Its spells always prepared: Entangle and Hideous Laughter (1st), Hold Person and Blindness/Deafness (3rd), Fear and Bestow Curse (5th), Blight and Confusion (7th), Insect Plague and Hold Monster (9th) -- the ground the god lies under, the laugh that is his call, the hold, the pack's terror, the curse, the rot. DEEP16: deep16/js/classes.js NPC.SUBS 'the Keeping'.
entries.why: Griz, 10-16: "Give the superhero entangle? There's good cleric stuff high level that didn't exist in chainmail I think" -- Entangle his; the rest of the list and the name the seat's drafts (the past-the-SRD principle, RULED 09-28g). PROPOSED for the realm wiki's Gnoll Hills page.

entries.what: The Gray Keeping's band and its young blood each carry a minor relic of the tribe, so their matriarch-clerics can pray away from the Mane (the relic-tether: keepers cast only in a relic's presence). Which relics, and whose keeping, stay the register's OPEN.
entries.why: The seat's lean on the relic-tether (gnoll-hills.md, RULED 08-13d; minor and major relics per tribe CANON by the 09-16e blanket, specifics OPEN), in Griz's "all 8 leans are go" (10-16). PROPOSED.

entries.what: The Eldest of the death-watch and the matriarch who goes with the Gray Keeping's band: on DEEP16's grid a cleric 9 and a cleric 6 of the Keeping (deep16/js/classes.js NPC.NAMED matriarch, matriarchlama; data/foes.js gnollmatriarcheldest, gnollmatriarchlama), STR 15 DEX 12 CON 14 INT 10 WIS 18 CHA 12 and STR 14 DEX 12 CON 13 INT 10 WIS 16 CHA 11, the skull-staff a quarterstaff, hide and mail a chain shirt, darkvision 60; the death-watch's other women the SRD gnoll's block (gnollmatriarch). Their look is ART-68's matriarch-cleric (gnollmatriarch_p1). Off the Pocket DM's random pot and the shelf's duplicates. The Snoot sends the Eldest first, then her matriarchs; one who falls on the grid falls on the map. A BOSS ON THE GRID (10-16): the Eldest at 175 HP with Legendary Resistance 3 and three legendary actions a round -- the Skull-Staff, Sacred Flame, and Rhollor's Call (2: she cackles, and each of the death-watch within 30 ft spends its reaction to move half its speed and strike one blow); the death-watch keeps three bodyguards (gnollmatriarchguard: the SRD Troll's numbers without Regeneration, her sheet and size, bite and two staff blows) and eight matriarchs. DEEP16 gained two legendary kinds for it (js/traits.js `cast`, `call`), and a class-built foe keeps its sheet's legendary fields (js/battle.js makeFoe).
entries.why: Griz, 10-16, "all 8 leans are go" (the Eldest cleric 9, the band's cleric 6 on the grid; Book I's Patriarch of 9th and Lama). The numbers are the seat's drafts: the register gives "larger and fiercer", "the greyest, longest-lived" and no sheet. Benched 10-16: the four at 8 beat the whole death-watch 10 of 10 at 94% HP -- his to tune. Griz, 10-16: "approve 3 leans above" (the bodyguards by OD&D Book II -- a gnoll king's 1-4 bodyguards fight as trolls without the regeneration; legendary actions with the Call; her hit points up and the four at 8 winning about 6 in 10). Benched over 40: 25 won, 28% HP left, about two downs a fight (four bodyguards made it 9 of 20; 198 HP 21 of 40; 150 HP 26 of 40). The Call and the numbers are the seat's.

entries.what: THE WAGON ROAD, the module that comes with the Pocket DM (10-17, deep16/data/modules.js D.MODULES 'wagonroad'): four at 1st level hired to see a wagon through two days -- 'Bandits on the road' (4 bandits, The Road South), 'Wolves at the bridge' (3 wolves, The Bridge), 'The hobgoblin scouts' (2 hobgoblins and a goblin runner, The Hex), a night at the waystation with its market, 'Stirges in the Glowseep' (5 stirges), 'Gnolls in the hills' (3 gnolls and a hyena, The Gnoll Hills), 'The bugbear in the pit' (a bugbear and 2 goblins, GreyFang's Pit: 'The wagons that went missing went here.'). The waystation is named nowhere on a map.
entries.why: Griz, 10-17: "to test it can you make a 6 fight module for a starting lvl 1 party of 4 that we can include for new users to have as example module?" -- the seat drafted the premise, names and lines; SRD 5.1 foes only; benched 16 of 20 done by the AI's party (bench16 mode=module1017).

entries.what: THE LOCATIONS' grounds (10-17, step C, deep16/js/pocketdm.js PD.LAND): each grid floor the Pocket DM deals tagged UNDERGROUND (the king's road, the Warrens, the caves: 26), URBAN (the Hex, the Inn Yard, GreyFang's pit, the Edifice, the Lighthouse: 5) or OUTDOORS (Web Gulch, the Bridge, the Glowseep, the two roads, the Gnoll Hills, the Point, the Climbing Floor: 8); a map's own `land` field stands over the table; one in neither goes UNDERGROUND when dark, else OUTDOORS. Size bands by the squares one can stand on: SMALL under 150, MEDIUM under 250, LARGE the rest.
entries.why: his 10-17 note: 'a locations store that works like the monster store by tileset (i.e. underground, urban, outdoors - probably matching world tile) sorted by map size'; the prices 50/100/200 sp by band RULED ('4-8 yes'); the grounds and the band lines are the seat's read of each floor -- his to move

entries.what: A villain of a class costs and counts at its level's CR (deep16/js/pocket.js PK.levelCR): 1st CR 1/4 (the SRD acolyte), 5th CR 2 (the priest), 9th CR 6 (the mage), 18th CR 12 (the archmage), the levels between by line, to the nearest CR: 3rd 1, 4th 2, 7th 4, 12th 8.
entries.why: RULED 10-17 ('4-8 yes'): the priest, mage and archmage anchors; the acolyte at 1st is the seat's, so the line has a floor below 5th

entries.what: Corwen Dace goes no farther than the mine: walking out of the guano mine by any way off galleries_g* with him a guest, he stops at the mouth with a line of his (text.json dace.mouth: "This is as far as I go. The road's yours -- the mine's mine.") and goes back up to the house, the escort over (js/events.js EV.warp; daceWith and daceAfter cleared, so he can be asked again).
entries.why: The road lane §4, his escort notes (1) (10-02), kept through the flip; the first game lane (10-20) built it on his '8 - yes' (game over if the kid falls stands). The line is the seat's draft (RULED 09-24: no [GRIZ] stubs), his to rewrite.

entries.what: What the lake gives back, found on the chuul's corpse when the party never had it from Elsbeth (the wagon let go, or her thanks still owed): the lead's armour +1, or a Ring of Protection -- the same as her gift (js/events.js EV.lakeGiftId, EV.lakeGiftHad; text.json lake.corpseGift). The dock is shut till the wagon night has played (mapgen.py rowboat cond flag:wagonNight), so the wagon is gone before the chuul.
entries.why: Griz, 10-20, to the lanes desk: "Find the lake gave back item on the corpse of the monster (didn't have time to give it back), wagon should still be gone before they can start the chuul fight - though we might have to turn the dock off until they stay at the inn once...". The line is the seat's draft (RULED 09-24), his to rewrite.

entries.what: WRETCH BLOODSNOUT'S COMPOUND, Silverton (the second game's town floor, deep16/js/town.js T.COMPOUND): a walled stone yard about 115 by 90 ft -- somewhat larger than a house -- on the open ground east of the Arena Plaza, behind the fighters' stables (19) and the arena family's house (24), against the stockade; its gate toward the plaza, shut; a barracks along its east side, the master's house in the yard's north-west corner, the yard between where his thirty or so drill. Drawn, never entered. Not on city map v6.
entries.why: Griz, 10-20, to the lanes desk: "yes v6 - but the orc with the fighting slaves needs a proper compound on the map not currently on the map (not accessible to game)"; then, asked which, "drawn but not enterable - it'll be larger than a house somewhat". The place on the map, its walls, barracks and house the Silverton roam seat's draft (the yard of ~30: wiki/silverton-people.md, CANON 09-19c).

entries.what: The gate hand at Silverton's west gate on the second game's town floor says: "West gate. The road runs a mile to the fork: the Tower north of it, the Pit south down the long road. East gate's the farms and the coast. Nobody bothers the dwarves." (deep16/js/town.js T.LINE) -- the 8-bit's line without its north gate.
entries.why: RULED 10-17: no road north out of Silverton, no north gate (the 8-bit's line names one; the first game keeps its own, bug fixes only). The Silverton roam seat's draft, 10-20.

entries.what: The Doors' schools placed on the realm hex map: the five-school valley (Enchantment the keyholder, Transmutation, Divination, Illusion, Abjuration) north-east of the hub toward the north coast, its floor about 2,400 ft under rims to 7,400, and the farm valley (the Granger) beside it; Thresholding Hold (Necromancy) on the west coast; the Furnace (Evocation) a day east of it on the geothermal seam; the Sealward at the ice line (about 9,500 ft). The DOORS is Conjuration's hub.
entries.why: The world map seat 10-20, his: "please place the doors schools - the one with 5 of the schools, and the rest solo amongst the black mountains ... in reference locations we can move later but probably never will" (the maps lane 2f; tools/hexmap.js seedDoors).

entries.what: A shallow wet trough along the black mountains' foot, from the western bogs to the Glowseep's harvest below the Guano Galleries' block: a thin water table falling from 420 to 320 ft, Halfway Lake (about 230 ft) below it.
entries.why: The world map seat 10-20, his: "can we lower a spot at the foot of the black mountains so the bog and the glowseep have a thin layer all the way to the glowseep section we harvest".

entries.what: Web Gulch on the realm hex map: on the Pit road between the fork and the Halfway Inn, where corridor v3 draws it, the road running down through it; a cut 350 ft under its banks.
entries.why: The world map seat 10-20, his: "gulch isn't gulching or a location" (wiki/web-gulch.md's placing, drawn).

entries.what: The Coldridge Route goes at x1.43 a road's going (the weather and the switchbacks): three wagon-days on his 35.7 mi drawing. On the second game's world map it is not walked: a door at the Galleries junction and at The DOORS, its own roam to come.
entries.why: The world map seat 10-20, his: "1 yes" to a road's own going (RULED 10-17: 3 days), and "the coldridge route as a roam probably, with up into and on mountain hexes not a thing on the world map".

entries.what: The Furnace sits on a hot seam far up the mountains to the west (a day from Thresholding Hold on the west coast), not a day up from Silverton: the Galleries module's line repaired.
entries.why: The world map seat 10-20, his: "7 - module repair" (TarlynsPit/GalleriesModule/guano-galleries-DM.md 35).

entries.what: The second game's world map goes by the SRD: 24 mi a day on foot (8 hours), difficult ground half pace (woods, bog, gulch, the three mountain kinds; hills not). Ours where the SRD has none: 17 mi a wagon-day, a road's own going number, the gulch and the Rift difficult. Book III's going stays the Snoot's.
entries.why: RULED 10-20, his: "SRD for world map and book III for snoot-play. If DMG has rules SRD doesn't, we can author our own fill in of the gap".

entries.what: The world map's road fights: the 8-bit's zone tables (content/encounters.json) read off the painted ground, a quarter of their steps in 5-mile hexes, a road counting half; the fight a lineup on a small field of the hex's ground, the four and the foes one square apart; and the MIRROR-MADE entry on every table, a group of the zone made by Mr. Ripples (the mirror hyena, else the Mirror's eyes), weighing nothing on the first day and half a group more each day after, to six.
entries.why: RULED 10-20, his: "let's try simplified random encounters suspecting we'll let players turn on a 'full grid rando' option", "note an entry on the encounter table for 'mirror-made version' weighed by game day".

entries.what: The realm hex map's heights, the seat's draft: plains about 250 ft, the Verge 150, farmland 220, foothills 1,400, hills 900 (rolling), woods 500, bog 60, black mountains 6,000 (peaks to about 9,700 with the lifts), gray 5,000, the coastal range 3,200; a gulch a cut 350 ft under its banks, the Rift 1,800; a city on its own ground (Silverton about 850 ft).
entries.why: The world map seat 10-20 (the realm names no heights), his: "2 stands", "1 yes".

entries.what: On the second game's town floor, after Winters gives the first errand: "Winters' errand is in your JOURNAL now (M, then JOURNAL), and pinned: the gold arrow marks who is next, and the line at the top of the screen says it in words." (deep16/js/counter.js C.LINES) -- the first game's winters.journalHint with the grid's menu key and the floor's top line named. 10-21 later: its last words now "...and the NEXT line says it in words" (the first game's), and the floor's own top line is gone.
entries.why: 10-21, Griz to the lanes desk: 'start a seat to get Winters set up for giving the starter mission and doing sales'; the brief: reuse the first game's words, new ones only where the grid needs them. The Winters seat's draft. RULED 10-21, Griz: "should function the same as the 8-bit unless we add a feature".

entries.what: On the second game's grid Winters keeps his errands and his shelves; his Ring of Binding (the lake) and the copper scraping offer are held, and his 'not ready' line after a talk is left off (deep16/js/counter.js C.winters). 10-21 later: not dropped -- both come to the second game, waiting on the lake (the chuul is not on the grid yet).
entries.why: 10-21: the ring and the scraping are the first game's lake story; the second game's story pass decides them. The Winters seat's call, put to Griz as a lean through the lanes desk. RULED 10-21, Griz: "they'll be in this one too, do you need more poses?".

entries.what: On the second game's counter, when the party puts Winters' work off (NOT NOW): "The dead keep. Come back when your hands are free." (deep16/js/counter.js C.LINES.notNow); the offer comes again on a later visit.
entries.why: 10-21, Griz, on the counter: "Need to 'not now' option the work/mission 'offers'" -- the first game has no refusal, so no line of his to reuse. The Winters seat's draft.

entries.what: Ned Halloway's words in his second-game scene at Percy's counter (deep16/js/counter.js C.NED_LINES; his first-game school line stays his own, content/npcs.json ned): the Doorwardens story, YOU KNOW THAT SPELL?, what a familiar is for (senses, a touch spell carried), CAN YOU CAST IT? -- "Show me." and his laugh, the rest of his story ("I decided to stick around"), the 50-silver sale, the Insight's "They are..." and the tongue asked for, no harvester, the harvest line, the page given, his "Mine eats better than I do". All drafts by the keepers cutter seat; Griz's words set them later. 10-22: his "Ned waits, a jar label half-lettered under his hand" prompt and the plain "How is it? The familiar." are retired (Ned's last line stays on the screen while Aurdin answers; the familiar is asked after by its kind) -- the new lines are ned-aurdin-replies-grid.
entries.why: 10-21 night, the house lane's "Ned and Find Familiar", THE SCENE (RULED): his design and flow quoted there; the desk: "you draft them in his voice ... Griz's words set them later".

entries.what: The Doorwardens (Conjuration; their door the man-sized cut beside the Great Door) will not take a student without a familiar -- why Ned Halloway, wizard 2, turned back at the cut.
entries.why: 10-21 night, Griz: "pick a school that isn't evocation and Ned tell story about how if you didn't have a familiar, they wouldn't accept you as a student"; "1 conjuration" (TarlynsPit/wiki/the-doors.md :29, the cut).

entries.what: Ned Halloway learned Find Familiar in the end, in Silverton, from a book he paid too much for; his familiar is a rat that rides his shoulder and sits on Percy's counter.
entries.why: 10-21 night, Griz: "He finally learned the spell, but decided to stay in town (can we code draw a rat familiar without going back to art dept?)"; "3 - on neds shoulder on counter screen and on counter on floor screen if possible".

entries.what: Ned's Page (the second game's JOURNAL, deep16/js/counter.js C.OWN_QUESTS): after Aurdin's silent Insight sees through him ("Because the components are fascinating?"), Ned trades the page with Find Familiar on it for a fresh snake's tongue off a Glowseep snake, taken by someone with Survival or Nature; turned down, the choice stays; taken, he no longer sells the copy for 50 silver.
entries.why: 10-21 night, Griz: "he'll agree then offer quest for some component from the glowseep - he wants a fresh one - and will trade the paper for that"; "2 - is the tongue something percy buys, and yes".

entries.what: The second game's way between Silverton and the Crawler Warrens' mouth camp: Silverton's feed track where it runs off the town floor's east edge opens the camp (in on the road below the bridge, the first game's warp square), and the camp's far squares go back up the feed track to Silverton; its two cards: "The feed track, out past the east gate and over the bridge: the Crawler Warrens' mouth camp." / "The feed track, back over the bridge to Silverton's east side." (deep16/js/mines.js M.LINES, M.cross). THE WORLD has no Warrens site.
entries.why: 10-21 night, the top levels seat, on Griz's "convert the warrens top levels ... onto the tiling engine": the realm puts the camp ~4 mi out over the bridge on the feed track (TarlynsPit/wiki/the-warrens.md, CANON 09-09) and the first game's quest says "out the east gate and over the bridge"; put to him as lean 5 (or a site he paints).

entries.what: On the Galleries' mouth in the second game, TAKE HIM from Corwen Dace gives his first-game join line and then "(Dace walks with the party when the dark galleries below come onto the grid and the house takes guests. Till then he waits by the beam.)" -- no daceWith flag set (deep16/js/mines.js M.LINES.daceWaits). SUPERSEDED 10-28 (the deep gallery seat): TAKE HIM takes him into the party token now, and the line is gone -- invented.json deepgallery-dace-words.
entries.why: 10-21 night, the top levels seat: the escort walks the dark floors (g3, g4), which wait for the grid's roam, and the house has no guests yet (the house lane); the flags stay the first game's names for when it does.

entries.what: A warp from the Warrens' or the Galleries' top floors to a dark floor (the abandoned workings, the Wet, the dens, the deep gallery) says "{the floor's name}. The dark floors below come onto the grid with its roam (the Wet is there already, held for the house). The party keeps to the lit floors for now." and keeps the party (deep16/js/mines.js M.held). 10-21 night: the abandoned workings and the dens are top levels after all (his "rather than the cloaker fight, that hole floor. above it are top levels") -- the line now stands only on the Wet's stairs and the ways to the deep gallery, the hole floor (g2's slide, g3's ladder); the dens' two pits say "A pit: it drops to the deep gallery, the hole floor." with it and step the party back.
entries.why: 10-21 night, the top levels seat, on Griz's "top levels": the lit, worked floors to the town's tiles; the dark fight floors are a later roam (lean 1 put to him).

entries.what: The Warrens' and the Galleries' top floors on the town's tiles take the first game's maps square for square: the first game's brown roofs blue slate and its stone roofs grey shingle (Silverton's), a door's threshold the square south of it, a lantern a post where it stands free and rock where it is in a wall, a mouth's stair with the rock behind it so the face shows the way in; the grounds drawn in code -- guano a dusty brown crust chalk-white where dry, deep guano wetter and darker (difficult going), the cave floor, cart rails with sleepers, gravel, the fungus beds, a mouth's dark, a ladder on the guano (deep16/js/topview.js TV.LOOKS; deep16/js/mines.js M.LAY).
entries.why: 10-21 night, the top levels seat, on his "onto the tiling engine we're using for silverton" and his 10-21 "The roof brown and the road brown are too close together" (Silverton's roofs went blue and grey); his eye on the looks (eyes rows eyes-warrens-camp-1021h and the three after it).

entries.what: A shift at the Warrens' pens on the second game's floor (the pens' gates, E from below) runs the first game's own table rule rolled straight -- six draws, a d20 and the milker's Animal Handling or Nature against 12, a 6 or less a CON save at 13 (the draught: the better of two) or the shift ends touched -- on the counter screen titled "The pens, mouth N" (deep16/js/mines.js M.pen); the cradle picture (js/cradle.js) stays the first game's.
entries.why: 10-21 night, the top levels seat: the first game's S.pen has the table as its own fallback when no cradle scene is loaded; the cradles were held for the second game (the house lane) till their floor came over.

entries.what: The Warrens' bunkhouses as the second game's inn with no watch: the mouth camp's bunkhouse (the resident core's) free to the party once it has worked a shift at the cradles (crew), else 1 sp; the Pellam barns at the south landing 1 sp (a thimble's price, Skarn's board). Its lines: "A bunk for the night? (free, crew sleep free / 1 sp, a silver for a stranger / rent paid in thimbles: a silver)", A BUNK / LEAVE; "The bunks fill with the shift coming off; somebody snores through the lot. Nobody stands a watch -- the staff keep the door."; "Morning, and the camp's bell."; "Not without the silver." The night is the house's long rest: THE WORLD's clock to the morning, every sheet whole, the levels' picks on the floor (deep16/js/mines.js M.INNS, M.inn, M.sleep).
entries.why: RULED 10-21 night, Griz to the lanes desk: "the bunkhouses wouldn't need watching (watched by staff) - free/cheap inn function"; the prices and the free-to-crew rule the top levels seat's (the realm: the bunkhouse the resident core's, the barns bunking day-crews for rent paid in thimbles -- TarlynsPit/wiki/the-warrens.md, CANON 09-17d).

entries.what: The Glowseep as a floor of the second game's own (deep16/js/mines.js M.SEEP_ROWS, M.seepMap): 40 x 28 north up, the mile two squares wide down its east side (in and out by it north, south and east), the bog west of it wetter westward -- mud, reeds, pools, moss beds -- a deep drain winding south to Halfway Lake with a shallow ford mid-way, the light-crews' camp by the road (a fire pit, three tents, lantern-poles, the offering stump where the wisp story is told), lantern-poles out in the moss beds; by night dark but for the moss, the poles and the fire. Its looks: bog mud, reeds, moss flecked with glow (deep16/js/topview.js TV.LOOKS A, E, N).
entries.why: 10-21 night, Griz to the desk: "Go on the Glowseep - run with its leans for all, including the time-slowing but that might be adjusted. Thematically correct"; the first game has no map of it. The seat's draft from TarlynsPit/wiki/glowseep.md (the drain to Halfway Lake, the lantern-poles, the stump-offerings, the night harvest), for his paint later.

entries.what: The Glowseep's three veteran light-crew hands on the second game's floor, unnamed ("The eldest of the three", "A pole-hand", "The quiet one"): at their camp by day, out at the moss beds with their poles by night. Their lines -- the eldest: "Day's for sleeping. The moss doesn't show till dark, and the bog's worse by day than it looks." / "Pole up, not out. You hold it over the moss and it tells you where it's thick." / with Aurdin by day: "The evoker! You walked up the mile with us, the morning after the dark. Still got all your fingers?"; the pole-hand: "Rillo buys at his shed in town, by the clean warehouse. Tell him the seep sent you and he'll weigh you honest." / "That light out past the far pool? Not one of ours. Don't go after it."; the quiet one: "Nobody owns a crop till it's picked. That's the whole of it." then "And don't go into debt." -- the realm's laugh -- / by night only a nod. The fire: "The crews' fire. The veterans keep it; nobody stands a watch here.", SLEEP HERE / LEAVE, "You sleep by the crews' fire. Somebody comes in off the bog before dawn, and nobody wakes you.", "Morning over the seep. The moss has gone back to green."; the floor's turns: "Night comes down on the Glowseep: the moss lights, and the crews go out with their poles." / "Day on the Glowseep: the moss goes dull, and the crews come in to sleep." (deep16/js/mines.js M.CREW, M.CREW_LINES, M.LINES.seep). 10-28 (the Glowseep fix seat, his 2i): the fire's box in his own words, "The Veterans keep Watch." (not the seat's); the sleep's line without "before dawn" ("You sleep by the crews' fire. Somebody comes in off the bog, and nobody wakes you."), and two wakings drafted for a long rest by the clock: "Day over the seep: the moss gone dull, and the crews in and asleep round the fire." / "Night over the seep: the moss lit, and the crews gone out with their poles."
entries.why: 10-21 night, his "run with its leans for all": the crew's names stay OPEN by his ruling (TarlynsPit/wiki/glowseep.md, held 09-09); the laugh is the realm's (Aurdin I, "And don't go into debt," all three laughing); Rillo's name the crews gave Aurdin (CANON 08-29); the wisp a dead colleague the crews won't chase (CANON 09-09). The seat's drafts; Griz's words set them. 10-28: sleep at the fire is eight hours on the clock (his "I can't repeatedly sleep to get back to night time"), so the party may wake by day or by night.

entries.what: THE WORLD's clock on the Glowseep's floor: an hour for every 150 squares walked and for every fight, a night at the crews' fire to the morning (a long rest with no watch); by night the floor's fights come twice as often, the stirges and the wisp weighing twice, the wisp only by night. The numbers in one place, deep16/js/mines.js M.SEEP (squaresPerHour, fightHours, nightRate, nightWeigh).
entries.why: 10-21 night, Griz: "possible watch-less camp location with roam (with associated timeslow) that allows player grinding", then "run with its leans for all, including the time-slowing but that might be adjusted". The seat's reading of his time-slow: the clock moves on the floor, slowly, so grinding costs days against his clock.

entries.what: Marko Thorne's greeting on the second game's counter (deep16/js/counter.js C.GREET): "Rope, tents, torches, lanterns. Arrows and bolts by the bundle." -- in place of the first game's "Rations, rope, tents, mules. Guards by the day: two gold a man.", which content/shops.json keeps for the first game.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz: "change line for now", on his "Gonna have to let the players hire fighters if we keep Marko's dialogue..." -- the second game hires out no guards; the line names only what his shelf sells (rope, tent, torch, lantern, arrows, bolts).

entries.what: Aurdin's side of Ned's scene, in his speech bubble on the second game's counter (deep16/js/counter.js C.NED_REPLIES): "Yes." / "No.", "Can I copy it from you?", "Because the components are fascinating?", "Deal.", "What did you want for that Find Familiar spell?" (his words), and the seat's drafts "One snake's tongue. Fresh.", "Fifty it is.", "Not now.", "We should get going."; Ned's new drafts beside them (C.NED_LINES): the fair copy for the silver ("Ned counts the silver twice, then slides a loose page out from under the jar labels -- the ritual, copied out fair in his own hand."), the page waiting in the pack ("That page wants to be in your book, not your pack. The rat has opinions about loose paper."), the job offered with no one to take it ("... Find one, and bring them along."), his familiar asked after by its kind ("How's the {kind}? Mine eats better than I do."), and his "Looks like you're learning without the classes." (Griz's words). The page itself is Sheet: Find Familiar (content/items.json sheet_findfamiliar), given as a story's end gives a sheet: "Received: Sheet: Find Familiar."
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz's notes on the scene (his ear file 0046Z, eyes-ned-familiar-1021e, "easy"): "Can we put Aurdin's portrait in the bottom left and have his text choices be in his speech bubble? ... where he'll say 'deal' instead of player clicking 'take it' / with quest taken Aurdin "what did you want for that find familiar spell?" instead of 'can i copy it" again / text should be same as fight end, where 'sheet: Find Familiar" or whatever is awarded ... some times Ned rips it out page (good) - hands him a copied page is good too, letting him copy out of book text is not" · "Not having harvester shouldn't prevent quest acceptance" · "Aurdin knows it - no spell talk:  Looks like you're learning without the classes - only asks about familiar by type if Aurdin has one with him".

entries.what: The second game's morning after a long rest (deep16/js/house.js H.Morning) opens on a card: "MORNING -- day N, <the hour>." over the first game's "Everyone wakes rested. HP and spells restored." and what the night did -- the first game wakes by a fade alone. The rest of the morning (THE NIGHT'S BONDS, THE DAY'S SPELLS, "Write down the day? (Save)") is the first game's own words; the same morning at camp on THE WORLD, at Cassia's inn and on Aldwin's floor.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz, on the house's row: "camping the night with no encounter doesn't prompt the same as 'you just stayed at inn' - can't tell it's morning, no bond-report or morning castings routines ran" -- the services seat's draft of the line that says it is morning.

entries.what: Korvin, keeper of the Hex's betting book, wears a slate-grey waistcoat (the palette's silver ramp) over his cream rolled-sleeve shirt, on his portrait and his town figure, his trousers brown. The art desk's ART-95 drew it brown, as Percy's is; the cutter dyes it at the cut (tools/portrait-sheet.py PEOPLE recolour). The colour was the seat's pick from the two the desk left open (slate grey or a dark blue); the brief never names one.
entries.why: The NPC cutter seat 10-22, his "Go for recolor without reroll" (the desk had found Percy his near-twin); slate judged in a 4x lineup beside Percy and Merrick, where a dark blue sank into the counter screen's navy.

entries.what: The Hex's third floor on the grid (deep16/js/hex.js HX.THIRD): the town meeting lounge's long council table under the Big Window, on a red rug, eight chairs; Urtusk's desk and an iron strongbox in his office; two weapon racks and a chest in the Armory. The rooms are the register's (TarlynsPit/wiki/the-hex.md, the third floor); what stands in them is the seat's draft.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz, on the Hex's floors: "1 - build all 3, where 3 can be just the meeting room and the offices upstairs and currently turned off for player access".

entries.what: The Hex's gambling floor on the grid (deep16/js/hex.js): a red rug round the ring, the owners' lounge on the south block on a blue rug with two benches along each face, four stools at each felt table, Vair's empty chair north of the north-east table.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz: "1 - build all 3"; the register's six felt tables, the south block's seating and Vair's chair (the-hex.md; the first game's hex2 `vairseat`).

entries.what: The Hex's ground floor on the grid (deep16/js/hex.js): Korvin's odds-board, a chalked slate on legs, standing beside him south of the sand; the contraband box an iron box at the south end of the east guard station; the premises (Mama's, the concession) walled in timber, their hatches shut behind shutters.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz: "2-3 - match the 8-bit and let me know where you have to vary" -- the first game's Korvin 'at the slate' (content/npcs.json korvinSlate); the register's stations and premises.

entries.what: Inside the Hex on the grid, Mama's premises and the cold-food concession are walled rooms with no way in: Mama trades from her booth outside (deep16/js/town.js T.MAMA), the concession has no keeper or name yet (Q41, held).
entries.why: 2026-10-22, the Hex interior seat; Griz 10-21 on Mama's door: "mama's shop may have to come out adjacent like the 8 bit did it".

entries.what: The Hex on the grid is entered by four doors: the south tip's double doors (the front), the north tip's (the back), and the single doors at the east and west faces' middles; each comes out on the town floor beside that door. The first game's Hex had the south doors only.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, the Hex interior seat: the register's openings (the-hex.md, 'Eight ground openings'); the premises' street door and window are not ways in.

entries.what: The Hex's spiral on its second floor (deep16/js/hex.js HX.stair): "The spiral winds down to the sand and on up to the third floor." -- DOWN / UP / STAY; UP is answered by the first game's own line (hex.warda) and the party stays.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz: "3 can be just the meeting room and the offices upstairs and currently turned off for player access".

entries.what: A Hex bout on the grid (deep16/js/hex.js HX.bout, HX.field): one hero on the Hex's own sand, a hexagon with two board tiers stepping up to a crowd of the town's plain folk, the party's other three at the rail nearest the hero; the simple screen by default and ON THE GRID the other way (Korvin's last question, FIGHT / ON THE GRID); no running; won 'THE ROOM ROARS.', lost 'DOWN ON THE SAND.'; a won bout's XP the fighter's alone (banked for the long rest in the house).
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz, to the seat's lean (a bout on the Hex's own sand, the crowd round it, the rest at the rail): "4 - let's see how that comes out"; 10-21: "sand is 'hex' fights, silverton internal".

entries.what: Once the party has killed three of the Wet's six crawlers (the Warrens' stock; R.WARN_AT, one knob), Skarn sends word down: Jory Slade, the mouth camp's crew boss, comes down the stalls' stair with a lit lantern, walks to the party, gives Skarn's word, and goes back up. He comes once, and only if the stock isn't all dead yet (deep16/js/roam.js R.lanternMan; flag herdWarned).
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz to the lanes desk: "There's also a 'send a warning with a lantern man' to warn them about culling the herd too much when they've killed (I think 3 out of 6 before trigger?)". The seat's pick of the man is the first game's jory (content/npcs.json, WarrensModule §4). The realm's clock has Skarn holding the lantern-token and sending it on when production falls, with dead stock bringing Thrane's hire of Dunmore's stable (TarlynsPit/wiki/the-warrens.md). The drafts stand, his to overrule.

entries.what: Jory Slade's words on the Wet (the counter screen, his name; the seat's drafts): "A lantern comes down the stalls' stair, and a man under it, picking his way round the wet." / "Jory Slade. Crew boss, up top. Skarn sent me down with the lamp." / "That's three of the stock you've put on the stone. Every one of them is a cradle's worth of thimbles nobody milks, and Edric writes the short against somebody's name." / "Down here they're stock, not quarry. One comes at you, give it room and walk on. That's Skarn's word, not mine: kill the herd and the man who owns it hears, and he doesn't send a lamp." / "Well?" WE'LL GIVE THEM ROOM -- "Good. Keep your light off the cradles; they come at a lamp." / THEY CAME AT US -- "They come at anybody. Walk round them. A dead one's a line in the book, and the book goes up the hill." / "Jory takes his lantern back up the stair." (deep16/js/roam.js R.JORY)
entries.why: 2026-10-22, the Wet seat, on his lantern man (wet-lantern-man): the first game has no such scene. The thimble, the book and Edric are the first game's (S.pen, S.edric); "the man who owns it" is Thrane, unnamed to the party.

entries.what: The Wet on the second game's own screens: the deep rate's counter screen named "The deep station: cradle N" with the plain shape where a face would go; the drained stair's fight set where the night crews come "down the daytime way" (crew boss, two thugs, two robbers on the floor); Katarina's Book opened on a floor gives its first line and "(Its pages read in the first game's book scene; the grid has no book screen yet.)"; any other field action with no rule gives the first game's "Nothing happens."; the show deep16/?wetshow, THE WET ON THE HOUSE, five beats each a NEW GAME staged with two torches in the pack.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, the Wet seat, on Griz's "yeah, work the wet": the first game's scenes (EV.deepRate, js/deep.js S.dryStair, S.holdStair, EV.useFieldItem) played on the grid with no hand-back to the 8-bit.
