entries.what: THE CRADLE on the second game's grid (deep16/js/cradle.js): the crawler in the cradle drawn in the grid's pixels at 480 x 270, a pale ringed body hunched behind the slats, the plum maw and its fangs, two eye stalks, eight red feelers pinned under the bar to their glands, a hanging lamp, the milker's hands and the thimble; its own words on a band under the work, "hold E, or the mouse on the gland -- let go in the gold. arrows or a click: another feeler" and "let go in the gold"; the place and the hands in two lines; the save's panel "CONSTITUTION SAVE -- DC 13" ("the draught: two, the higher kept"); the first game's own cradle lines (w.cradle.*, w.draw*) for the rest. The show deep16/?cradle (THE CRADLE, 10-22): a shift at the pens, the deep rate, WORK A SHIFT at pen two, the seed pinned.
entries.why: 2026-10-22, Griz to the lanes desk: "Crawler game needs rebuilt for this engine I suspect"; the desk's ruling with him away, the seat's lean 1: "build look 1, the DEEP16 scene of its own in the grid's pixels ... keep the first game's rules exactly ... Mouse first, keys as before" -- his eye on the show door the ruling on the look. The rules are the first game's js/cradle.js, number for number.

entries.what: VILAR'S FORGE-BOOTH, Silverton's Arena Plaza (the second game's town floor, deep16/js/town.js T.PINHOUSE): v6 puts the show-armorer's slot (pin 20) out in the open plaza among the stalls, 99 ft from any house, so he has a building of his own at his pin -- a forge-booth on Mama's pattern, 24 ft square under low blue slate, beside her booth by the Hex, its door in the south wall under the first game's sword sign. His room inside is the game's (T.TRADE shop:vilar).
entries.why: 10-22, the lanes desk's call standing for Griz's overrule (he is away): "a building of its own at each pin with its door in the south wall. Size each by what it is, per the wiki ... Vilar is the show-armorer (burned fingers), so a forge-booth on Mama's pattern (T.MAMA) fits"; on the desk's "A door goes on the keeper's own building, never the next house along". TarlynsPit/wiki/silverton-people.md 20, the-hex.md's fighter trade. (Was arena-plaza-booths, the house seat's first draft of both booths, 10-22.)

entries.what: DAVOS KREN'S LEECH-HOUSE, Silverton's Arena Plaza (the second game's town floor, deep16/js/town.js T.PINHOUSE): v6 puts the leech-house's slot (pin 21) out in the open plaza by its west side, 73 ft from the nearest shack, so it has a building of its own -- the arena's own surgery, a small house of red tile 60 by 50 ft round the room of cots the game builds behind its door (T.TRADE leech:davos), the pin a square inside its south wall, its door there under the first game's sign.
entries.why: 10-22, the lanes desk's call standing for Griz's overrule (he is away): "Davos Kren's leech-house is the arena's own surgery, which bought him out of indenture, so give it a small house with room for its cots, not a booth"; TarlynsPit/wiki/silverton-people.md 21, the-hex.md's fighter trade ("the arena's own surgery; the mother pays its bills").

entries.what: The Pocket DM's character sheet as a PDF (deep16/js/sheetpdf.js): the race traits' lines drafted from the SRD 5.1's (Darkvision, Fey Ancestry, the dwarf's and tiefling's Resilience, Dwarven Toughness, Relentless Endurance, Savage Attacks, Lupine Senses), the sheet's headings and pencil rows (ON THE DAY: current hit points, temporary, hit dice left, death saves), and the skills note: the Pocket DM keeps the skills its fights read, the rest stand at the ability's modifier with an empty circle for the table to mark.
entries.why: 10-26, Griz: "Somewhere in the pocket DM - reference user interface best practices - players should be able to save pdf of character sheet"; the seat's drafts, standing (RULED 09-24, no [GRIZ] stubs).

entries.what: The Company on the second game (deep16/js/company.js): NEW GAME's pick and its question are the first game's (js/scenes.js LeadSelect, its own words), the opening's three pages its text.json intro.world, intro.<lead> and intro.motive -- its fourth, the 8-bit's keys, left for the floor's own first card; each hire the first game's scene and terms on the counter screen, the hero's face where a keeper's portrait stands (Aurdin's portrait at twice its size, the others their own figure at three times), the place named on it (The Hex, Vice row, Aldwin's mission chapel) and the JOURNAL's step under it; Barley's bout labelled BARLEY, ON THE CARD TONIGHT, its card opening on the first game's hire.barleyBout, FIGHT or ON THE GRID asked as Korvin's slate asks it; Vivian and Aurdin standing on the street in their own figures (the first game's look for each), not the street's stand-in; the one hired joining where they stood; a pinned Company step's marker over the one it wants, or on the way (the Hex's front doors, a room's door, the Hex's spiral or its front doors).
entries.why: 10-28, Griz: "Getting to the point we need to add the select character part to 'new game' and restore the 8 bit missions to form the party"; "Barley and Lyman should be restored during the restoration of the company mission from the first game"; "what part of cloning the 8 bit beginning mission need discuss?" -- the opening seat's calls where the clone met the grid

entries.what: MARTA VENN'S COOK-STALL, Silverton's Arena Plaza (the second game's town floor, deep16/js/town.js T.STALL, T.lay): a market stall of her own, two squares wide, on the ground south of where she stands at her slot (pin 22, the cook-stalls), she behind it facing the plaza; the crates that stood round her cleared off. E at the stall, or a click on it, is a word with her across it.
entries.why: Griz, 10-28 (his ear file 0258Z, on eyes-doors-walls-1022): "she needs a vender stall rather than a crate". The realm's slot 22 is her cook-stalls (silverton-people.md, the-venns.md); the stall's shape is the seat's (the town's market stall, as Fountain Street's).

entries.what: MARTA'S HOT MEAL (the second game's counter, deep16/js/counter.js C.meal): every day at her stall, after the bat wings if any, A HOT MEAL -- a silver a head for those standing, Vivian free at her mother's stall -- eaten where it is bought: each one who eats with a level of exhaustion sheds one (the SRD's six, the fourth's halved hit points given back below it); with nobody worn it is supper and no more, and her offer says so before a coin goes down. Her lines are the seat's drafts: "A hot meal off the fire, eaten here: {cost}.", "Somebody's dragging. Hot food takes the edge off.", "Nobody here's dragging. It's supper, no more."; the served card "Bowls of her stew, bread to wipe them, eaten standing at the stall.", "{name} is less worn (exhausted {n}).", "{name} eats the weariness off: not exhausted now.", "Warm and fed."
entries.why: Griz, 10-28 (his ear file 0258Z): "Viv's mom should sell some food item regularly that functions as if it were used when it were bought - like 'hot meal' that clears a level of exhaustion or something". The price is the SRD's modest meals (3 sp a day), a meal of the three; Vivian free and the no-exhaustion supper are the seat's plain calls (the lane's leans).

entries.what: THE EDIFICE FROM ABOVE on Silverton's town floor (deep16/js/topview.js TV.edStrip; js/town.js def.edifice): drawn by code as the building, not the cliff -- the facade 45 ft by the houses' measure (a two-floor house's face is 20), dressed ashlar in courses with two string courses at 15 and 30 ft, pilasters every 24 ft, an arcade's arch in every fourth bay at its foot (tops at 15 ft), a window to each bay on the second and third floors, merlons along the top; the vault's great arch at the middle (v6's 128 ft) with the two doors (planks, a dark X of braces, a gold ring on a dark boss); a spout at 12 ft over each of v6's fountains, its water down the wall to a basin lip; the roof skylight glass in 12 ft panes with a stone rim and merlons along its front, the orchard under it a tree to every 20 ft in rows, the falls run down the middle in a channel, the Sunshaft's round west of it. Its squares stay closed rock to the rules.
entries.why: Griz, 10-28 (his ear file 0336Z): "edifice looks like a mountain flattened at 10 ft tall". The realm's deepholm-and-the-edifice.md ("The face, as the game builds it", PROPOSED 10-04/10-05): three floors of 15 ft, arches every four columns, the fountains along the wall, the two vault doors, the skylight roof with rim and merlons over the orchard, the falls through the middle. The bay widths, the windows and the orchard's rows are the seat's.

entries.what: THE HEX'S TWO HATCHES ON THE GRID (deep16/js/hex.js HX.PEOPLE; deep16/js/counter.js C.SCRIPTS.hatch, C.SHOP16): Higertha stands behind Mama's hatch onto the concourse (open, a board sill, its shutters back) in the druid's figure, and sells Mama's shelves through it -- no words of hers (she is the register's reserved), only the scene's line "Higertha works Mama's hatch onto the concourse, the jars on the shelf behind her."; a hired town youth behind the cold-food concession's hatch ("A town youth on the concession's hatch: cold pies, a silver apiece.") sells Bat-Wing Pies cold at a silver each, buying nothing -- its shelf titled 'The Cold-Food Concession' (a description, not a name: its name is held, Q41).
entries.why: Griz, 10-28 (his ear file 0336Z): "we need Higertha in the window on mama's side and consider a concessions vendor". The realm's the-hex.md: Higertha works the arena-side window, a serving hatch onto the concourse (CANON 09-13); the concession the house's not-hot side, entered only from inside, a serving hatch, hired town youths (CANON 09-13, 09-16b). The pies and their price, and selling Mama's shelves at the hatch, are the seat's plain calls.

entries.what: THE HEX'S THIRD FLOOR OPEN ON THE GRID (deep16/js/hex.js HX.stair, HX.PEOPLE[3], HX.LINES.warda3): the second floor's spiral UP goes up to it -- the council's lounge under the Big Window, Urtusk's office, the Armory, walked -- with no outside stairs; the inside balcony and its rooms stay shut, Warda's; Warda stands in the lounge on an ordinary day (moved up from the ground floor's spirals, where the first game had her keep the stairs), her line the first game's turned to the open stairs: "Warda keeps the third floor and the ring of keys. The rooms round the balcony are not for you."
entries.why: Griz, 10-28: "The third floor problem is the outside stairs 3rd floor and there's no reason the player can't go up to the town meeting and urtusk office 3rd floor"; then "we don't need to add the outside stairs unless we use the hex in a combat map, since we're not really adding those services to the game... consider if we should have NPC on the 3rd floor where the council meet when it's not a council meeting though". Warda as that NPC is the seat's lean (the-urtusks.md: she keeps the third floor and the ring of keys).

entries.what: THE FIGHTERS' STABLES, Silverton (Venn Hale): Wretch Bloodsnout's compound itself, its own gate in its west wall on the plaza side the stables' door (since 10-28 later; the door at pin 19 gone, his "this sounds like the compound was moved instead of moving the door to the compound") and the room in through it the compound at true scale, 115 by 90 ft (23 x 18 squares) -- its stone wall, the barracks along its back (east, 25 ft deep) with two ways in through its wall and fourteen cots, the master's house in the yard's north-west corner, training rails and weights in the beaten-earth yard, and Venn Hale at a short table across the yard's head; in by the gate from the plaza facing east, out facing the plaza. (deep16/js/town.js T.DOORS `gate`, T.lay, T.TRADE keeper:venhale `doorSide`, T.room's `compound` dress) SUPERSEDED 10-28 later on his word ("re pin 19 - the case is most likely that i confused Venn Hale and forgot he's the human fighter slaver and have had him moved into bloodsnouts camp / if 19 on the fullsize map is enough to house his slaves and just looks small on the 30ft shrinkage, restore 19 to before my confusion"): pin 19's house at v6's true scale is 68.7 x 57.2 ft, two floors; the stables are there again, Venn Hale's door at it with no room behind it, and the compound is Bloodsnout's own, its gate shut (his 10-20 "drawn but not enterable", the desk's call). The room laid for the compound is kept, unwired: deep16/js/town.js T.TRADE compound:bloodsnout (its table no one's yet).
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Wouldn't the fighters stables be the compound we added (venn hale)"; RULED "compound as room". The yard's furniture is the seat's draft from the-hex.md's "barracks and training yards, part gymnasium, part debtors' prison". The fold: the place is Bloodsnout's compound (bloodsnout-compound); this line's barracks, cots, master's house and rails describe its inside when he opens it.

entries.what: The Warrens' mouth camp: the bunkhouse's door hangs the first game's bed sign, its mouseover "The Bunkhouse: a flop for the night" and the night's price ("A bunk for the night, 1 sp (a silver for a stranger)", or free to crew); the Pellam barns "The Pellam Barns: bunks for the day-crews"; the mouth camp's first card names the bunkhouse and its price, and its counter is headed by that name. (deep16/js/mines.js M.INNS names, M.priceLine, M.bunkLine)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "I didn't finish a shift but the available doors didn't look or talk about flophouse so I went back outside and camped". Connective words, the seat's draft.

entries.what: The second game's JOURNAL keeps a line of its own once Warrens Pete has talked of the Warrens (on the street or in the Hex: heardWarrens; or the rumor's heardPete, or the camp reached -- his "Talking to a 'nearby start' NPC to add the things to the journal, not just in there without trigger. i.e. warrens pete"): THE CRAWLER WARRENS -- "Across the river, the Crawler Warrens: the mouth camp, where the cradles take hands on by the shift and the bunkhouse gives a bed for the night.", NEXT "The feed track: walk off Silverton's east edge where it leaves the town, over the bridge to the mouth camp. The town map (L) marks it."; done once Edric Pellam has the party in his book (tallyMet). The town map (L) marks the feed track's squares at the east edge in gold and labels them THE WARRENS. (deep16/js/counter.js C.OWN_QUESTS warrens; js/roam.js R.paintMap)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "having a difficult time figuring out how to get to the warrens". The seat's draft.

entries.what: A bout lost on the Hex's sand (Korvin's card, and Barley's at his hire): the one who fell is stitched to half their hit points on the house, and the party is out of the Hex on the threshold of Davos Kren's leech-house, facing his door, with the card "Davos Kren's door: out of the Hex with {name}, stitched and standing ({hp}/{max})." (deep16/js/hex.js HX.toDavos)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "kick the party to krenn if a fighter falls (out of the hex and at his shop door - but already serviced)". Half as Davos stitches a fallen hero for his five (C.leech). The card's words are the seat's draft.

entries.what: A second game NEW GAME with one lead starts them where their page puts them, not at the west gate: Aurdin on the square outside Aldwin's mission chapel where he stands to be hired; Vivian in front of her mother Marta Venn's cook-stall, facing it; Lymen before Papa Urtusk at the Hex's front doors, facing him; Barley at the door of Kess's flop-cellars on the Shaft Rows, facing it. (deep16/js/company.js CO.START, CO.startAt)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Aurdin should start near where the story says he slept. Vivian should start near her mom's stall. Lymen in front of Urtusk and Barley near kess."

entries.what: Under a roost (the Guano Galleries' working gallery and dens), the Light (and Daylight) cast from the menu is refused -- "The roost overhead: no bright light. The Light would spook the roost." -- as no torch is lit there; a Light carried in is let go at the floor's door as before, one cast in a fight there brings the roof down as before, and any Light a fight hands back is let go on the floor (a backstop); Dancing Lights, dim, is lawful there (RULED 09-28). (deep16/js/roam.js R.menuAct, the pull-in's hand-back) 10-28 later (the grid seat, mode=gridlight1028): the refusal now holds by the mouse -- the menu hands the spell itself, not its id, and the menu's Light was being cast under the roost -- and a Light let go at the roost's door is let go off the sheet too (it came back when the party left the roost). 10-28 night: the refusal is gone -- his "the party has to cast it inside after to shame fail": cast inside, the roof comes down (ottilie-mouth-lights). 10-28 night, later: oil thrown under a roost catches -- "<name> throws the Oil Flask. It catches, under the roost." -- and the roof comes down ("Fire under a roosted ceiling."), as the first game; no longer greyed (his "2 - as the first game"; deep16/js/oil.js).
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "check 'light' being cast in battle or from the menu carrying over to whether they can go in the guano mines".

entries.what: SILVERTON'S EAST ROAD SPLITS outside the east gate: a thin track north along the stockade's outside to the feed track's corner (the bridge and the Warrens' mouth camp), and the road out bending south-south-east to the farms and the fishing coast; the way to the Pit is back out through the west. On the world map the east gate's way is south-east. (deep16/js/town.js T.EAST; deep16/js/world.js W.DOORS.silverton)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "the 'east' road could split a thinner track that runs to the galleries map and aim more sse as the road out", "warrens mouth, not the guano mine, sorry", "8 yes, down to the pit is back out through the west"

entries.what: THE WARRENS ON THE REALM HEX MAP: the mouth camp a place at environs v3's spot (122.34, 28.43 mi), on a bench along the river's north bank some 100 ft over the water (330 to 300 ft, the six mouths at its back rising up the chain's face to about 500, the crook at 2,570 above); the feed track a track from Silverton down the south bank to the bridge (tools/hexmap.js seedSilverton, the lift v-warrens and the path feedtrack)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "adjust the elevations around silverton and the warrens to fit the wiki re altitudes", then "you're good to move and reshape things to add realism that fits the wiki" and "9 yes"

entries.what: THE HEIGHTS ROUND SILVERTON on the second game's world map (the realm names no feet): the Edifice's gate about 770 ft, the town falling south to the Hex about 670 and its south edge 650, the road west over a shoulder about 830 a mile out and down into his trough along the range's foot; the river from about 240 at its head down to the sea, never climbing (tools/hexmap.js buildBeds, cityOn; his two sinks beside the town moved 3 mi west) -- 10-28b: the sinks went on to 3 mi SOUTH-WEST instead, into his trough's floor (3 mi west had sunk the black range behind the town); the shoulder now about 1,130 a mile out
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "adjust the elevations around silverton and the warrens to fit the wiki re altitudes"; "1 - show me what's there now, they're probably just me being sloppy, and I think you're good to move and reshape things to add realism that fits the wiki (2-4)"; then on the first seed in his browser, "hex map link makes it look like all the mountains behind silverton have been flattened"

entries.what: The second game's JOURNAL holds nothing at NEW GAME; each mission opens on the word that names it (a talk branch's set, or a rumour that points at work: r-pete The Missing Five, r-doserate and r-mouths The Cradles, r-guanowages and r-roost The Cull, r-cloaker and its two The Forty-Gold Tail, r-hexcard r-talmok r-fronted Fight Night, r-winters Finding Work), townsfolk saying their rumours in turn into THE TALK; the moment one opens a card says so in plain words (In your JOURNAL: <name>. <its words>) and the first opened is pinned when nothing is; a save from before keeps its JOURNAL as it stood, no cards; the Snoot's news (r-snoot) only from the first morning after the moot. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.MISSIONS, H16.missionCard, C.RUMOR_OPENS; deep16/js/counter.js C.words, C.quests)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Talking to a 'nearby start' NPC to add the things to the journal, not just in there without trigger. i.e. warrens pete"; "Batch with NPC texts mapping to pinnable rumor missions"; on the lane's 5, "yes, but 'spoken words fill' sounds too full if we add better dialogue, the way 'the talk' section currently works is good". The cards' words and the missions' plain lines are the story window's drafts.

entries.what: Pete's Five in the second game is THE MISSING FIVE, taking in the Crawler Warrens line: Warrens Pete's word opens it, its first waypoint Edric Pellam at the tally-house with the way there in words (the feed track off the east edge, over the bridge), then Skarn, then the flooded stair; done when the five's tokens come home. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.MISSIONS warrens)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "talking to pete makes 'the missing 5' a journal that points to the booking guy on the surface at the cradles as first waypoint"; the name RULED on his "15 yes".

entries.what: FINDING WORK, a mission that fills: each word that names a place of work adds it (Winters' papers on Fountain Street, Hessle's board at the Weigh-House, the Warrens' cradles over the bridge, Korvin's slate in the Hex), in the order heard; done the moment the party takes up any one -- WORK from Winters, the board read, Edric's book, a bout -- whose own mission is in the JOURNAL by then. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.WORK; deep16/js/counter.js C.flagOn)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "talking to nearby NPCs opens 'finding work' quest to talk to winters about work (or point to the bounty board, or crawler milking or fighting at the hex) as appropriate"; on the lane's 7, "sounds like an AND when we should make it an OR. Finding work as a quest fills up with options as you talk to various NPC, getting a quest from where it points (winters, the board) completes the finding work quest. Board adds each entry as pinnable area pointer mission in journal".

entries.what: The first time the party comes up to the Hex's front door, Lymen (Warda's youngest, in show-armorer's chain) is in the door talking up at Papa Urtusk: gnolls on the road at night north of the Gulch where they never come, the Dominion's wagons down there talking to them all summer, nobody going to look -- he will, and he'll find people who'll stand up; Papa: 'Alone.', then to the party 'There's a few standing about'; Lymen: make a name first and find him in the Hex; Papa names where Barley, Marta's girl and the farm boy with a spellbook are, and the four kinds of work ('Winters pays for honest legs. Hessle's board pays for brave ones. The Warrens pay for strong backs. The sand pays for fools.'). With Lymen leading, Lymen himself in the door, and Papa: 'Then go and find some.' The Company opens on it, pinned, and Finding Work. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.papaScene)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Have Urtusk and Lymen being Lymen telling Urtusk about finding friends to investigate the rumblings about gnolls on the road and activate company as active quest"; RULED on the lane's 6, "yes". Every line the story window's draft (the no-stubs law, RULED 09-24).

entries.what: Beside each lead's start, a word that puts Finding Work in the JOURNAL: Aldwin in his chapel (Aurdin's start) -- Ambrose Winters pays for honest legs, tell him the chapel sent you; Marta at her stall (Vivian's) -- 'You're up. Eat.' and work Hessle's board, where she can hear about it; Kess at her door (Barley's) -- the Warrens take anyone with two hands, a silver the thimble; and Papa's for Lymen. Papa's own word after: 'Make a name. Then they'll follow you.', with the four 'Four of you. Bring them back.' (deep16/js/hours.js C.TALK16)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "talking to nearby NPCs opens 'finding work' quest"; RULED on the lane's 7. The lines the story window's drafts.

entries.what: Lucia, who is Mama, speaks as 'I' at her counter: her opener the first that holds -- the morning after the moot, once, the Pit's word up her back stairs and 'Then it was never the gnolls they were after.' (the realm's own line); a hero worn, eat first at Marta's; her first word to each lead (Aurdin the calling herbs are hers alone; Barley the whole Hex saw him get up against Cutter; Vivian 'Marta's girl. Urtusk's rules hold at my counter too.'; Lymen 'You took your oath alone. Now you want company for it. Good.'); Lymen in the party, 'Find ones who duck.'; else 'I mix. Higertha sells at the hatch, in the Hex. What hurts?' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.LUCIA)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Mama should have more starter character specific and current game state specific opening texts and possible interactions"; "Lucia wouldn't say "mama mixes" she'd say "I mix" if that was her line"; RULED on the lane's 8, "yes". The news line's second sentence is TarlynsPit/wiki/campaign-start.md's (CANON 08-25); the rest the story window's drafts.

entries.what: CONSULT at Mama's counter, free: Lucia looks the party over and names one fix a hurt -- a hero down to Davos Kren's door, poison to her antitoxin, a worn hero to Marta's hot meal and a night's sleep, a bad bleed to a healing potion or a night at Cassia's, a cut to an hour's rest; nothing wrong, 'Nothing I can fix. Go and get hurt properly.' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.consult)
entries.why: His note's 'possible interactions'; the shop card's own word, CONSULT LUCIA (RULED 09-02); RULED on the lane's 8, "yes".

entries.what: Sylvia Swann's booth: a draped table, a cup of tea going cold, an owl that watches your hands; READ for 5 sp -- her line for the mission she reads, then its next step in plain words; nothing pinned, she pins the first open mission, and with none open opens the first work not yet heard; nothing left, 'The cup's dry. Come back when the town's moved.' and no silver; from the first morning after the moot, once, 'An old thing walks. Not your business yet.' No reading names the Tower. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.SWANN)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Swann dialogue pointing to next quest or upcoming part of existing quest for 5 sp - consult story wiki for timeline on when she reads the old one's presence"; RULED on the lane's 9, "yes, in the case of no pinned messages a consult will pin one first". The register: her reading fired at the moot through the object on Gnash (TarlynsPit/wiki/the-wizard-networks.md, CANON 09-16/16b); her cap RULED 08-29g. Her lines the story window's drafts.

entries.what: The night of the first day after the moot the Weigh-House lamp burns past the fourth bell and the council sits on the Hex's third floor: Hessle gives the Pit's word (the gnoll king dead at the moot by Dominion hands, their wagons gone south); Merrick, 'There's more coming up that road. Don't ask me how I know.'; Androit posts fifty gold for true word of the gnolls, sworn before him, and ten a fortnight for a watch kept on the road; Ottak Harrow, 'Post it twice.'; Hessle's 'a hundred for a Lupine's head --', Papa's 'Strike it. We pay for word.' Played to the player at the party's next long rest from that dusk, wherever they sleep; the morning after, the paper is on Hessle's board (before it the board has no Snoot paper and Hessle's word no notice). (deep16/js/hours.js H16.COUNCIL.notice, D.house.morning; deep16/js/counter.js C.noticeUp) RE-CUT 10-30 (the story seat, on his word): the Lupine-head exchange cut (Hessle's 'And a hundred for a Lupine's head --', Papa's 'Strike it. We pay for word.', 'Struck.'); the night tells the news from the Pit -- Hessle 'Word's come up the road from Tarlyn's Pit, where Newland's patrols stop. Every gnoll tribe in the hills met at the full moon, for a moot.' / Androit 'Plainly, for the record. Gnolls are the hyena-folk of the hills down the road, and a moot is all their tribes together under one king.' / Hessle 'The Dominion killed that king at the moot. Gnash the Gnarled, a hundred years under their Mane, and the Dominion's wagons gone before he was cold.' / Androit 'So they've gone Snoot. With no king, the Mane goes to whoever wins the most glory, and to a gnoll glory is killing: the most savage of them will be king. The last time a king died, the histories say --' / Papa 'Enough history, Aldwyn. They'll come up the road for their glory. What do we do?' / Merrick, Androit's notice and Harrow as before. Androit the explicit one (the realm's 'historian fella', who wants the history written down true), Papa the brusque.
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "consider 3rd floor council cut scenes in various appropriate places"; RULED "Consider C1 a cutscene that plays for the player at the parties nearest (chronological) rest cycle". The realm's own Day-1 beat (TarlynsPit/wiki/campaign-start.md, CANON 08-25); the lines the story window's drafts. 10-30, Griz: "we're wasting expository space. What actually came in from newland? Summed up as 'all the tribes gathered for a moot, and now they've gone snoot - most savage as the new gnoll king' - spin up a seat to write the scripting - someone at the table that likes things explicit clarifying what's there vague for people that have never heard of gnolls, someone brusk cutting them off and keeping things moving?" The cut is his own 08-25 ruling in the realm (S1-22; the 08-25 story's footer item 22); the news is the realm's (campaign-start, the-snoot, gnoll-hills).

entries.what: When the lantern man has come down the Wet (the party's third of the House's six crawlers killed), the council sits again that night: the east side's man -- 'Somebody is culling a herd that isn't theirs.' -- Casper Venn ('Ask what they went for'), Hessle (the board fines no one), Papa ('A warning's gone down. Once. Next.'); and if the whole stock dies, again: the House hires the Captain's line to hold the mouth camp and the bridge, Androit swears it, Papa: 'Then they'll hold a bridge over an empty pen.' Each at the party's next long rest; Hessle's word on the five after says the council sat only if it did. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.COUNCIL.herd, .stock)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "C3 is that any crawler kill trigger or the thinning the herd too much amount"; "18 - yes, lantern warning same trigger as council meeting". The lines the story window's drafts.

entries.what: Once the party has made a name (renown 2): in the Hex a Hex boy runs up, 'Papa wants you on the third floor'; up the spiral the council at the long table looks them over, a line each saying who they are and what they do -- Androit's seal, Hessle's scales, Casper Venn's coin, Ottak Harrow's farms south of the river, Merrick's window -- and Papa: 'They've seen you. That's all this was. Go on.' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.COUNCIL.looks) RE-CUT 10-29 (the story window, RULED, his "Leans stand" on his NOTES "Council looking you over dialogue seems same text as store-walk - why is the council taking a look at them, if not disappoint why not quest (true word gnolls?)"): the who's-who cut; Papa 'These are the ones I told you about. They take work, and they come back from it.', Harrow 'Every wagon out of Silverton goes south through Web Gulch, and there's an ettercap strung across the far end of it.', Hessle 'Forty gold on my board for it, and ten more since it snared a lad. Nobody has collected.', Androit 'Then it's sworn before me: the gulch cleared, and its fangs brought to Hessle's scales. It's yours, if you'll take it.', Merrick 'After the gulch, the road north, where the gnolls are. When it's time, we'll send for you again.', Papa 'That's what this was. Go on.'; The Braiding Ettercap opened and pinned; the call a Hex boy of his own (hexboy-runner-1029). 10-29 night (the story seat): Warda speaks first on her own face, 'This is the group you asked about, Papa.' (his own words), and Papa after her, 'That's them. They take work, and they come back from it.'; Merrick's last line 'After the gulch, the gnolls. They're coming north up that same road, out of the south. When it's time, we'll send for you again.' (was 'After the gulch, the road north, where the gnolls are.')
entries.why: The lane's C2, RULED 10-28, his "17 - yeah, that's good": a who's-who of the council for new players. The lines the story window's drafts. 10-29 night, Griz: "if warda has a portrait - warda shows you should be portrait version 'this is the group you asked about papa'"; "gnolls are coming up north along the south of silverton road (north road would point to the doors)".

entries.what: Silverton keeps THE WORLD's clock on its street: an hour each 15,000 ft walked (500 squares at the town's 30 ft), a Hex bout a quarter hour, a bed to the morning, and WAIT (the M menu, after NOTES or SAVE, on the street) to the next bell; only the band's word is shown (the HUD: '..., dusk'; WAIT: 'The bells go for midday.'). The street is laid again at four turns -- early (dawn, morning), day, dusk, night -- with a card at each ('The bells go for dawn. Silverton wakes: the stalls open, and the bread line forms at Aldwin's.'; 'The bells go for dusk. The town comes out ...'; 'Night. The streets empty; the Hex and vice row stay lit.'). What players use is open at every hour, and the four hires stand at their spots at every hour; the keepers whose counters do nothing yet (Marin Voss, Venn the barber, Mela Sorris, Venn Hale, Aldric Vest, Merrick, Tam Vere) are out at an evening spot of their own at dusk, their doors and signs 'Closed.' at dusk and by night (Falstaff's too); Warrens Pete off the street to the Hex's bar from dusk; Gull at the Rows' end, Kael at his yard's side gate, Old Hob by Kess's cellars from dusk; Brennock at Marta's at dusk; the boy, the girl, the factor's man, the warehouse clerk, Idony and the rope-maker home by night. One table (H16.STREET, EVENING, SHUT) with room for a festival's set over it (H16.SETS). (deep16/js/hours.js)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Giving silverton time means shop hours and 'where should NPCs be when'"; RULED on the lane's 1-4, 11-14: "1 - I'm onboard", "2 - basically the stuff the players actually use almost always open, with the shops the players are unlikely to use (or haven't been built yet, wagons and weighing stuff come to mind) where those shop keeps roam around town during the evening - breadline in the morning in the slums stuff, prep for what we'll do when the festival is in town - mouseover just 'closed' if closed", "3 - easier to make the party collection a time independent exception to hours of operation", "4 - yes", "11 leans agreed", "12 agree to script walkings later", "14 yes"; his 10-21 "step-clock will be lenient in towns". The spots, the rate and the cards the story window's drafts.

entries.what: Silverton by night: a dark wash over the street, cut away in pools of light at the lit places -- the Hex's four doors, vice row's booth, Percy's and Tam's doors, Merrick's lantern house, Cassia's inn, Aldwin's chapel, Davos Kren's door, the west gate -- and round the party, warm at the lamps; the Weigh-House lamp lit on a night the council sits; at dusk a warm wash. Drawn over the street under the HUD, not as the floor's dark (the town's top view draws a dark floor black). (deep16/js/hours.js H16.paintNight)
entries.why: RULED on the lane's 4, "4 - yes" (night on the floor, the lit places drawn, nothing new to fight). The look the story window's draft, for his eye.

entries.what: Aldwin's bread line: in the early hours a line of four of the Rows' people at the mission chapel's door ('Bread at six. Don't push.'), and Aldwin hands the party a loaf a hero, once a morning: Mission Bread, the second game's own thing (the SRD's day of rations as a loaf), eaten out of a fight for 1d2 hit points. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.BREAD, missionbread)
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "breadline in the morning in the slums stuff"; "13 yes, he'd give 4 to the party token". The 1d2 is the story window's, his to overrule.

entries.what: The second game's words pass for new and younger players: a person keeps their own voice and the card that opens a mission says plainly what and where; the lines that sent a player nowhere they could go or priced what the game doesn't sell said plainly on the second game's side -- Old Hob ('I milk the crawlers at the cradles, across the water ... that's what dosed means'), Kael (ladders and poles for the shafts, no prices), Vera (what's stolen turns up at her door or Kessler's, sell to him), Merrick (word by the lantern network; a noon sending tells everyone it's urgent), Venn Hale (fight? Korvin's slate in the Hex is where you put your name down), and Lymen's 'Make a name first' with where a name comes from (Finding Work, in the JOURNAL). The first game keeps its own words. (deep16/js/hours.js C.TALK16, H16.TEXT) 10-29 night (the story seat): Vera's line re-cut, 'Nothing on my table is for strangers, and I don't buy from them. Kessler, the pawnbroker on Fountain Street, buys: sell to him, not me.'
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "Dialogue review for vaguery reduction for new and younger players"; the lane's 4.9, RULED with the rest. The lines the story window's drafts. 10-29 night, Griz: "vera doesn't actually sell and claims to".

entries.what: The second game's field Light (THE WORLD's M menu and a house floor's): WHO CARRIES IT? asks whose gear it touches, a card clicked; the words "<caster>'s Light on <name>'s gear: bright 20 ft and dim 20 more, for an hour." (or "<caster>'s own gear") before the first game's g.light; it lasts an hour on THE WORLD's clock (until), and "<name>'s Light goes out: its hour is up." when the clock passes it on THE WORLD's walk, its AN HOUR, after a road fight, on Silverton's street and on the Glowseep; cast again, the caster's earlier Light ends, in a fight too. A Light cast in a house fight takes its hour from the hand-back. The first game's menu unchanged (its Light a line). (js/menu.js MagicPage; deep16/js/house.js FD.cast, H.lightsOut; deep16/js/roam.js R.lasting) 10-28 night: the hour RULED (his "now that there's a clock, SRD"). Daylight is not asked: SRD 5.1's sphere on what the caster holds, bright 60 ft and dim 60 more, an hour, its 3rd-level slot spent (his "5- fix": it had landed as a Light, 20 ft, and free) -- "<caster>'s Daylight on what <caster> holds: bright 60 ft and dim 60 more, for an hour."
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "i need a grid seat to check how we're doing the out-of-combat casting of light via the menu on the world map and on roams. it doesn't seem to choose a target or impact entering the guano mines". SRD 5.1 Light: "You touch one object", "Duration: 1 hour", "The spell ends if you cast it again". The 10-20 ruling's long rest (his "that seems aligned with SRD") stood in for the hour while the game had no clock; the long rest still ends it. The words are the seat's.

entries.what: When the council sits -- the night the Pit's word comes or the herd's council's night, from dusk, or the party called up at renown 2 -- the Hex's third floor seats them at the long table under the Big Window: Papa at the head of the north side, Androit and Hessle beside him, Casper Venn and Ottak Harrow at the ends, Merrick across the table when word from outside matters, the east side's man across for the herd; in their own figures where they have them. The party that climbs up sees them there on the map's camera, the camera along the table and a card (C2's 'The council sits at the long table under the Big Window. Warda shows the party in, and nobody tells them to sit.'; a council's night 'The scales are lit ... Warda at the lounge door: "Stand at the back. Say nothing."', once a night), before C2's portraits; after C2 they break up and Papa goes back down to his door. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.TABLE)
entries.why: Griz 10-28, on the window's four calls (the sittings as portraits among them): "yes but a scene at start or between that shows them on the 3rd floor". Who sits where and the cards the story window's drafts.

entries.what: At the Guano Galleries' mouth Ottilie stops every bright light burning on the party -- a Light or a Daylight on someone, a torch lit in a hand -- beside what is always lit (the first game's): "<names>. I can see that light on you from my stool. Let it go before you go in -- it would spook the roost." / "<names>. Put that torch out. Nobody carries fire under the roost." / "Put it out, or turn around." -- PUT IT OUT (the spell let go, the torch put out and spent) or TURN BACK; then "Dark, then. Go on -- and do not touch the roost." A lantern goes by, lawful hood down (RULED 09-29). A Light or Daylight cast inside under the roost is the roost's law broken: the run ends as the first game's RoostFail (NOT THIS KIND OF NAME), no longer refused. (deep16/js/mines.js M.burning, M.roostDoor, M.LINES.ottilie*; deep16/js/roam.js R.menuAct) 10-28 night, later: a lantern or the Ledger-Lamp lit hood up is not stopped -- Ottilie: "<names>. That lantern -- hood it down. Low and dim, or the roost wakes.", the hood lowered, "Low like that. Go on." -- and it goes down in the same hand (his "3 - if they have a hooded lantern and the hood not down, ottilie will interact and the hood will end up lowered, then he'll let them by"); a hood already down goes by unspoken (RULED 09-29). A lantern in hand is the pack's at every hand-back now (it was lost between floors) and the mines' next floor takes it up again (deep16/js/mines.js M.go; deep16/js/house.js H.fromFloor).
entries.why: Griz 10-28 night: "Ottille stops light violations at the entrance, the party has to cast it inside after to shame fail". Her words are the seat's drafts on the first game's (g1.ottilieLightWield, g1.ottilieLightAsk).

entries.what: Web Gulch on the second game's grid (deep16/js/gulch.js, the seat's draft for his paint later): a cut 40 x 112 squares, north up, the Pit road down its bed -- in from the fork's end at the north mouth, out toward the Halfway Inn at the south, bending a little east going south as his road does -- rock banks either side; the silk-cutters' camp (two tents, a fire, crates) just inside the north mouth west of the road, with their descent down the west bank; the webs harvested along the bed's sides, thickest near the camp and going south; the snared lad between two stunted trees off the road on the east side midway; the strung end, a side gully off the west bank near the south mouth with the ettercap's shelf at its back and a potion beside it; a path up the east bank midway; two healer's kits in a nook off the east bank.
entries.why: Griz 10-28: "I think we're ready to build the gulch roam. The 8bit one wasn't bad, but we want this one to slow down time progression greatly (compared to road) and run basically N-S ish like it looks like on the map (8 bit was kinda east to west)"; the seat's five leans, his "Gulch's leans look good". The first game's beats laid N-S along the 10-20 seed's line (seeded.gulch1020; wiki/web-gulch.md).

entries.what: Web Gulch's clock and hours on the grid: 300 squares walked are an hour of THE WORLD's clock (the Glowseep's 150, Silverton's 500), a fight fifteen minutes; the silk-cutter out at the near webs and the drummer boy drumming 11:00 to 14:00, at their camp otherwise and by their fire at night; the spider table's count between fights doubled at noon (half as often) and halved by night (twice as often); the gulch dark by night, the cutters' fire lit; no bed and no SAVE in it (the first game's gulch saved none).
entries.why: Griz 10-28, his leans 2, 4 and 5 ("Gulch's leans look good"); the realm's noon: silk-cutters work at noon when the spiders are slowest (wiki/web-gulch.md, CANON).

entries.what: Web Gulch's ways on the grid: the Pit road's gulch hexes on the Silverton area (55,40 to 57,36) are the floor -- a step into one takes the party down by the mouth or the descent facing the way it came (refunding nothing: the step in is the march's); out by a mouth onto the road's next hex beyond the cut (57,35 north, 55,41 south), out by a descent onto the bank top 2.2 mi to that side, asked first (RETURN / STAY). On THE WORLD alone (&far) the site's door, offered where a walk ends there. The two beats ask before their fights: FIGHT or LEAVE IT at the snared lad, FIGHT or BACK AWAY at the strung end (the first game asked neither).
entries.why: Griz 10-28, his lean 1 ("Gulch's leans look good"): "if you make it through the gulch, you get to the inn" (wiki/web-gulch.md); the asks the seat's, for a mouse that clicks a step too far.

entries.what: Web Gulch's words on the grid: noon, "Noon in the gulch: the silk-cutters go out to the webs, and the boy starts drumming. The spiders sulk in the heat."; after it, "The cutters come in off the webs with their skeins, and the drumming stops. Out in the silk, the spiders stir."; morning, "Morning comes down the gulch. The cutters stir round their fire."; night, "Night in the gulch. The cutters bank their fire; out in the silk, things wake."; the mouths, "The Pit road, up out of the cut: north to the fork." / "... south toward the Halfway Inn."; the hello, "The Pit road runs down its bed: north up out of it to the fork, south to the Halfway Inn. The banks are a way up where they open."
entries.why: the seat's connective words (10-28), drafted from the first game's (content/npcs.json silkcutter: "We cut at noon, when the spiders sulk").

entries.what: The second game's Corwen Dace, drafted where the first game's words would break the roost's law: at TAKE HIM, "Corwen Dace takes up his staff and his year-old book. \"No light on it till we're past the roost. I know the law better than you do.\"" (then the first game's dace.join second line); stepping into the deep gallery, "Corwen Dace lifts his staff, and the light comes up on its head. \"No roost down here. It's lawful.\"" (the Light cantrip on his staff); at the dens' shaft head with the party, the first game's second Dace's words (npcs.json dacedown) as his own, then "Dace touches the mark as he passes it, the way the hands touch it going home."; the JOURNAL's CORWEN DACE: "Corwen Dace walks with you in the guano mine: he has wanted the deep gallery all his life. entries.why: RULED 10-29 (Griz, the story window), verbatim: "don't send the grok faces, just make sure the new art dept is working with the old portrait sheets md descriptions along with what we've given it (defer to original if our newer contradicts)"; "the ones without portrait sheets description makes sure art dept is getting enough info (hex family probably means half-orc) to work with".

entries.what: The second game's floors on the grid's diamonds (deep16/js/mines.js ON THE DIAMONDS, 10-29): the deep gallery and Web Gulch drawn as the Wet is, no turn (north up the screen's right); the first game's things given pieces -- the grid's tree, stalagmite and cocoon, and the seat's own drawn in code: a silk-cutters' tent (a pale A-frame, its flap open to the east), a ladder standing up the rock at each way up, bones and old webbing lying on the floor, the camp's fire by the campfire's flames; a ladder near the party keeps the walls in front of it cut; the cave's stone under a cave floor and its cut field; the Wet's zoom. Web Gulch's drummer boy stands by night east of the fire (13,10), not in front of it (13,11).
entries.why: Griz, 10-29: "NEW:  Conversion of topdown roam of cloaker fight level and(?) new gulch as iso-roams like the Wet"; the seat's seven leans, "those 1-7 look good" (lean 5: the grid's own code drawing, a piece for each first-game thing, no art order). The pieces are the seat's drafts for his eye (eyes-isoroams-1029, eyes-isoroams-gulch-1029).

entries.what: The Guano Galleries' mouth camp: the module's "bunkhouse where the hands sleep" (GalleriesModule/guano-galleries-DM.md, G1) is the building west of the path under the Pollards' house, its door the second game's (the first game drew it doorless); a bed's sign, "The Bunkhouse: where the house's hands sleep"; free to the house's hands once Sabeth's work is taken, a silver for a stranger and after the roost is broken. Its words: "The house's hands sleep here, in off the dens before the dusk river goes out. Bunks two high, scarves hung to dry on the posts, a hooded lamp by the door." The night: "The hands come in ahead of the wings; nobody talks over the roar of them leaving. Nobody stands a watch -- the house keeps its own door." The morning: "Morning, and the river of wings coming home over the mouth." (deep16/js/mines.js M.INNS keeper:galbunk)
entries.why: Griz 10-29 to the lanes desk: "in the game 2 guano mine surface, I'm still not seeing the door to where you can sleep as crew after taking a job" -- the notes seat's drafts; which building, the price rule (the Warrens' bunkhouse's shape, his 10-21 "free/cheap inn function") and the roost rule (the module's "put on the sledge track and never asked back") the seat's calls

entries.what: A council's night sitting at the party's rest (C1, C3) plays over a picture of the Hex's third floor: the council in their seats at the long table under the Big Window, Warda in the lounge, a low wash and a warm pool at the table -- dimmed behind the counter's screen, and behind each speaker's portrait the table itself; the card pages show the room alone. C2 plays on the third floor itself and keeps the counter's own screen. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.backdrop, H16.thirdShot; deep16/js/counter.js o.bg)

entries.what: The council's night as a cutscene at the party's rest, before the sitting: SILVERTON, AT DUSK -- "Dusk. Hessle comes out of the Weigh-House and lights the lamp by its door: the scales are lit, and the council sits tonight." (Hessle out of his door, a step along the street, the lamp at the door's east jamb lit); THE HEX, THE THIRD FLOOR -- "Up the Hex's spiral, one by one, the council comes to the long table under the Big Window and takes their seats. Warda keeps the lounge door." (each walks from the spiral's head to their place in turn); then the sitting over the third floor. (deep16/js/hours.js H16.night, H16.CUT, H16.layLamp, H16.layArrive) RE-CUT 10-29 (the story window, RULED, his "Leans stand" on his note "the first cutscene has redundancy - explainer line replaced by shots. The background of the scene vs background in the portrait window"): the sitting opens on its first speaker when every shot was gone past by hand (its card only after X); the arrival's caption its title alone; the third floor behind the screen only, a little brighter, the portrait on its own plain window, no counter, no purse; the stock night's east side's man stands at the table's end.
entries.why: Griz 10-29 to the story window: "I think we should do a shot of the lamp being lit a dusk and maybe them arriving and being seated on the third floor, expository cut scene" (RULED, PATCHLOG 18ee529a) -- the notes seat's build and drafts: Hessle as the one who lights the Weigh-House lamp (his door is the scales' light, H16.LIGHTS.scales), the order up the spiral (the table's own), the cards' words

entries.what: Ottak Harrow's look for the art desk (art-wanted section 26, ART-123-HARROW): an orc of seventy-seven, broad and heavy-shouldered, a farmer's thick hands, grey-green skin weathered dark, short tusks, iron-grey hair cropped close, a lined, patient, calculating face; a good plain wool coat over a work shirt, no ornament; his WORK row rubs a pinch of wheat grain and lets it fall (his tithe is paid in grain).
entries.why: Griz 10-29, 'Write his block': cutscene 1 seats him and gives him a line with no portrait or figure; no portrait sheet has him, so the look is the lanes desk's draft over the register (the-council.md, the-slave-economy.md: age 77 by H-1, the wheat tithe).

entries.what: Papa Urtusk and Warda on the grid as the art desk drew them (ART-123-URTUSK, ART-123-WARDA; 3b10a0c1, cdf9f9c1): Papa's skin the palette's orc green (the art desk painted a khaki olive that snapped to grey stone, an old human's face), sparse white hair on his scalp beside the white jaw fringe (the art desk's own), and he stands 58 px where the town's grown men stand 50 -- the largest at the council's table; Warda a half-orc with olive skin and small tusks, a grey-streaked dark bun, a charcoal dress, the ring of keys at her belt (the art desk's choices under her paragraph). 10-29 later: Ottak Harrow the same way (ART-123-HARROW, 96abfa51) -- his khaki olive skin turned to the orc green as Papa's, his cream work shirt kept (the band narrowed: hues 33-60, value to 0.75), 50 px as the town's men.
entries.why: The cutscene cutter seat's cut, on Griz's "Urtusk just landed in fresh, give the cutscene its own cutter" (10-29): the art desk's notes ask for orc skin on the orc ramp and not to normalize Papa to an ordinary man's height; the governing paragraphs are art-wanted section 26 as re-cut at bd2b7be0 (now on deep16-art-in-hand.md). Griz to the lanes desk: "harrows in, might as well spin up another cutter for skarn".

entries.what: The Missing Five by words in the second game: Edric Pellam tells it himself as he books the party -- 'He turns back a page. "Five names in this book have no return line. Warrens Pete's crew, gone down past the wet after leavings, and Pete came up alone."' and '"Skarn holds the gate to where they went. Ask him, not me."'; the mission's words by who told it (Pete's, Edric's, Skarn's); Skarn's lines the player picks -- 'PETE'S FIVE. WHERE DID THEY GO DOWN?' with the five carried, 'ANY WORK BESIDES THE CRADLES?' without (his answer '"Past the pens there's one job, and nobody takes it."' and the five), the slave stance one rude line 'OPEN UP, COLLAR.' (the Champion); Edric after the five '"Five return lines. The book balances, for once."' and '"Skarn pays for it out of the office box. Tell him yourself."'; Pete after them 'Five came up. Edric wrote them in, every one.' / 'He doesn't say six any more. He doesn't say much.'; 'paid at the pen' for the first game's 'paid at the board' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.FIVE_BY, H16.TEXT w16.*, C.TALK16 pete; deep16/js/mines.js Skarn, Edric)
entries.why: His NOTES of 10-29 1808Z, day 4, the mouth camp 9,8 and 4,9: "there's no real taking of the missing 5 quest ... should get from warrens pete, or with dialogue from Edric. Both should point to ask Skarn step. the speak to him as a man or a slave should be lines the player chooses (rather than conversational stance presented) or absent"; "post quest edric text". The story window's leans 1-5, RULED, his "Leans stand" (the lanes desk's relay). The lines the window's drafts; the module's test (WarrensModule/crawler-warrens-DM.md §4) kept as the rude line.

entries.what: The Braiding Ettercap a JOURNAL mission: 'Forty gold on Hessle's board, and ten more since it snared a lad: an ettercap strung across Web Gulch, on the road south out of Silverton. Bring its fangs to the Weigh-House.'; opened by the board read, the rumour r-ettercap, or the council's ask (C2), which pins it; its step Web Gulch (THE WORLD's site webgulch), then the fangs to Hessle; done when paid. Swann's line for it: 'Silk across a road, and something braiding it. Go at noon, when the spiders sulk.' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.MISSIONS ettercap, C.RUMOR_OPENS, H16.SWANN.q)
entries.why: His 10-28 "16 yes" (a board paper a mission once its ground is built) and Web Gulch built 10-28 (`4c96cfd`); the story window's lean 7's find, RULED, "Leans stand". The ettercap's bounty is the realm's (wiki/web-gulch.md, CANON).

entries.what: PROPOSED for the realm: the territorial understanding between Venn the barber-surgeon and Davos Kren of the leech-house -- the Hex's own fighters are Davos's, stitched on the house (the mother pays the leech-house's bills); Venn, who taught him the needle, takes what the house won't pay for -- the crowd's cuts, the brawls off the card, and what isn't to be written down -- from the Hex's door on fight nights. The game's words: 'Shave, tooth, stitch. The house's fighters are Davos Kren's. I taught him the needle.' / 'Fight nights I sit at the Hex's door for what the house won't pay for. Three coppers, and I don't write it down.' (deep16/js/hours.js C.TALK16 barber, H16.ABOUT barber)
entries.why: His NOTES of 10-29 1808Z, day 3, Silverton 31,41: "How does canon play out between Krenn and the barber surgeon and his npc text?" The register (TarlynsPit/silverton-personae.md slot 10: 'shares arena surgery work on a territorial understanding'; 'stitching fast and off the books, someone thinks of Venn'; slot 21; wiki/the-hex.md, the leech-house the arena's own surgery) left the territory open; the story window's lean 8, RULED, "Leans stand", proposed for the realm (fold person).

entries.what: PROPOSED for the realm: Hessle's board hangs outside, on the Weigh-House's front wall beside its door on Fountain Street -- planks, the town's bounties nailed up on it, each sworn before notary; a paper is taken down by whoever takes the job, and proof is brought to Hessle inside, where the scales pay it. The game's: a paper for each bounty standing (the cloaker's gone brown, the Snoot's under a red seal), its screen's words 'Hessle's board, on the Weigh-House wall: the town's bounties, each one nailed up and sworn before notary.' / 'Take a paper down and the job is yours. Bring proof to Hessle inside, and the scales pay it.', 'You take the paper down off its nail. It goes in your JOURNAL.', and the Snoot's 'That one stays up: true word is brought to Hessle, whoever brings it.'; Hessle's 'The board's on the wall outside my door. Take a paper down; the scales pay what's posted, sworn before notary.' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.BOARD)
entries.why: Griz to the lanes desk, 10-29: "we actually also need a visible board, either inside or outside of hessles - the way hessle reads the board should instead be clickable missions below it (as if they're taking the mission off the board) - I think at present it's a multipart mission or something". Outside the story window's call (his "either"): the 10-28 words already had it "on the Weigh-House wall on Fountain Street", and the first game's Hessle taps it through the window glass. A place's detail, proposed for the realm (fold place).

entries.what: PROPOSED for the realm: Edric Pellam, the Crawler Warrens' tally-man, was a farmhand who worked the carrion crawler milking station before he was advanced to the book, because he can write -- Griz's own word to the art desk for his portrait (ART-123-EDRIC): "make him uglier - farmhand that works carrion crawler milking station (advanced to bookkeep)". The art desk drew a balding labourer in his fifties, heavy-browed and jowled, ink-stained hands, a frayed good brown coat over a waistcoat (deep16/art/pt_edric, edric_p1). Not a seat's invention: his word, logged here for the fold.
entries.why: Griz, 10-29, to the lanes desk, on the Edric and Dace cutter seat's question 5 (fold Edric's farmhand line onto the realm's Edric page?): "5 - yes". The wiki's Edric (TarlynsPit wiki/the-warrens.md, the Pellams) is 'a Pellam who can still write'; this is where he came from.

The council had work for you.' The gold marker on the Hex's front doors, inside on the nearest spiral up. Swann's line for it: 'A stair that turns and turns, and a long table at the top of it. Don't keep them waiting.' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.MISSIONS council, H16.pinSq hex3, H16.SWANN.q.council)
entries.why: Griz, his ear file of 10-29 2212Z on eyes-runner-1029b: "should put a quest in your journal to guide you to the third floor". The words the story seat of 10-29 night's drafts (the no-stubs law, RULED 09-24).

entries.what: The keepers out on Silverton's street at dusk say their evening's word, not their counter's: Marin 'Shop's shut. The dye sits in the vats till morning.' / 'Come by in the day for cloth. At dusk I eat Marta's pie like everyone else.'; the barber 'Fight night's coming in. I sit here at the Hex's door for whoever the house won't pay to stitch.' / 'My shop's shut till morning. If one of yours is down, Davos Kren's door is by the Hex.'; Mela 'The baths are banked for the night. I sit by the fountains at dusk and let the town talk.' / 'Shut till morning.'; Venn Hale 'The stables lock at dusk, and the fighters with them. I come out to see who walks in at the gate.' / 'Want a fight tonight? Korvin's slate, inside the Hex. It never closes.'; Aldric 'The factor house is shut. At dusk I walk Fountain Street and count the wagons in.' / 'Business is by day, at the house.'; Merrick 'The window's shut to callers. Dusk is when the lanterns talk, and I listen.' / 'Come back by day.'; Tam 'The smoke room fills after dark, and it's no place for you.' / 'Go and find a bed.' (deep16/js/hours.js H16.OUT, H16.outWords)
entries.why: Griz, his ear file of 10-29 2212Z: "Out at dusk merchants - same inside text". The story seat of 10-29 night's drafts (the no-stubs law).

entries.what: Aldwin's bread line moves: in the early hours on the street, every seven seconds the one at the front walks up to the chapel door and goes in, the other three each step up a place, and a newcomer comes up behind; their talk squares go with them, and 'Mind the line. It moves.' is kept (deep16/js/hours.js H16.breadTick, H16.BREAD.every, .step) 10-30: they get their bread and leave -- the one at the door goes in, comes back out with a loaf in hand (drawn at the hands), walks down the street round the line and the party to the nearest other door and in at it; someone new comes up behind later (H16.breadTick's five legs, H16.paintLoaves).
entries.why: Griz, his ear file of 10-29 2212Z: "Breadline is good except it says that it moves and doesn't yet" -- the story seat of 10-29 night's lean (move the line, keep the word), built, a call standing for his overrule. 10-30, Griz on the seat's call: "solid, i assume they get their bread and leave" (RULED).

entries.what: The Threshing Floor, a fighter's archetype of our own at 3 beside the SRD's Champion (Barley's road: 'He went down once against Cutter on fight night and got back up'). 3rd: HARD GROUND -- prone is no trouble: its melee attacks while prone at no disadvantage, no advantage for a creature within 5 ft for its being prone, standing up for 5 ft; UP OFF THE FLOOR -- once per long rest, dropped to 0 HP and not killed, it rises at the start of its next turn with its fighter level + CON modifier in HP, standing at no cost, its first attack that turn at advantage. 7th: THRESHING -- once a turn, a melee weapon hit on a prone creature deals one more weapon die. 10th and later waiting. Built on the grid 10-30; the Pocket DM's maker asks it at 3.
entries.why: Griz, 10-29/30: 'I want the players to be making the same decisions at level up as they would be playing in a version using the PHB and DMG, and where we have to we will event the options they're choosing between'; on the choice at 3, 'i'd say yes'. Drafted in leveling-srd-by-class.md 2.1, not the Battle Master or the Eldritch Knight; his test of distinct, 'whether it can be built within the claude constitution'.

entries.what: The Drillyard, a fighter's archetype of our own at 3 beside the Champion and the Threshing Floor: set plays bought with openings (two a short rest, three at 7), one play a turn, three known (five at 7). On a weapon hit: WHEEL (the fighter and a friend within 5 ft trade places, no opportunity attacks), BIND (no reactions till its next turn), BREAK STRIDE (10 ft less speed through its next turn), PIN THE SHIELD (its shield adds nothing to its AC till the fighter's next turn); CALL THE MARK, a bonus action (each friend's first hit on one foe +2 till the fighter's next turn); HOLD GROUND, the reaction to a push or a knockdown. Built on the grid 10-30; the Pocket DM's maker asks it at 3 and its plays at 3 and 7.
entries.why: Griz, 10-30: 'take leveling's leans and it can start building' -- the Battle Master's role a veteran misses (leveling-srd-by-class.md 5, 6.1): no superiority dice, no die on any roll, none of its maneuvers; his test of distinct, 'whether it can be built within the claude constitution'.

entries.what: Follow-Through, a feat of our own (STR 13, any class, the second game's): with a heavy melee weapon, a blow that drops a creature carries the damage past its last hit point to another foe within reach, no roll, once; and once a turn, before a swing, WIDE SWING -- a hit deals twice the proficiency bonus more, a miss puts the next attack that turn at disadvantage. Built on the grid 10-30; never on the first game's pick.
entries.why: Griz, 10-30: 'take leveling's leans and it can start building' -- the role of the PHB's Great Weapon Master a veteran misses (leveling-srd-by-class.md 5, 6.3): no -5/+10 trade, no bonus-action attack; his test of distinct, 'whether it can be built within the claude constitution'.

entries.what: Gnawing Word, a 1st-level warlock spell of our own (enchantment): a bonus action, 60 ft, concentration up to a minute; each time the caster hits the foe with an attack it takes psychic equal to the hits landed since the casting, 1, 2, 3, to 5 (+2 to the most a slot level above 1st); it ends when the foe drops. On the warlock's list (the last of its 1st, so the generic warlock is unchanged). Built on the grid 10-30.
entries.why: Griz, 10-30: 'take leveling's leans and it can start building' -- the role of the PHB's Hex a veteran misses (leveling-srd-by-class.md 5, 6.4): no curse on an ability's checks, no moving to a new target, a minute not an hour, damage that grows with each hit.

entries.what: Rootdrag, a druid cantrip of our own (transmutation): an action, 30 ft, a creature standing on the ground, Large or smaller, saves STR or takes 1d6 bludgeoning (2d6 at 5th, 3d6 at 11th, 4d6 at 17th) and roots drag it 10 ft along the ground the way the caster chooses (the AI: toward its nearest friend). Nothing aloft, no spell attack. On the druid's list, its last cantrip. Built on the grid 10-30.
entries.why: Griz, 10-30: 'yeah, thorn whipping people into things happens at my friday table I think. draft for the two mentioned'; 'take leveling's leans and it can start building' -- the role of the PHB's Thorn Whip (leveling-srd-by-class.md 6.5): no spell attack, no pull toward the caster alone, nothing aloft.

entries.what: Called to Account, a 1st-level paladin spell of our own (abjuration): a bonus action, 30 ft, concentration up to a minute; a foe saves WIS or, while it lasts, takes 1d8 radiant (+1d8 a slot level above 1st) each time it deals damage to anyone but the caster. It ends when the caster attacks or casts a spell at another, or ends a turn more than 30 ft from it. On the paladin's list (the last of its 1st, so the generic paladin is unchanged); not on Lymen's (the first game's list). Built on the grid 10-30.

entries.what: Held Breath, a feat of our own (DEX 13, any class, the second game's): not having moved yet this turn, ranged weapon attacks that turn ignore half cover and take no disadvantage at long range, and the first that hits deals one more weapon die. entries.what: The Circle of the Pelt, a druid's circle of our own at 2 beside the SRD's Land: WEAR THE BEAST, a bonus action and a use of Wild Shape -- one beast part on the druid's own body for the fight, its HP, gear, spells and concentration kept: CLAWS (unarmed 1d8 slashing with WIS), HIDE (AC at least 13 + WIS), HAUNCHES (10 ft more speed, up for 5 ft); THICK PELT, temporary HP twice the druid level as a part goes on; at 6 TWO PARTS from one use and the claws magical. entries.what: Long Guard, a feat of our own (STR 13, any class, the second game's): with a reach weapon in hand, KEEP BACK -- the reaction when a creature it can see moves into its reach, a STR save (DC 8 + proficiency + STR) or pushed 5 ft back, out of reach, its move ended; and SET AGAINST THE CHARGE -- one that came 20 ft or more straight at it this turn and stands within its reach takes one more weapon die on its next hit before the end of its next turn. Built on the grid 10-30 after the SRD's reach weapons (glaive, halberd, pike, whip); never on the first game's pick.
